title: Iliad, Book I
author: Homer
source_notes: Greek text: Monro & Allen, Oxford Classical Text, via Perseus Digital Library (canonical-greekLit). English: Samuel Butler, 1898, revised by Timothy Power and Gregory Nagy, via Perseus Digital Library.
reading_notes: Book 1 of the Iliad: the quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles over the captured woman Chryseis, the plague sent by Apollo, the withdrawal of Achilles from battle, and the appeal of Thetis to Zeus. 611 lines. Line-by-line Greek with per-line gloss; Butler's prose translation presented as a parallel panel for context.

lines.original: μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος
lines.english: Sing, O goddess, the anger [] of Achilles son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans. Many a brave soul [] did it send hurrying down to Hades, and many a hero…
lines.gloss: μῆνιν (acc. sg. of μῆνις) 'wrath, anger'; ἄειδε (pres. imperative of ἀείδω) 'sing!'; θεά (voc. sg.) 'goddess' (invoking the Muse); Πηληϊάδεω (gen. sg. patronymic) 'of the son of Peleus'; Ἀχιλῆος (gen. sg.) 'of Achilles.'

lines.original: οὐλομένην, ἣ μυρίʼ Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγεʼ ἔθηκε,

lines.original: πολλὰς δʼ ἰφθίμους ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν

lines.original: ἐξ οὗ δὴ τὰ πρῶτα διαστήτην ἐρίσαντε

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης τε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν καὶ δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς.

lines.original: τίς τʼ ἄρ σφωε θεῶν ἔριδι ξυνέηκε μάχεσθαι;

lines.original: Λητοῦς καὶ Διὸς υἱός· ὃ γὰρ βασιλῆϊ χολωθεὶς

lines.original: νοῦσον ἀνὰ στρατὸν ὄρσε κακήν, ὀλέκοντο δὲ λαοί,

lines.original: οὕνεκα τὸν Χρύσην ἠτίμασεν ἀρητῆρα

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης· ὃ γὰρ ἦλθε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδα δὲ μάλιστα δύω, κοσμήτορε λαῶν·
lines.english: and he besought the Achaeans, but most of all the two sons of Atreus, who were their chiefs. "Sons of Atreus," he cried, "and all other Achaeans, may the gods who dwell ingrant…

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ἄλλοι μὲν πάντες ἐπευφήμησαν Ἀχαιοὶ

lines.original: αἰδεῖσθαί θʼ ἱερῆα καὶ ἀγλαὰ δέχθαι ἄποινα·
lines.english: and he besought the Achaeans, but most of all the two sons of Atreus, who were their chiefs. "Sons of Atreus," he cried, "and all other Achaeans, may the gods who dwell ingrant…

'ransom'. Both infinitives depend on the previous line's verb of approval, expressing what the Achaeans approved: to respect the priest and accept the splendid ransom.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ οὐκ Ἀτρεΐδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονι ἥνδανε θυμῷ,

lines.original: ἀλλὰ κακῶς ἀφίει, κρατερὸν δʼ ἐπὶ μῦθον ἔτελλε·

lines.original: τῇ δεκάτῃ δʼ ἀγορὴν δὲ καλέσσατο λαὸν Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: and prayed apart to King Apollo whom lovely Leto had borne. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla and rulewith your might, hear me O god of…
lines.gloss: τῇ δεκάτῃ (dat. sg. fem., agreeing with ἡμέρᾳ understood) 'on the tenth (day)'; ἀγορήν (acc. sg. of ἀγορή) 'assembly'; καλέσσατο (aor. mid. of καλέω) 'summoned, called together'; λαόν (acc. sg. of λαός) 'the host, the people'.

lines.original: τῷ γὰρ ἐπὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη·
lines.english: and prayed apart to King Apollo whom lovely Leto had borne. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla and rulewith your might, hear me O god of…
lines.gloss: τῷ (dat. sg. demonstrative) 'to him' (i.e., Achilles); φρεσὶ (dat. pl. of φρήν) 'in the mind, heart'; θῆκε (aor. of τίθημι) 'put, placed'; λευκώλενος (nom. sg. fem.) 'white-armed' (epithet of Hera, from λευκός 'white' + ὦλενος 'arm').

lines.original: κήδετο γὰρ Δαναῶν, ὅτι ῥα θνήσκοντας ὁρᾶτο.
lines.english: and prayed apart to King Apollo whom lovely Leto had borne. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla and rulewith your might, hear me O god of…
lines.gloss: κήδετο (3rd sg. impf. mid. of κήδομαι) 'she cared for, was concerned about'; Δαναῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Danaans/Greeks'; ὅτι 'because'; θνήσκοντας (pres. part. acc. pl. masc. of θνῄσκω) 'dying'; ὁρᾶτο (3rd sg. impf. mid. of ὁράω) 'she saw'.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν ἤγερθεν ὁμηγερέες τε γένοντο,
lines.english: and prayed apart to King Apollo whom lovely Leto had borne. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla and rulewith your might, hear me O god of…
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. demonstrative) 'they'; ἐπεὶ οὖν 'when then, and so when'; ἤγερθεν (aor. pass. ind., 3rd pl. of ἀγείρω) 'were gathered'; ὁμηγερέες (nom. pl. masc. adj.) 'assembled together, in one place'; γένοντο (aor. mid. ind., 3rd pl. of γίγνομαι) 'became, were'.

lines.original: τοῖσι δʼ ἀνιστάμενος μετέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: and prayed apart to King Apollo whom lovely Leto had borne. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla and rulewith your might, hear me O god of…
lines.gloss: τοῖσι (dat. pl. of ὁ) 'to them, among them'; ἀνιστάμενος (pres. mid. participle) 'standing up, rising'; μετέφη (3rd sg. impf. of μεταφημί) 'spoke among, addressed'; πόδας ὠκύς (acc. + nom., formulaic epithet) 'swift-footed'; Ἀχιλλεύς (nom. sg.) 'Achilles.'

lines.original: ἤτοι ὅ γʼ ὣς εἰπὼν κατʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετο· τοῖσι δʼ ἀνέστη
lines.english: or burned for you thigh-bones in fat of bulls or goats, grant my prayer, and let your arrows avenge these my tears upon the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his…
lines.gloss: ἤτοι 'thus, so then' (transitional particle); ὣς 'thus, in this way' (adverb); εἰπών (aor. act. participle of εἶπον, nom. sg. masc.) 'having spoken'; κατʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετο (aor. mid. of ἕζομαι) 'sat down'; ἀνέστη (aor. of ἀνίστημι) 'stood up, arose'.

lines.original: Κάλχας Θεστορίδης οἰωνοπόλων ὄχʼ ἄριστος,
lines.english: or burned for you thigh-bones in fat of bulls or goats, grant my prayer, and let your arrows avenge these my tears upon the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his…
lines.gloss: Κάλχας (nom. sg.) 'Calchas'; Θεστορίδης (nom. sg., patronymic) 'son of Thestor'; οἰωνοπόλων (gen. pl. of οἰωνοπόλος) 'of bird-interpreters, augurs'; ὄχ(α) (adv., here with superlative) 'by far'; ἄριστος (nom. sg. masc. superlative of ἀγαθός) 'best, most excellent.'

lines.original: ὃς ᾔδη τά τʼ ἐόντα τά τʼ ἐσσόμενα πρό τʼ ἐόντα,
lines.english: or burned for you thigh-bones in fat of bulls or goats, grant my prayer, and let your arrows avenge these my tears upon the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his…
lines.gloss: ὃς (relative pronoun, nom. sg.) 'who'; ᾔδη (pluperfect of οἶδα) 'knew'; τά τʼ ἐόντα (neut. pl. pres. participle of εἰμί) 'things that are/the present'; τά τʼ ἐσσόμενα (neut. pl. fut. participle) 'things that will be/the future'; πρό τʼ ἐόντα (neut. pl. with πρό) 'things that were before/the past.'

lines.original: καὶ νήεσσʼ ἡγήσατʼ Ἀχαιῶν Ἴλιον εἴσω
lines.english: or burned for you thigh-bones in fat of bulls or goats, grant my prayer, and let your arrows avenge these my tears upon the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his…
lines.gloss: νήεσσι (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships'; ἡγήσατο (aor. mid. of ἡγέομαι) 'led, guided'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans'; Ἴλιον (acc.) 'Ilion, Troy'; εἴσω (adv.) 'into, toward'.

lines.original: ἣν διὰ μαντοσύνην, τήν οἱ πόρε Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων·
lines.english: or burned for you thigh-bones in fat of bulls or goats, grant my prayer, and let your arrows avenge these my tears upon the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his…
lines.gloss: ἣν (acc. sg. fem. relative pronoun) 'which' (referring to μαντοσύνην); διὰ (prep. + acc.) 'because of, through'; μαντοσύνην (acc. sg. of μαντοσύνη) 'prophetic skill, art of divination'; τήν (acc. sg. fem. relative pronoun) 'which'; πόρε (3rd sg. aor. of πορεῖν) 'gave, granted'; Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων (nom.) 'Phoebus Apollo.'

lines.original: ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·
lines.english: with his bow and his quiver upon his shoulder, and the arrows rattled on his back with the rage that trembled within him. He sat himself down away from the ships with a face as…
lines.gloss: ὅ (nom. sg. relative pronoun) 'who'; σφιν (dat. pl. pronoun) 'to them'; ἐὺ φρονέων (pres. participle) 'thinking well, with good intent'; ἀγορήσατο (aor. mid.) 'addressed the assembly'; μετέειπεν (aor.) 'spoke among them, addressed'.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: with his bow and his quiver upon his shoulder, and the arrows rattled on his back with the rage that trembled within him. He sat himself down away from the ships with a face as…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. demonstrative pronoun) 'him'; ἀπαμειβόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'answering, replying to'; προσέφη (3rd sg. aor. of προσφημί) 'addressed, spoke to'; πόδας ὠκὺς (nom. sg., formulaic epithet) 'swift-footed'; Ἀχιλλεύς (nom. sg.) 'Achilles'.

lines.original: καὶ τότε δὴ θάρσησε καὶ ηὔδα μάντις ἀμύμων·
lines.english: with his bow and his quiver upon his shoulder, and the arrows rattled on his back with the rage that trembled within him. He sat himself down away from the ships with a face as…
lines.gloss: θάρσησε (aor. of θαρσέω) 'took courage, took heart'; ηὔδα (impf. of αὐδάω) 'spoke, addressed'; μάντις (nom. sg.) 'seer, prophet'; ἀμύμων (nom. sg. adj.) 'blameless, excellent'.

lines.original: ἤτοι ὅ γʼ ὣς εἰπὼν κατʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετο· τοῖσι δʼ ἀνέστη
lines.english: with his bow and his quiver upon his shoulder, and the arrows rattled on his back with the rage that trembled within him. He sat himself down away from the ships with a face as…
lines.gloss: ἤτοι (particle) 'and so, indeed'; ὅ γ(ε) 'he' (nom. sg., the prophet); ὣς 'thus, in this way'; εἰπών (aor. participle of εἶπον) 'having spoken'; κατ(ά)... ἕζετο (aor. mid. of ἵζω) 'sat down'; τοῖσι (dat. pl.) 'among them'; ἀνέστη (aor. of ἀνίστημι) 'stood up, arose'.

lines.original: ἥρως Ἀτρεΐδης εὐρὺ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: with his bow and his quiver upon his shoulder, and the arrows rattled on his back with the rage that trembled within him. He sat himself down away from the ships with a face as…
lines.gloss: ἥρως (nom. sg.) 'hero'; Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg., patronymic) 'son of Atreus'; εὐρὺ κρείων (nom. sg. masc. participle of εὐρὺ κρείειν) 'wide-ruling' or 'ruling widely'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) 'Agamemnon' — a formulaic expansion identifying the hero who stood up.

lines.original: ἀχνύμενος· μένεος δὲ μέγα φρένες ἀμφιμέλαιναι
lines.english: First he smote their mules and their hounds, but presently he aimed his shafts at the people themselves, and all day long the pyres of the dead were burning. For nine whole days…
lines.gloss: ἀχνύμενος (pres. mid. participle) 'grieving, distressed'; μένεος (gen. sg. of μένος) 'rage, fury'; φρένες (nom. pl.) 'heart, mind, lungs' (seat of emotion); ἀμφιμέλαιναι (nom. pl. fem. adj.) 'black all around, utterly dark' (modifying φρένες).

lines.original: πίμπλαντʼ, ὄσσε δέ οἱ πυρὶ λαμπετόωντι ἐΐκτην·
lines.english: First he smote their mules and their hounds, but presently he aimed his shafts at the people themselves, and all day long the pyres of the dead were burning. For nine whole days…
lines.gloss: πίμπλαντʼ (3rd pl. impf. mid. of πίμπλημι) 'were being filled'; ὄσσε (nom./acc. dual of ὄσσε) 'the two eyes'; πυρὶ λαμπετόωντι (dat. sg. pres. participle of λάμπω) 'with blazing fire'; ἐΐκτην (3rd dual impf. of ἔοικα) 'resembled, were like'.

lines.original: Κάλχαντα πρώτιστα κάκʼ ὀσσόμενος προσέειπε·
lines.english: First he smote their mules and their hounds, but presently he aimed his shafts at the people themselves, and all day long the pyres of the dead were burning. For nine whole days…
lines.gloss: Κάλχαντα (acc. sg. of Κάλχας) 'Calchas,' the seer; πρώτιστα (adv.) 'first of all'; κάκʼ (neut. acc. pl. of κακός, crasis for κακά) 'evil things, troubles'; ὀσσόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'prophesying, foretelling'; προσέειπε (aor. of προσεῖπον) 'addressed, spoke to.'

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: First he smote their mules and their hounds, but presently he aimed his shafts at the people themselves, and all day long the pyres of the dead were burning. For nine whole days…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. demonstrative pronoun) 'him' (referring to Agamemnon); ἠμείβετο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of ἀμείβομαι) 'answered, replied'; ἔπειτα (adv.) 'then, thereupon'; ποδάρκης (nom. sg. adj.) 'swift-footed'; δῖος (nom. sg. adj.) 'godlike, noble'; Ἀχιλλεύς (nom. sg.) 'Achilles' (subject).

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: First he smote their mules and their hounds, but presently he aimed his shafts at the people themselves, and all day long the pyres of the dead were burning. For nine whole days…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. demonstrative) 'him'; ἀπαμειβόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'answering in turn, replying'; προσέφη (3rd sg. aorist) 'addressed, spoke to'; κρείων (nom. sg. masc. participle of κρείω, used as epithet) 'lord, ruler'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) 'Agamemnon'.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἄρʼ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: moved thereto by Hera, who saw the Achaeans in their death-throes and had compassion upon them. Then, when they were got together, he rose and spoke among them. "Son of Atreus,"…
lines.gloss: ὑπόδρα (adverb) 'looking darkly, with a scowling glance'; ἰδών (aor. participle of ὁράω, nom. sg. masc.) 'having looked, looking'; πόδας ὠκύς (acc. pl. + nom. sg., formulaic epithet) 'swift-footed'; the phrase ὑπόδρα ἰδών conveys Achilles' angry, resentful gaze as he responds.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: moved thereto by Hera, who saw the Achaeans in their death-throes and had compassion upon them. Then, when they were got together, he rose and spoke among them. "Son of Atreus,"…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. of ὁ, demonstrative) 'him'; ἠμείβετο (aor. mid. of ἀμείβω) 'answered, replied'; ἔπειτα (adv.) 'then, thereupon'; ἄναξ (nom. sg.) 'lord, king'; ἀνδρῶν (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'of men'.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο· Πηλεΐωνι δʼ ἄχος γένετʼ, ἐν δέ οἱ ἦτορ
lines.english: moved thereto by Hera, who saw the Achaeans in their death-throes and had compassion upon them. Then, when they were got together, he rose and spoke among them. "Son of Atreus,"…
lines.gloss: ὣς φάτο (aor. mid. 3rd sg. of φημί) 'thus he spoke'; Πηλεΐωνι (dat. sg.) 'to/for the son of Peleus' (Achilles); ἄχος (nom. sg.) 'grief, pain'; γένετο (aor. mid. 3rd sg. of γίγνομαι) 'came to be, arose'; ἦτορ (nom. sg.) 'heart'; the δέ marks contrast and οἱ is dative 'for him.'

lines.original: στήθεσσιν λασίοισι διάνδιχα μερμήριξεν,
lines.english: moved thereto by Hera, who saw the Achaeans in their death-throes and had compassion upon them. Then, when they were got together, he rose and spoke among them. "Son of Atreus,"…
lines.gloss: στήθεσσιν (dat. pl. of στῆθος) 'in his breast, in his heart'; λασίοισι (dat. pl. of λάσιος) 'shaggy, hairy' (epithet for chest); διάνδιχα (adv.) 'in two ways, in both directions'; μερμήριξεν (aor. of μερμηρίζω) 'he pondered, debated'—Achilles deliberates two courses of action in his heart.

lines.original: ἢ ὅ γε φάσγανον ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος παρὰ μηροῦ
lines.english: moved thereto by Hera, who saw the Achaeans in their death-throes and had compassion upon them. Then, when they were got together, he rose and spoke among them. "Son of Atreus,"…
lines.gloss: ἤ 'or'; φάσγανον (acc. sg.) 'sword'; ὀξύ (acc. sg. adj.) 'sharp'; ἐρυσσάμενος (aor. mid. participle) 'drawing (for himself)'; παρὰ μηροῦ (gen. sg.) 'from beside his thigh'.

lines.original: τοὺς μὲν ἀναστήσειεν, ὃ δʼ Ἀτρεΐδην ἐναρίζοι,
lines.english: turn roving home if we would escape destruction, for we are being cut down by war and pestilence at once. Let us ask some priest or seer [], or some reader of dreams (for dreams,…
lines.gloss: τοὺς μέν 'the others' (acc. pl., direct object); ἀναστήσειεν (aor. opt. of ἀνίστημι) 'make stand up, disperse'; ὃ δέ 'but he' (nom. sg., subject, Achilles); Ἀτρεΐδην (acc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (Agamemnon); ἐναρίζοι (pres. opt. of ἐναρίζω) 'slay, kill'.

lines.original: ἦε χόλον παύσειεν ἐρητύσειέ τε θυμόν.
lines.english: turn roving home if we would escape destruction, for we are being cut down by war and pestilence at once. Let us ask some priest or seer [], or some reader of dreams (for dreams,…
lines.gloss: ἦε 'or' (introducing alternative); χόλον (acc. sg. of χόλος) 'anger, wrath'; παύσειεν (aor. opt. of παύω) 'make cease, stop'; ἐρητύσειε (aor. opt. of ἐρητύω) 'restrain, check'; τε 'and'; θυμόν (acc. sg. of θυμός) 'spirit, passion.'

lines.original: ἧος ὃ ταῦθʼ ὥρμαινε κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν,
lines.english: turn roving home if we would escape destruction, for we are being cut down by war and pestilence at once. Let us ask some priest or seer [], or some reader of dreams (for dreams,…
lines.gloss: ἧος 'while' (temporal conjunction); ὥρμαινε (imperf. 3rd sg. of ὁρμαίνω) 'he was pondering, debating'; κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν 'in his mind and heart' (distributive κατά with acc., indicating the seat of deliberation); ταῦθ(α) (neut. acc. pl. demonstrative) 'these things.'

lines.original: ἕλκετο δʼ ἐκ κολεοῖο μέγα ξίφος, ἦλθε δʼ Ἀθήνη
lines.english: turn roving home if we would escape destruction, for we are being cut down by war and pestilence at once. Let us ask some priest or seer [], or some reader of dreams (for dreams,…
lines.gloss: ἕλκετο (imperf. mid.) 'he was drawing (for himself)'; ἐκ κολεοῖο (gen. sg. of κολεός) 'from the scabbard'; μέγα ξίφος (acc. sg. neut.) 'great sword'; ἦλθε (aor.) 'came'; Ἀθήνη (nom. sg.) 'Athena.'

lines.original: οὐρανόθεν· πρὸ γὰρ ἧκε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη
lines.english: turn roving home if we would escape destruction, for we are being cut down by war and pestilence at once. Let us ask some priest or seer [], or some reader of dreams (for dreams,…
lines.gloss: οὐρανόθεν 'from heaven' (adverb with directional suffix -θεν); πρὸ (adverb) 'forth, forward'; ἧκε (aor. of ἵημι) 'sent'; λευκώλενος (nom. sg. fem.) 'white-armed' (epithet modifying Ἥρη).

lines.original: ἄμφω ὁμῶς θυμῷ φιλέουσά τε κηδομένη τε·
lines.english: whether it is for some vow that we have broken, or hecatomb that we have not offered, and whether he will accept the savor of lambs and goats without blemish, so as to take away…
lines.gloss: ἄμφω (acc. dual) 'both'; ὁμῶς (adv.) 'equally, alike'; θυμῷ (dat. sg.) 'in heart/spirit'; φιλέουσα (pres. part. nom. sg. fem.) 'loving'; κηδομένη (pres. part. nom. sg. fem., from κήδομαι) 'caring for, being concerned for'; both participles agree with the subject θεά (Hera) and govern ἄμφω (Achilles and Agamemnon).

lines.original: στῆ δʼ ὄπιθεν, ξανθῆς δὲ κόμης ἕλε Πηλεΐωνα
lines.english: whether it is for some vow that we have broken, or hecatomb that we have not offered, and whether he will accept the savor of lambs and goats without blemish, so as to take away…
lines.gloss: στῆ (3rd sg. aor. of ἵστημι) 'stood, took her stand'; ὄπιθεν (adv.) 'behind, from behind'; ξανθῆς (gen. sg. fem. of ξανθός) 'blonde, golden'; κόμης (gen. sg. of κόμη) 'hair'; ἕλε (3rd sg. aor. of αἱρέω) 'seized, took hold of'; Πηλεΐωνα (acc. sg.) 'son of Peleus' (i.e., Achilles).

lines.original: οἴῳ φαινομένη· τῶν δʼ ἄλλων οὔ τις ὁρᾶτο·
lines.english: whether it is for some vow that we have broken, or hecatomb that we have not offered, and whether he will accept the savor of lambs and goats without blemish, so as to take away…
lines.gloss: οἴῳ (dat. sg. masc. of οἶος) 'to him alone'; φαινομένη (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. fem.) 'appearing, being visible'; τῶν δʼ ἄλλων (gen. pl. of ἄλλος) 'of the others'; οὔ τις 'no one'; ὁρᾶτο (imperf. mid./pass.) 'saw, beheld'.

lines.original: θάμβησεν δʼ Ἀχιλεύς, μετὰ δʼ ἐτράπετʼ, αὐτίκα δʼ ἔγνω
lines.english: whether it is for some vow that we have broken, or hecatomb that we have not offered, and whether he will accept the savor of lambs and goats without blemish, so as to take away…
lines.gloss: θάμβησεν (3rd sg. aor. of θαμβέω) 'was amazed, astonished'; μετὰ δʼ ἐτράπετʼ (3rd sg. aor. mid. of τρέπω) 'turned around'; αὐτίκα 'immediately, at once'; ἔγνω (3rd sg. aor. of γιγνώσκω) 'recognized, knew'.

lines.original: Παλλάδʼ Ἀθηναίην· δεινὼ δέ οἱ ὄσσε φάανθεν·
lines.english: whether it is for some vow that we have broken, or hecatomb that we have not offered, and whether he will accept the savor of lambs and goats without blemish, so as to take away…
lines.gloss: Παλλάδʼ Ἀθηναίην (acc. sg.) 'Pallas Athena' (object of ἔγνω from previous line); δεινὼ (nom. dual, masc./neut. of δεινός) 'terrible, dreadful'; οἱ (dat. sg. pronoun) 'to him, for him' (dative of reference); ὄσσε (nom./acc. dual of ὄσσε) 'eyes'; φάανθεν (3rd pl. aor. pass. of φαίνω) 'shone, gleamed.'

lines.original: καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
lines.english: who knew things past present and to come, rose to speak. He it was who had guided the Achaeans with their fleet to, through the prophesyings with which Phoebus Apollo had inspired…
lines.gloss: μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him/her' (enclitic form); φωνήσας (aor. participle, nom. sg. masc.) 'addressing, calling to'; ἔπεα πτερόεντα (acc. pl. neut.) 'winged words' (formulaic phrase for swift, apt speech); προσηύδα (impf. 3rd sg.) 'he/she addressed, spoke to'.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖτε προσέειπε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: who knew things past present and to come, rose to speak. He it was who had guided the Achaeans with their fleet to, through the prophesyings with which Phoebus Apollo had inspired…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. masc. of ὁ) 'him'; αὖτε 'again, in turn'; προσέειπε (3rd sg. aor. of προσεῖπον) 'addressed, spoke to'; θεὰ (nom. sg.) 'goddess'; γλαυκῶπις (nom. sg. fem. adj.) 'bright-eyed, gleaming-eyed' (epithet of Athena); Ἀθήνη (nom. sg.) 'Athena'.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: who knew things past present and to come, rose to speak. He it was who had guided the Achaeans with their fleet to, through the prophesyings with which Phoebus Apollo had inspired…
lines.gloss: τὴν (acc. sg. of ἥ) 'her'; ἀπαμειβόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc.) 'answering in turn, replying'; προσέφη (3rd sg. aor. of προσφημί) 'addressed, spoke to'; πόδας ὠκύς (nom. sg. masc., accusative of respect) 'swift-footed'; Ἀχιλλεύς (nom. sg.) 'Achilles.'

lines.original: ἦ καὶ ἐπʼ ἀργυρέῃ κώπῃ σχέθε χεῖρα βαρεῖαν,
lines.english: who knew things past present and to come, rose to speak. He it was who had guided the Achaeans with their fleet to, through the prophesyings with which Phoebus Apollo had inspired…
lines.gloss: ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed'; ἐπί (+ dat.) 'upon'; ἀργυρέῃ (dat. sg. fem. of ἀργύρεος) 'silver'; κώπῃ (dat. sg. of κώπη) 'hilt, handle'; σχέθε (3rd sg. aor. of ἔχω, here intransitive) 'held, checked'; χεῖρα (acc. sg. of χείρ) 'hand'; βαρεῖαν (acc. sg. fem. of βαρύς) 'heavy, strong'.

lines.original: ἂψ δʼ ἐς κουλεὸν ὦσε μέγα ξίφος, οὐδʼ ἀπίθησε
lines.english: who knew things past present and to come, rose to speak. He it was who had guided the Achaeans with their fleet to, through the prophesyings with which Phoebus Apollo had inspired…
lines.gloss: ἂψ (adv.) 'back again'; κουλεόν (acc. sg.) 'sheath, scabbard'; ὦσε (aor. of ὠθέω) 'thrust, pushed'; μέγα ξίφος (acc. sg.) 'great sword'; ἀπίθησε (aor. of ἀπειθέω) 'disobey, refuse' (with negation: 'he did not disobey').

lines.original: μύθῳ Ἀθηναίης· ἣ δʼ Οὔλυμπον δὲ βεβήκει
lines.english: anger [] of King Apollo, I will therefore do so; but consider first and swear that you will stand by me heartily in word and deed, for I know that I shall offend one who rules the…

lines.original: δώματʼ ἐς αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς μετὰ δαίμονας ἄλλους.
lines.english: anger [] of King Apollo, I will therefore do so; but consider first and swear that you will stand by me heartily in word and deed, for I know that I shall offend one who rules the…
lines.gloss: δώματα (acc. pl. of δῶμα) 'halls, palace'; αἰγιόχοιο (gen. sg. of αἰγίοχος) 'aegis-bearing'; μετά (prep. + acc.) 'among, to join'; δαίμονας (acc. pl. of δαίμων) 'divinities, gods'.

lines.original: Πηλεΐδης δʼ ἐξαῦτις ἀταρτηροῖς ἐπέεσσιν
lines.english: anger [] of King Apollo, I will therefore do so; but consider first and swear that you will stand by me heartily in word and deed, for I know that I shall offend one who rules the…
lines.gloss: Πηλεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Peleus' (i.e., Achilles); δ' = δέ (postpositive particle) 'and, but'; ἐξαῦτις (adv.) 'again, once more'; ἀταρτηροῖς (dat. pl. of ἀταρτηρός) 'abusive, reproachful'; ἐπέεσσιν (dat. pl. of ἔπος) 'with words, speeches.'

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδην προσέειπε, καὶ οὔ πω λῆγε χόλοιο·
lines.english: anger [] of King Apollo, I will therefore do so; but consider first and swear that you will stand by me heartily in word and deed, for I know that I shall offend one who rules the…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδην (acc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (i.e., Agamemnon), object of προσέειπε (aor. 3rd sg.) 'he addressed'; οὔ πω 'not yet'; λῆγε (imperf. 3rd sg. of λήγω) 'he was ceasing'; χόλοιο (gen. sg. of χόλος) 'anger, wrath' (gen. of separation).

lines.original: ὣς φάτο Πηλεΐδης, ποτὶ δὲ σκῆπτρον βάλε γαίῃ
lines.english: anger [] of King Apollo, I will therefore do so; but consider first and swear that you will stand by me heartily in word and deed, for I know that I shall offend one who rules the…
lines.gloss: ὣς φάτο (aor. mid. of φημί) 'thus he spoke'; Πηλεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Peleus,' i.e., Achilles; ποτί (= πρός) 'toward, to'; σκῆπτρον (acc. sg.) 'staff, scepter'; βάλε (aor. of βάλλω) 'he hurled, threw'; γαίῃ (dat. sg. of γαῖα) 'to the ground.'

lines.original: χρυσείοις ἥλοισι πεπαρμένον, ἕζετο δʼ αὐτός·
lines.english: A plain man cannot stand against the anger of a king, who if he swallow his displeasure now, will yet nurse revenge till he has wreaked it. Consider, therefore, whether or no you…
lines.gloss: χρυσείοις (dat. pl. of χρύσεος) 'golden'; ἥλοισι (dat. pl. of ἧλος) 'with nails, studs'; πεπαρμένον (perf. pass. part. of πείρω, acc. sg.) 'studded, fixed'; ἕζετο (aor. mid. of ἵζω) 'sat down'; αὐτός (nom. sg.) 'himself' (emphatic).

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης δʼ ἑτέρωθεν ἐμήνιε· τοῖσι δὲ Νέστωρ
lines.english: A plain man cannot stand against the anger of a king, who if he swallow his displeasure now, will yet nurse revenge till he has wreaked it. Consider, therefore, whether or no you…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (i.e., Agamemnon); ἑτέρωθεν (adv.) 'on the other side, for his part'; ἐμήνιε (imperf. 3rd sg. of μηνίω) 'was angry, nursed wrath'; τοῖσι (dat. pl. demonstrative) 'to them, among them'; Νέστωρ (nom. sg.) 'Nestor' (subject of verb in next line).

lines.original: ἡδυεπὴς ἀνόρουσε λιγὺς Πυλίων ἀγορητής,
lines.english: A plain man cannot stand against the anger of a king, who if he swallow his displeasure now, will yet nurse revenge till he has wreaked it. Consider, therefore, whether or no you…
lines.gloss: ἡδυεπής (nom. sg. masc.) 'sweet-spoken, honey-voiced'; ἀνόρουσε (aor. act. indic. 3rd sg. of ἀνορούω) 'sprang up, rose'; λιγύς (nom. sg. masc.) 'clear-voiced, shrill'; Πυλίων (gen. pl. of Πύλιος) 'of the Pylians'; ἀγορητής (nom. sg.) 'speaker, orator, counselor'.

lines.original: τοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ γλώσσης μέλιτος γλυκίων ῥέεν αὐδή·
lines.english: A plain man cannot stand against the anger of a king, who if he swallow his displeasure now, will yet nurse revenge till he has wreaked it. Consider, therefore, whether or no you…
lines.gloss: τοῦ (gen. sg. of ὅς) 'of whom, his'; γλώσσης (gen. sg. of γλῶσσα) 'tongue'; μέλιτος (gen. sg. of μέλι) 'honey'; γλυκίων (comparative of γλυκύς) 'sweeter'; ῥέεν (impf. of ῥέω) 'flowed'; αὐδή (nom. sg. of αὐδή) 'voice, speech.'

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἤδη δύο μὲν γενεαὶ μερόπων ἀνθρώπων
lines.english: A plain man cannot stand against the anger of a king, who if he swallow his displeasure now, will yet nurse revenge till he has wreaked it. Consider, therefore, whether or no you…
lines.gloss: τῷ (dat. sg. demonstrative) 'for him' (referring to Nestor); δύο 'two'; γενεαί (nom. pl. of γενεά) 'generations'; μερόπων (gen. pl. of μέροψ, epithet) 'of articulate-speaking' or 'mortal'; ἀνθρώπων (gen. pl. of ἄνθρωπος) 'of men'; ἤδη 'already'; ἐφθίαθʼ (= ἔφθιαθεν, 3rd pl. pluperfect of φθίω) 'had passed away, perished.'

lines.original: ἐφθίαθʼ, οἵ οἱ πρόσθεν ἅμα τράφεν ἠδʼ ἐγένοντο
lines.english: "Fear not, but speak as it is borne in upon you from heaven, for by Apollo, Kalkhas, to whom you pray, and whose oracles you reveal to us, not a Danaan at our ships shall lay his…
lines.gloss: ἐφθίαθʼ (3rd pl. pluperfect of φθίω) 'had perished, passed away'; οἵ (nom. pl. relative pronoun) 'who'; πρόσθεν (adverb) 'before, formerly'; ἅμα (adverb) 'together with (him)'; τράφεν (3rd pl. aorist passive of τρέφω) 'were reared, grew up'; ἠδʼ = ἠδέ (conjunction) 'and'; ἐγένοντο (3rd pl. aorist middle of γίγνομαι) 'were born'.

lines.original: ἐν Πύλῳ ἠγαθέῃ, μετὰ δὲ τριτάτοισιν ἄνασσεν·
lines.english: "Fear not, but speak as it is borne in upon you from heaven, for by Apollo, Kalkhas, to whom you pray, and whose oracles you reveal to us, not a Danaan at our ships shall lay his…
lines.gloss: ἐν Πύλῳ ἠγαθέῃ 'in sacred Pylos' (locative phrase; ἠγαθέῃ 'holy, noble'); μετὰ δὲ τριτάτοισιν 'and among the third generation' (dat. pl. of τρίτατος, 'third'); ἄνασσεν (impf. of ἀνάσσω) 'he ruled, was king.'

lines.original: ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·
lines.english: "Fear not, but speak as it is borne in upon you from heaven, for by Apollo, Kalkhas, to whom you pray, and whose oracles you reveal to us, not a Danaan at our ships shall lay his…
lines.gloss: σφιν (dat. pl. pronoun) 'to them, for them'; ἐὺ φρονέων (pres. participle, nom. sg.) 'thinking well, being well-disposed'; ἀγορήσατο (aor. mid.) 'addressed (the assembly), spoke'; μετέειπεν (aor.) 'spoke among them, addressed'.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: "Fear not, but speak as it is borne in upon you from heaven, for by Apollo, Kalkhas, to whom you pray, and whose oracles you reveal to us, not a Danaan at our ships shall lay his…
lines.gloss: τὸν (acc. sg. of ὁ, demonstrative) 'him'; ἀπαμειβόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'answering, replying'; προσέφη (3rd sg. aor. of προσφημί) 'spoke to, addressed'; κρείων (nom. sg., epithet) 'lord, ruler'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) 'Agamemnon' (subject of the verb).

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἄρʼ ὑποβλήδην ἠμείβετο δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: "Fear not, but speak as it is borne in upon you from heaven, for by Apollo, Kalkhas, to whom you pray, and whose oracles you reveal to us, not a Danaan at our ships shall lay his…
lines.gloss: ὑποβλήδην (adverb) 'looking darkly/from under, with a scowling glance'; ἠμείβετο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of ἀμείβομαι) 'answered, replied'; δῖος (epithet, nom. sg.) 'noble, godlike'; ἄρα (particle) marks transition or emphasis.

lines.original: ὣς τώ γʼ ἀντιβίοισι μαχεσσαμένω ἐπέεσσιν
lines.english: no, not though you name Agamemnon himself, who is by far the foremost of the Achaeans." Thereon the seer [] spoke boldly. "The god," he said, "is angry neither about vow nor…
lines.gloss: ὣς 'thus, so'; τώ (nom. dual) 'the two'; ἀντιβίοισι (dat. dual of ἀντίβιος) 'opposing, hostile'; μαχεσσαμένω (aor. mid. participle, nom. dual) 'having fought, contended'; ἐπέεσσιν (dat. pl. of ἔπος) 'with words, speeches'.

lines.original: ἀνστήτην, λῦσαν δʼ ἀγορὴν παρὰ νηυσὶν Ἀχαιῶν·
lines.english: no, not though you name Agamemnon himself, who is by far the foremost of the Achaeans." Thereon the seer [] spoke boldly. "The god," he said, "is angry neither about vow nor…
lines.gloss: ἀνστήτην (dual aor. of ἀνίστημι) 'they two stood up, arose'; λῦσαν (3rd pl. aor. of λύω) 'they dissolved, broke up'; ἀγορήν (acc. sg.) 'assembly'; παρά (prep. + dat.) 'beside, by'; νηυσίν (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: Πηλεΐδης μὲν ἐπὶ κλισίας καὶ νῆας ἐΐσας
lines.english: no, not though you name Agamemnon himself, who is by far the foremost of the Achaeans." Thereon the seer [] spoke boldly. "The god," he said, "is angry neither about vow nor…
lines.gloss: Πηλεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Peleus' (i.e., Achilles); μέν (postpositive particle) marks contrast with following clause; ἐπί (prep. + acc.) 'to, toward'; κλισίας (acc. pl. of κλισίη) 'huts, shelters'; ἐΐσας (acc. pl. fem. of ἐΐσας) 'well-balanced, well-proportioned' (modifying νῆας).

lines.original: ἤϊε σύν τε Μενοιτιάδῃ καὶ οἷς ἑτάροισιν·
lines.english: no, not though you name Agamemnon himself, who is by far the foremost of the Achaeans." Thereon the seer [] spoke boldly. "The god," he said, "is angry neither about vow nor…
lines.gloss: ἤϊε (3rd sg. impf. of εἶμι) 'went, departed'; σύν (prep. + dat.) 'with, together with'; Μενοιτιάδῃ (dat. sg.) 'son of Menoetius' (i.e., Patroclus); οἷς (dat. pl. possessive adj.) 'his own'; ἑτάροισιν (dat. pl. of ἑταῖρος) 'companions, comrades.'

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης δʼ ἄρα νῆα θοὴν ἅλα δὲ προέρυσσεν,
lines.english: no, not though you name Agamemnon himself, who is by far the foremost of the Achaeans." Thereon the seer [] spoke boldly. "The god," he said, "is angry neither about vow nor…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (Agamemnon); θοήν (acc. sg. fem. of θοός) 'swift'; ἅλαδε (adv.) 'to the sea, seaward'; προέρυσσεν (aor. of προερύω) 'drew down, launched forth.'

lines.original: ἐν δʼ ἐρέτας ἔκρινεν ἐείκοσιν, ἐς δʼ ἑκατόμβην
lines.english: in that he would not free his daughter nor take a ransom for her; therefore has he sent these evils upon us, and will yet send others. He will not deliver the Danaans from this…
lines.gloss: ἐν ... ἐρέτας (acc. pl. of ἐρέτης) 'rowers, oarsmen'; ἔκρινεν (aor. of κρίνω) 'chose, selected'; ἐείκοσιν (indecl. numeral) 'twenty'; ἑκατόμβην (acc. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatomb, great sacrifice (originally of 100 oxen)'.

lines.original: βῆσε θεῷ, ἀνὰ δὲ Χρυσηΐδα καλλιπάρῃον
lines.english: in that he would not free his daughter nor take a ransom for her; therefore has he sent these evils upon us, and will yet send others. He will not deliver the Danaans from this…
lines.gloss: βῆσε (aor. of βαίνω) 'he caused to embark' or 'he placed aboard' (θεῷ dative 'for the god'); ἀνὰ δέ 'and upon [the ship], up'; Χρυσηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Chryseis'; καλλιπάρῃον (acc. sg. fem. of καλλιπάρῃος) 'fair-cheeked, beautiful-cheeked.'

lines.original: εἷσεν ἄγων· ἐν δʼ ἀρχὸς ἔβη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς.
lines.english: in that he would not free his daughter nor take a ransom for her; therefore has he sent these evils upon us, and will yet send others. He will not deliver the Danaans from this…
lines.gloss: εἷσεν (3rd sg. aor. of ἵζω) 'seated, placed aboard'; ἄγων (pres. part. nom. sg. of ἄγω) 'leading, bringing'; ἀρχός (nom. sg.) 'leader, commander'; ἔβη (3rd sg. aor. of βαίνω) 'went, stepped aboard'; πολύμητις (nom. sg. adj.) 'of many counsels, resourceful'—an epithet modifying Ὀδυσσεύς.

lines.original: οἳ μὲν ἔπειτʼ ἀναβάντες ἐπέπλεον ὑγρὰ κέλευθα,
lines.english: in that he would not free his daughter nor take a ransom for her; therefore has he sent these evils upon us, and will yet send others. He will not deliver the Danaans from this…
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun) 'they who'; ἀναβάντες (aor. participle, nom. pl. masc. of ἀναβαίνω) 'having embarked, boarding'; ἐπέπλεον (imperf. 3rd pl. of ἐπιπλέω) 'they sailed over/across'; ὑγρὰ κέλευθα (acc. pl. neut.) 'the watery paths' or 'the wet ways' (poetic for the sea).

lines.original: λαοὺς δʼ Ἀτρεΐδης ἀπολυμαίνεσθαι ἄνωγεν·
lines.english: in that he would not free his daughter nor take a ransom for her; therefore has he sent these evils upon us, and will yet send others. He will not deliver the Danaans from this…
lines.gloss: λαοὺς (acc. pl. of λαός) 'the people, troops'; Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (Agamemnon); ἀπολυμαίνεσθαι (pres. mid. inf. of ἀπολυμαίνομαι) 'to purify themselves, cleanse themselves'; ἄνωγεν (impf. of ἄνωγα) 'commanded, ordered.'

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἀπελυμαίνοντο καὶ εἰς ἅλα λύματα βάλλον,
lines.english: to. Thus we may perhaps appease him." With these words he sat down, and Agamemnon rose in anger. His heart was black with rage, and his eyes flashed fire Chryse
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. of ὅς) 'they'; ἀπελυμαίνοντο (impf. mid./pass., 3rd pl. of ἀπολυμαίνομαι) 'purified themselves, cleansed themselves'; εἰς ἅλα 'into the sea' (ἅλς, acc. sg.); λύματα (acc. pl. of λῦμα) 'defilements, pollutions, refuse from purification'; βάλλον (impf. act., 3rd pl. of βάλλω) 'they threw, cast'.

lines.original: ἕρδον δʼ Ἀπόλλωνι τεληέσσας ἑκατόμβας
lines.english: to. Thus we may perhaps appease him." With these words he sat down, and Agamemnon rose in anger. His heart was black with rage, and his eyes flashed fire Chryse
lines.gloss: ἕρδον (3rd pl. impf. of ἕρδω) 'they performed, sacrificed'; Ἀπόλλωνι (dat. sg.) 'to Apollo'; τεληέσσας (acc. pl. fem. of τελήεις) 'perfect, complete'; ἑκατόμβας (acc. pl. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatombs' (sacrifices of many animals, literally 'hundred oxen').

lines.original: ταύρων ἠδʼ αἰγῶν παρὰ θῖνʼ ἁλὸς ἀτρυγέτοιο·
lines.english: to. Thus we may perhaps appease him." With these words he sat down, and Agamemnon rose in anger. His heart was black with rage, and his eyes flashed fire Chryse
lines.gloss: ταύρων (gen. pl. of ταῦρος) 'of bulls'; ἠδέ (conjunction) 'and'; αἰγῶν (gen. pl. of αἴξ) 'of goats'; παρά (prep. with acc.) 'along, beside'; θῖνα (acc. sg. of θίς) 'shore, beach'; ἁλός (gen. sg. of ἅλς) 'of the sea'; ἀτρυγέτοιο (gen. sg. of ἀτρύγετος, epithet) 'barren, unharvested' or 'unweariable.'

lines.original: κνίση δʼ οὐρανὸν ἷκεν ἑλισσομένη περὶ καπνῷ.
lines.english: to. Thus we may perhaps appease him." With these words he sat down, and Agamemnon rose in anger. His heart was black with rage, and his eyes flashed fire Chryse
lines.gloss: κνίση (nom. sg. of κνίσα/κνίση) 'savor of burnt fat, sacrificial smoke'; οὐρανόν (acc. sg.) 'heaven, sky'; ἷκεν (aor. 3rd sg. of ἱκνέομαι) 'reached, came to'; ἑλισσομένη (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. fem.) 'whirling, coiling'; περί (prep. + dat.) 'together with, in company with'; καπνῷ (dat. sg. of καπνός) 'smoke.'

lines.original: ὣς οἳ μὲν τὰ πένοντο κατὰ στρατόν· οὐδʼ Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: to. Thus we may perhaps appease him." With these words he sat down, and Agamemnon rose in anger. His heart was black with rage, and his eyes flashed fire Chryse
lines.gloss: ὣς "thus, so"; οἳ μέν (nom. pl.) "they" (the Achaeans at large); πένοντο (impf. mid. of πένομαι) "were busying themselves, toiling"; κατὰ στρατόν "throughout the camp"; οὐδέ "nor, and not"; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) "Agamemnon" (transitioning to a contrasting action by the king).

lines.original: λῆγʼ ἔριδος τὴν πρῶτον ἐπηπείλησʼ Ἀχιλῆϊ,
lines.english: as he scowled on Kalkhas and said, "Seer [] of evil, you never yet prophesied smooth things concerning me, but have ever loved to foretell that which was evil. You have brought me…
lines.gloss: λῆγʼ (3rd sg. impf. of λήγω) 'was ceasing, leaving off'; ἔριδος (gen. sg. of ἔρις) 'of strife, quarrel'; τὴν πρῶτον 'which at first'; ἐπηπείλησʼ (3rd sg. plupf. of ἐπαπειλέω) 'he had threatened'; Ἀχιλῆϊ (dat. sg.) 'to Achilles.'

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅ γε Ταλθύβιόν τε καὶ Εὐρυβάτην προσέειπε,
lines.english: as he scowled on Kalkhas and said, "Seer [] of evil, you never yet prophesied smooth things concerning me, but have ever loved to foretell that which was evil. You have brought me…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, however'; ὅ γε (nom. sg. masc.) 'he' (i.e., Agamemnon); Ταλθύβιόν τε καὶ Εὐρυβάτην (acc. sg., both proper names) his two heralds; προσέειπε (aor. act. ind., 3rd sg. of προσεῖπον) 'addressed, spoke to'.

lines.original: τώ οἱ ἔσαν κήρυκε καὶ ὀτρηρὼ θεράποντε·
lines.english: as he scowled on Kalkhas and said, "Seer [] of evil, you never yet prophesied smooth things concerning me, but have ever loved to foretell that which was evil. You have brought me…
lines.gloss: τώ (nom. dual) 'the two (of them)'; οἱ (dat. sg. possessive) 'his'; ἔσαν (3rd pl. impf. of εἰμί) 'were'; κήρυκε (nom. dual of κῆρυξ) 'heralds'; ὀτρηρώ (nom. dual adj.) 'ready, swift, attendant'; θεράποντε (nom. dual of θεράπων) 'servants, attendants.'

lines.original: ὣς εἰπὼν προΐει, κρατερὸν δʼ ἐπὶ μῦθον ἔτελλε·
lines.english: as he scowled on Kalkhas and said, "Seer [] of evil, you never yet prophesied smooth things concerning me, but have ever loved to foretell that which was evil. You have brought me…
lines.gloss: ὣς εἰπών (aor. participle of εἶπον) 'having spoken thus'; προΐει (impf. of προΐημι) 'sent forth'; κρατερόν (acc. sg. of κρατερός) 'strong, harsh'; μῦθον (acc. sg. of μῦθος) 'command, word'; ἔτελλε (impf. of τέλλω) 'laid upon them, enjoined'.

lines.original: τὼ δʼ ἀέκοντε βάτην παρὰ θῖνʼ ἁλὸς ἀτρυγέτοιο,
lines.english: as he scowled on Kalkhas and said, "Seer [] of evil, you never yet prophesied smooth things concerning me, but have ever loved to foretell that which was evil. You have brought me…
lines.gloss: τὼ (nom. dual) 'the two (heralds)'; ἀέκοντε (nom. dual pres. part. of ἀέκων) 'unwilling, against their will'; βάτην (3rd dual aor. of βαίνω) 'went'; παρὰ θῖνα (acc. sg. of θίς) 'along the shore'; ἁλὸς ἀτρυγέτοιο (gen. sg. of ἅλς + epithet ἀτρύγετος) 'of the barren/unharvested sea.'

lines.original: Μυρμιδόνων δʼ ἐπί τε κλισίας καὶ νῆας ἱκέσθην,
lines.english: that Apollo has plagued us because I would not take a ransom for this girl, the daughter of Chryses. I have set my heart on keeping her in my own house, for I love her better even…
lines.gloss: Μυρμιδόνων (gen. pl. of Μυρμιδόνες) 'of the Myrmidons' (Achilles' people); ἐπί (preposition + acc.) 'to, toward'; κλισίας (acc. pl. of κλισίη) 'huts, shelters'; ἱκέσθην (aor. mid. 3rd dual of ἱκνέομαι) 'they two arrived at, reached.'

lines.original: τὸν δʼ εὗρον παρά τε κλισίῃ καὶ νηῒ μελαίνῃ

lines.original: χερνίψαντο δʼ ἔπειτα καὶ οὐλοχύτας ἀνέλοντο.
lines.english: either Ajax, or Idomeneus, or yourself, son of Peleus, mighty warrior that you are, that we may offer sacrifice and appease the anger of the god." Achilles scowled at him and…
lines.gloss: χερνίψαντο (aor. mid. of χερνίπτομαι) 'they washed their hands (in ritual purification)'; ἔπειτα 'then, thereupon'; οὐλοχύτας (acc. pl. of οὐλοχύται) 'barley grains' (scattered on sacrifice); ἀνέλοντο (aor. mid. of ἀναιρέω) 'they took up, lifted'.

lines.original: τοῖσιν δὲ Χρύσης μεγάλʼ εὔχετο χεῖρας ἀνασχών·
lines.english: either Ajax, or Idomeneus, or yourself, son of Peleus, mighty warrior that you are, that we may offer sacrifice and appease the anger of the god." Achilles scowled at him and…
lines.gloss: τοῖσιν (dat. pl. pronoun) 'for them, on their behalf'; Χρύσης (nom. sg.) 'Chryses' (the priest); μεγάλα (adv., acc. pl. neut. as adv.) 'loudly, greatly'; εὔχετο (impf. mid.) 'prayed'; χεῖρας (acc. pl. of χείρ) 'hands'; ἀνασχών (aor. act. participle of ἀνέχω) 'having raised up, lifting up.'

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ εὐχόμενος, τοῦ δʼ ἔκλυε Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων.
lines.english: either Ajax, or Idomeneus, or yourself, son of Peleus, mighty warrior that you are, that we may offer sacrifice and appease the anger of the god." Achilles scowled at him and…
lines.gloss: ὣς (adv.) 'thus, in this way'; ἔφατο (3rd sg. impf. mid. of φημί) 'he spoke'; εὐχόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'praying'; τοῦ (gen. sg. of ὅ, demonstrative) 'him, his prayer'; ἔκλυε (3rd sg. aor. of κλύω) 'heard'; Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων (nom.) 'Phoebus Apollo' (epithet + name).

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί ῥʼ εὔξαντο καὶ οὐλοχύτας προβάλοντο,
lines.english: With what heart can any of the Achaeans do your bidding, either on foray or in open fighting? I came to make war here not because the Trojans are responsible [] for any wrong…
lines.gloss: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί 'but when' (conjunction introducing temporal clause); εὔξαντο (aor. mid. 3rd pl. of εὔχομαι) 'they prayed'; οὐλοχύτας (acc. pl. of οὐλοχύτη) 'barley grains' (ritual grains scattered on sacrificial victims); προβάλοντο (aor. mid. 3rd pl. of προβάλλω) 'they threw forward, cast forth.'

lines.original: αὐέρυσαν μὲν πρῶτα καὶ ἔσφαξαν καὶ ἔδειραν,
lines.english: With what heart can any of the Achaeans do your bidding, either on foray or in open fighting? I came to make war here not because the Trojans are responsible [] for any wrong…
lines.gloss: αὐέρυσαν (3rd pl. aor. of ἀνερύω) 'they drew back (the heads of the victims)'; πρῶτα 'first'; ἔσφαξαν (3rd pl. aor. of σφάζω) 'they slaughtered, cut the throats'; ἔδειραν (3rd pl. aor. of δέρω) 'they flayed, skinned'.

lines.original: μηρούς τʼ ἐξέταμον κατά τε κνίσῃ ἐκάλυψαν
lines.english: With what heart can any of the Achaeans do your bidding, either on foray or in open fighting? I came to make war here not because the Trojans are responsible [] for any wrong…
lines.gloss: μηρούς (acc. pl. of μηρός) 'thighbones'; ἐξέταμον (aor. of ἐκτέμνω) 'they cut out'; κατά... ἐκάλυψαν (tmesis, aor. of κατακαλύπτω) 'they covered over'; κνίσῃ (dat. sg. of κνίση) 'with fat' — the ritual preparation of thighbones wrapped in fat for burning as an offering to the gods.

lines.original: δίπτυχα ποιήσαντες, ἐπʼ αὐτῶν δʼ ὠμοθέτησαν·
lines.english: With what heart can any of the Achaeans do your bidding, either on foray or in open fighting? I came to make war here not because the Trojans are responsible [] for any wrong…
lines.gloss: δίπτυχα (acc. pl. neut. of δίπτυχος) 'double-folded, in two layers'; ποιήσαντες (aor. part. nom. pl. masc. of ποιέω) 'having made'; ἐπʼ αὐτῶν 'upon them' (the double-folded pieces); ὠμοθέτησαν (aor. ind. 3rd pl. of ὠμοθετέω) 'they placed the raw meat' (the verb combines ὠμός 'raw' and τίθημι 'to place').

lines.original: καῖε δʼ ἐπὶ σχίζῃς ὁ γέρων, ἐπὶ δʼ αἴθοπα οἶνον
lines.english: nor cut down my harvests on the fertile plains of; for between me and them there is a great space, both mountain and sounding sea. We have followed you, Sir Insolence! for your…
lines.gloss: καῖε (impf. of καίω) 'was burning, roasting'; σχίζῃς (dat. pl. of σχίζη) 'on split logs, billets of wood'; ὁ γέρων 'the old man' (nominative, subject); αἴθοπα (acc. sg. of αἴθοψ) 'gleaming, sparkling' (epithet for wine); οἶνον (acc. sg.) 'wine' (object of λεῖβε understood from next line, or of an implied verb of pouring).

lines.original: λεῖβε· νέοι δὲ παρʼ αὐτὸν ἔχον πεμπώβολα χερσίν.
lines.english: nor cut down my harvests on the fertile plains of; for between me and them there is a great space, both mountain and sounding sea. We have followed you, Sir Insolence! for your…
lines.gloss: λεῖβε (3rd sg. impf. of λείβω) 'he poured (libation)'; νέοι (nom. pl.) 'young men'; παρʼ αὐτόν 'beside him'; ἔχον (3rd pl. impf. of ἔχω) 'held'; πεμπώβολα (acc. pl. of πεμπώβολος) 'five-pronged forks' (for distributing meat); χερσίν (dat. pl. of χείρ) 'in their hands.'

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ κατὰ μῆρε κάη καὶ σπλάγχνα πάσαντο,
lines.english: nor cut down my harvests on the fertile plains of; for between me and them there is a great space, both mountain and sounding sea. We have followed you, Sir Insolence! for your…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ 'but, and then'; ἐπεί 'when, after'; κατὰ κάη (3rd sg. aor. pass. of κατακαίω) 'were burned up/consumed'; μῆρε (dual acc. of μηρός) 'thighs' (of the sacrificial animal); σπλάγχνα (neut. acc. pl.) 'entrails, inner organs'; πάσαντο (3rd pl. aor. mid. of πατέομαι) 'they tasted, ate.'

lines.original: μίστυλλόν τʼ ἄρα τἆλλα καὶ ἀμφʼ ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν,
lines.english: nor cut down my harvests on the fertile plains of; for between me and them there is a great space, both mountain and sounding sea. We have followed you, Sir Insolence! for your…
lines.gloss: μίστυλλον (3rd pl. impf. of μιστυλλεύω) 'they cut up, carved into pieces'; τἆλλα (crasis for τὰ ἄλλα, acc. pl. neut.) 'the other parts, the rest'; ἀμφ(ί) (preposition) 'on, around'; ὀβελοῖσιν (dat. pl. of ὀβελός) 'on spits'; ἔπειραν (3rd pl. aor. of πείρω) 'they pierced, spitted'.

lines.original: ὤπτησάν τε περιφραδέως, ἐρύσαντό τε πάντα.
lines.english: nor cut down my harvests on the fertile plains of; for between me and them there is a great space, both mountain and sounding sea. We have followed you, Sir Insolence! for your…
lines.gloss: ὤπτησαν (3rd pl. aor. indic. of ὀπτάω) 'they roasted'; περιφραδέως (adv.) 'carefully, skillfully'; ἐρύσαντο (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of ἐρύω) 'they drew off, pulled (from the spits)'; πάντα (acc. pl. neut.) 'all things, everything'.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ παύσαντο πόνου τετύκοντό τε δαῖτα
lines.english: You forget this, and threaten to rob me of the prize for which I have toiled, and which the sons of the Achaeans have given me. Never when the Achaeans sack any rich city of the…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ 'but, and then' (postpositive conjunction); ἐπεί 'when, after' (temporal conjunction); παύσαντο (aor. mid. 3rd pl. of παύω) 'they ceased, stopped'; πόνου (gen. sg. of πόνος) 'from toil, labor'; τετύκοντο (pluperfect mid./pass. 3rd pl. of τεύχω) 'they had prepared, made ready'; δαῖτα (acc. sg. of δαίς) 'the feast, banquet'.

lines.original: δαίνυντʼ, οὐδέ τι θυμὸς ἐδεύετο δαιτὸς ἐΐσης.
lines.english: You forget this, and threaten to rob me of the prize for which I have toiled, and which the sons of the Achaeans have given me. Never when the Achaeans sack any rich city of the…
lines.gloss: δαίνυντο (3rd pl. impf. mid. of δαίνυμι) 'they feasted'; οὐδέ τι 'not at all, in no way'; θυμός (nom. sg.) 'heart, spirit'; ἐδεύετο (3rd sg. impf. pass. of δεύομαι) 'was lacking, wanted'; δαιτός (gen. sg. of δαίς) 'feast'; ἐΐσης (gen. sg. fem. of ἐΐσος) 'equal, fair, well-shared.'

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο,
lines.english: You forget this, and threaten to rob me of the prize for which I have toiled, and which the sons of the Achaeans have given me. Never when the Achaeans sack any rich city of the…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ 'but, and then'; ἐπεί 'when, after'; πόσιος (gen. sg. of πόσις) 'drinking'; ἐδητύος (gen. sg. of ἐδητύς) 'eating, food'; ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο (aor. mid. of ἵημι) 'they satisfied their desire (for),' literally 'sent themselves out of desire.'

lines.original: κοῦροι μὲν κρητῆρας ἐπεστέψαντο ποτοῖο,
lines.english: You forget this, and threaten to rob me of the prize for which I have toiled, and which the sons of the Achaeans have given me. Never when the Achaeans sack any rich city of the…
lines.gloss: κοῦροι (nom. pl. of κοῦρος) 'young men, youths'; κρητῆρας (acc. pl. of κρητήρ) 'mixing-bowls' (large vessels for mixing wine and water); ἐπεστέψαντο (aor. mid. of ἐπιστέφω) 'crowned, filled to the brim'; ποτοῖο (gen. sg. of ποτός) 'of drink, of the beverage.'

lines.original: νώμησαν δʼ ἄρα πᾶσιν ἐπαρξάμενοι δεπάεσσιν·
lines.english: You forget this, and threaten to rob me of the prize for which I have toiled, and which the sons of the Achaeans have given me. Never when the Achaeans sack any rich city of the…
lines.gloss: νώμησαν (3rd pl. aor. of νέμω) 'they distributed, served out'; ἄρα 'then' (particle); πᾶσιν (dat. pl. of πᾶς) 'to all'; ἐπαρξάμενοι (aor. mid. participle, nom. pl.) 'having made first offerings, having begun with ritual offerings'; δεπάεσσιν (dat. pl. of δέπας) 'cups, goblets' (dative of means).

lines.original: οἳ δὲ πανημέριοι μολπῇ θεὸν ἱλάσκοντο
lines.english: though it is my hands that do the better part of the fighting. When the sharing comes, your share is far the largest, and I, indeed, must go back to my ships, take what I can get…
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun) 'they who'; πανημέριοι (nom. pl. adj.) 'all day long, the whole day'; μολπῇ (dat. sg. of μολπή) 'with song, with choral dance'; θεόν (acc. sg. of θεός) 'the god'; ἱλάσκοντο (impf. mid. of ἱλάσκομαι) 'they were appeasing, they propitiated.'

lines.original: καλὸν ἀείδοντες παιήονα κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: though it is my hands that do the better part of the fighting. When the sharing comes, your share is far the largest, and I, indeed, must go back to my ships, take what I can get…
lines.gloss: καλὸν (acc. sg. of καλός) 'beautiful, lovely'; ἀείδοντες (pres. part. nom. pl. of ἀείδω) 'singing'; παιήονα (acc. sg. of παιήων) 'paean, hymn of praise/healing'; κοῦροι (nom. pl. of κοῦρος) 'youths, young men'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: μέλποντες ἑκάεργον· ὃ δὲ φρένα τέρπετʼ ἀκούων.
lines.english: though it is my hands that do the better part of the fighting. When the sharing comes, your share is far the largest, and I, indeed, must go back to my ships, take what I can get…
lines.gloss: μέλποντες (pres. part. nom. pl. of μέλπω) 'celebrating, singing'; ἑκάεργον (acc. sg. epithet of Apollo) 'far-worker, far-shooter'; φρένα (acc. sg. of φρήν) 'heart, mind' (internal acc. with τέρπετο); τέρπετο (imperf. mid. of τέρπω) 'he took pleasure, was delighted'; ἀκούων (pres. part. of ἀκούω) 'hearing, listening'.

lines.original: ἦμος δʼ ἠέλιος κατέδυ καὶ ἐπὶ κνέφας ἦλθε,
lines.english: though it is my hands that do the better part of the fighting. When the sharing comes, your share is far the largest, and I, indeed, must go back to my ships, take what I can get…
lines.gloss: ἦμος (temporal adv.) 'when, at the time when'; δ(έ) (particle) marks transition; ἠέλιος (nom. sg.) 'sun'; κατέδυ (3rd sg. aor. of καταδύω) 'sank down, set'; ἐπί (adv.) 'upon, thereupon'; κνέφας (nom. sg. neut.) 'darkness, dusk'; ἦλθε (3rd sg. aor. of ἔρχομαι) 'came'.

lines.original: δὴ τότε κοιμήσαντο παρὰ πρυμνήσια νηός·
lines.english: though it is my hands that do the better part of the fighting. When the sharing comes, your share is far the largest, and I, indeed, must go back to my ships, take what I can get…
lines.gloss: δή (particle) 'then, at that time' (emphatic); τότε (adv.) 'then'; κοιμήσαντο (aor. mid. ind., 3rd pl. of κοιμάω) 'they went to sleep, lay down to rest'; παρά (prep. + acc.) 'beside, along'; πρυμνήσια (acc. pl. neut. of πρυμνήσιος) 'stern-cables' or 'things at the stern'; νηός (gen. sg. of ναῦς) 'of the ship'.

lines.original: ἦμος δʼ ἠριγένεια φάνη ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠώς,
lines.english: for me to return home with my ships, for I will not stay here dishonored to gather gold and substance for you." And Agamemnon answered, "Flee if you will, I shall make you no…
lines.gloss: ἦμος (adv.) 'when, at the time when'; ἠριγένεια (nom. sg. fem. epithet) 'early-born'; φάνη (3rd sg. aor. pass. of φαίνω) 'appeared, shone forth'; ῥοδοδάκτυλος (nom. sg. fem. compound adj.) 'rosy-fingered'; Ἠώς (nom. sg.) 'Dawn' (personified goddess).

lines.original: καὶ τότʼ ἔπειτʼ ἀνάγοντο μετὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν·
lines.english: for me to return home with my ships, for I will not stay here dishonored to gather gold and substance for you." And Agamemnon answered, "Flee if you will, I shall make you no…
lines.gloss: ἀνάγοντο (impf. mid., 3rd pl. of ἀνάγω) 'they put to sea, set sail'; μετὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν 'among/through the broad host of the Achaeans' — στρατόν (acc. sg.) 'army, host', εὐρύν (acc. sg. adj.) 'wide, broad', Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans'.

lines.original: τοῖσιν δʼ ἴκμενον οὖρον ἵει ἑκάεργος Ἀπόλλων·
lines.english: for me to return home with my ships, for I will not stay here dishonored to gather gold and substance for you." And Agamemnon answered, "Flee if you will, I shall make you no…
lines.gloss: τοῖσιν (dat. pl.) 'for them'; ἴκμενον (acc. sg. of ἴκμενος) 'favorable, propitious'; οὖρον (acc. sg.) 'wind, breeze'; ἵει (impf. 3rd sg. of ἵημι) 'sent forth'; ἑκάεργος (nom. sg.) 'far-working' (epithet of Apollo).

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἱστὸν στήσαντʼ ἀνά θʼ ἱστία λευκὰ πέτασσαν,
lines.english: for me to return home with my ships, for I will not stay here dishonored to gather gold and substance for you." And Agamemnon answered, "Flee if you will, I shall make you no…
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. of ὅς) 'they'; ἱστόν (acc. sg. of ἱστός) 'mast'; στήσαντ(ε) (aor. participle) 'having set up'; ἀνά (adverb/preverb) 'up'; ἱστία (acc. pl. of ἱστίον) 'sails'; λευκά (acc. pl. of λευκός) 'white'; πέτασσαν (impf. or aor.) 'they spread out, unfurled'.

lines.original: ἐν δʼ ἄνεμος πρῆσεν μέσον ἱστίον, ἀμφὶ δὲ κῦμα
lines.english: for me to return home with my ships, for I will not stay here dishonored to gather gold and substance for you." And Agamemnon answered, "Flee if you will, I shall make you no…
lines.gloss: ἐν (adverbial) 'in, into'; πρῆσεν (aor. of πίμπρημι) 'filled, swelled'; μέσον ἱστίον (acc. sg.) 'the mid-sail, mainsail'; ἀμφὶ δέ 'and around'; κῦμα (nom. sg.) 'wave, billow'.

lines.original: στείρῃ πορφύρεον μεγάλʼ ἴαχε νηὸς ἰούσης·
lines.english: who will do me honor, and above all Zeus, the lord of counsel. There is no king here so hateful to me as you are, for you are ever quarrelsome and ill affected. What though you be…
lines.gloss: στείρῃ (dat. sg. of στεῖρα) 'prow, stem (of a ship)'; πορφύρεον (acc. sg. neut. adj.) 'dark, purple-swelling'; μεγάλʼ (adv., = μεγάλα) 'loudly, greatly'; ἴαχε (3rd sg. aor. of ἰάχω) 'roared, resounded'; νηὸς ἰούσης (gen. sg. fem. pres. part. of εἶμι) 'of the ship going/rushing forward.'

lines.original: ἣ δʼ ἔθεεν κατὰ κῦμα διαπρήσσουσα κέλευθον.
lines.english: who will do me honor, and above all Zeus, the lord of counsel. There is no king here so hateful to me as you are, for you are ever quarrelsome and ill affected. What though you be…
lines.gloss: ἔθεεν (3rd sg. impf. of θέω) 'ran, sped'; κατὰ κῦμα 'over the wave' (κῦμα acc. sg. neut. 'wave, swell'); διαπρήσσουσα (pres. part. fem. nom. sg. of διαπράσσω) 'cutting through, cleaving'; κέλευθον (acc. sg. fem.) 'path, course'.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί ῥʼ ἵκοντο κατὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν,
lines.english: who will do me honor, and above all Zeus, the lord of counsel. There is no king here so hateful to me as you are, for you are ever quarrelsome and ill affected. What though you be…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ (postpositive particle) 'but, now'; ἐπεί (temporal conjunction) 'when, after'; ῥ(α) (enclitic particle, often untranslatable, adds liveliness); ἵκοντο (3rd pl. aor. mid. of ἱκνέομαι) 'they arrived, reached'; κατά (prep. + acc.) 'throughout, among'; στρατόν (acc. sg. of στρατός) 'army, encampment'; εὐρύν (acc. sg. masc. of εὐρύς) 'broad, wide'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: νῆα μὲν οἵ γε μέλαιναν ἐπʼ ἠπείροιο ἔρυσσαν
lines.english: who will do me honor, and above all Zeus, the lord of counsel. There is no king here so hateful to me as you are, for you are ever quarrelsome and ill affected. What though you be…
lines.gloss: νῆα (acc. sg. of ναῦς) 'ship'; μέλαιναν (acc. sg. fem. of μέλας) 'black'; ἐπʼ ἠπείροιο (gen. sg. of ἤπειρος) 'onto the mainland/shore'; ἔρυσσαν (3rd pl. aor. of ἐρύω) 'they dragged, hauled up'.

lines.original: ὑψοῦ ἐπὶ ψαμάθοις, ὑπὸ δʼ ἕρματα μακρὰ τάνυσσαν·
lines.english: who will do me honor, and above all Zeus, the lord of counsel. There is no king here so hateful to me as you are, for you are ever quarrelsome and ill affected. What though you be…
lines.gloss: ὑψοῦ (adv.) 'high up, up high'; ψαμάθοις (dat. pl. of ψάμαθος) 'sandy beach, sand'; ὑπό (prep. with acc.) 'under, beneath'; ἕρματα (acc. pl. of ἕρμα) 'props, supports, shores' (timbers to keep the ship steady); μακρά (acc. pl. neut. adj.) 'long'; τάνυσσαν (3rd pl. aor. of τανύω) 'they stretched, extended.'

lines.original: αὐτοὶ δʼ ἐσκίδναντο κατὰ κλισίας τε νέας τε.
lines.english: to lord it over the Myrmidons. I care neither for you nor for your anger; and thus will I do: since Phoebus Apollo is taking Chryseis from me, I shall send her with my ship and my…
lines.gloss: ἐσκίδναντο (3rd pl. impf. middle of σκίδνημι) 'scattered themselves, dispersed'; κατά (prep. with acc.) 'throughout, among'; κλισίας (acc. pl. of κλισία) 'huts, shelters'; τε ... τε (correlative conjunctions) 'both ... and'; νέας (acc. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships.'

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ μήνιε νηυσὶ παρήμενος ὠκυπόροισι
lines.english: to lord it over the Myrmidons. I care neither for you nor for your anger; and thus will I do: since Phoebus Apollo is taking Chryseis from me, I shall send her with my ship and my…
lines.gloss: αὐτὰρ 'but, however' (adversative particle); μήνιε (impf. 3rd sg. of μηνίω) 'was wrathful, nursed his wrath'; νηυσί (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'by/among the ships'; παρήμενος (pres. mid. ptc.) 'sitting beside, remaining by'; ὠκυπόροισι (dat. pl. of ὠκύπορος) 'swift-sailing' (modifying ships).

lines.original: διογενὴς Πηλῆος υἱὸς πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς·
lines.english: to lord it over the Myrmidons. I care neither for you nor for your anger; and thus will I do: since Phoebus Apollo is taking Chryseis from me, I shall send her with my ship and my…
lines.gloss: διογενὴς (nom. sg. masc.) 'Zeus-born, divine-born'; Πηλῆος (gen. sg.) 'of Peleus'; υἱὸς (nom. sg.) 'son'; πόδας ὠκὺς (acc. pl. + nom. sg., formulaic phrase) 'swift-footed'; Ἀχιλλεύς (nom. sg.) 'Achilles' — the line identifies the sulking hero with standard Homeric epithets.

lines.original: οὔτέ ποτʼ εἰς ἀγορὴν πωλέσκετο κυδιάνειραν
lines.english: to lord it over the Myrmidons. I care neither for you nor for your anger; and thus will I do: since Phoebus Apollo is taking Chryseis from me, I shall send her with my ship and my…
lines.gloss: οὔτε 'nor'; ποτέ (enclitic) 'ever'; εἰς (+ acc.) 'to, into'; ἀγορήν (acc. sg. of ἀγορή) 'assembly, gathering place'; πωλέσκετο (imperf. mid. of πωλέομαι) 'used to go, frequented'; κυδιάνειραν (acc. sg. fem. adj.) 'where men win glory, man-ennobling.'

lines.original: οὔτέ ποτʼ ἐς πόλεμον, ἀλλὰ φθινύθεσκε φίλον κῆρ
lines.english: to lord it over the Myrmidons. I care neither for you nor for your anger; and thus will I do: since Phoebus Apollo is taking Chryseis from me, I shall send her with my ship and my…

lines.original: μητρὶ φίλῃ ἐν χειρὶ τίθει καί μιν προσέειπε·
lines.english: and thrust it back into the scabbard as Athena bade him. Then she went back toamong the other gods [], and to the house of aegis-bearing Zeus. But the son of Peleus again began…
lines.gloss: μητρί (dat. sg. of μήτηρ) 'to his mother'; φίλῃ 'dear, beloved' (dat. sg. fem.); ἐν χειρί 'in the hand' (dat. sg. of χείρ); τίθει (pres. indic. 3rd sg. of τίθημι) 'he places, puts'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'her'; προσέειπε (aor. of προσεῖπον) 'he addressed, spoke to'.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο, μείδησεν δὲ θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη,
lines.english: and thrust it back into the scabbard as Athena bade him. Then she went back toamong the other gods [], and to the house of aegis-bearing Zeus. But the son of Peleus again began…
lines.gloss: ὣς φάτο (3rd sg. aor. of φημί) 'thus he/she spoke'; μείδησεν (3rd sg. aor. of μειδιάω) 'smiled'; θεὰ (nom. sg.) 'goddess'; λευκώλενος (nom. sg. fem. compound adj.) 'white-armed'; Ἥρη (nom. sg.) 'Hera'.

lines.original: μειδήσασα δὲ παιδὸς ἐδέξατο χειρὶ κύπελλον·
lines.english: and thrust it back into the scabbard as Athena bade him. Then she went back toamong the other gods [], and to the house of aegis-bearing Zeus. But the son of Peleus again began…
lines.gloss: μειδήσασα (aor. act. participle, nom. sg. fem.) 'smiling'; παιδός (gen. sg.) 'of her child/son'; ἐδέξατο (aor. mid. indic. 3rd sg.) 'she received, took'; χειρί (dat. sg.) 'with/in her hand'; κύπελλον (acc. sg.) 'cup, goblet'.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ τοῖς ἄλλοισι θεοῖς ἐνδέξια πᾶσιν
lines.english: and thrust it back into the scabbard as Athena bade him. Then she went back toamong the other gods [], and to the house of aegis-bearing Zeus. But the son of Peleus again began…
lines.gloss: αὐτὰρ (particle) 'but, then'; ὃ (nom. sg. masc. pronoun) 'he' (Hephaestus); τοῖς ἄλλοισι θεοῖς (dat. pl.) 'to/for the other gods'; ἐνδέξια (adv.) 'from right to left, rightward' (serving wine in proper ritual direction); πᾶσιν (dat. pl. masc. of πᾶς) 'to all'.

lines.original: οἰνοχόει γλυκὺ νέκταρ ἀπὸ κρητῆρος ἀφύσσων·
lines.english: "Wine-bibber," he cried, "with the face of a dog and the heart of a hind, you never dare to go out with the host in fight, nor yet with our chosen men in ambuscade. You shun this…
lines.gloss: οἰνοχόει (3rd sg. impf. of οἰνοχοέω) 'he poured wine, served as cupbearer'; γλυκὺ νέκταρ (acc. sg.) 'sweet nectar'; ἀπὸ κρητῆρος (gen. sg. of κρητήρ) 'from the mixing-bowl'; ἀφύσσων (pres. part. nom. sg. masc. of ἀφύσσω) 'drawing, ladling out'.

lines.original: ἄσβεστος δʼ ἄρʼ ἐνῶρτο γέλως μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν
lines.english: "Wine-bibber," he cried, "with the face of a dog and the heart of a hind, you never dare to go out with the host in fight, nor yet with our chosen men in ambuscade. You shun this…
lines.gloss: ἄσβεστος (nom. sg. adj.) 'unquenchable, inextinguishable'; ἐνῶρτο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of ἐνόρνυμι) 'arose, broke out'; γέλως (nom. sg.) 'laughter'; μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν (dat. pl.) 'among the blessed gods'—the immortals broke into uncontrollable laughter at the sight of Hephaestus bustling about serving them.

lines.original: ὡς ἴδον Ἥφαιστον διὰ δώματα ποιπνύοντα.
lines.english: "Wine-bibber," he cried, "with the face of a dog and the heart of a hind, you never dare to go out with the host in fight, nor yet with our chosen men in ambuscade. You shun this…
lines.gloss: ὡς (adv.) 'as, when'; ἴδον (3rd pl. aor. of ὁράω) 'they saw'; Ἥφαιστον (acc. sg.) 'Hephaestus'; διὰ δώματα (acc. pl. with διά) 'through the halls'; ποιπνύοντα (pres. part. acc. sg. masc. of ποιπνύω) 'bustling about, hurrying to and fro'.

lines.original: ὣς τότε μὲν πρόπαν ἦμαρ ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα
lines.english: "Wine-bibber," he cried, "with the face of a dog and the heart of a hind, you never dare to go out with the host in fight, nor yet with our chosen men in ambuscade. You shun this…
lines.gloss: ὣς 'thus, so'; τότε 'then'; μὲν (particle marking contrast); πρόπαν (neut. acc. of πρόπας) 'entire, whole'; ἦμαρ (neut. acc. sg.) 'day'; ἐς 'until'; ἠέλιον (acc. sg. of ἠέλιος) 'sun'; καταδύντα (aor. act. participle, acc. sg.) 'setting, going down.' The phrase describes feasting all day long until sunset.

lines.original: δαίνυντʼ, οὐδέ τι θυμὸς ἐδεύετο δαιτὸς ἐΐσης,
lines.english: "Wine-bibber," he cried, "with the face of a dog and the heart of a hind, you never dare to go out with the host in fight, nor yet with our chosen men in ambuscade. You shun this…
lines.gloss: δαίνυντο (3rd pl. impf. mid. of δαίνυμι) 'they feasted'; θυμός (nom. sg.) 'heart, spirit'; ἐδεύετο (3rd sg. impf. mid. of δεύομαι) 'lacked, wanted for'; δαιτός (gen. sg. of δαίς) 'feast, banquet'; ἐΐσης (gen. sg. fem. of ἐΐσης) 'equal, fair, well-shared.'

lines.original: οὐ μὲν φόρμιγγος περικαλλέος ἣν ἔχʼ Ἀπόλλων,
lines.english: rob his prizes from any man who contradicts you. You devour your people, for you are king over a feeble folk; otherwise, son of Atreus, henceforward you would insult no man.…
lines.gloss: φόρμιγγος (gen. sg. of φόρμιγξ) 'lyre, stringed instrument'; περικαλλέος (gen. sg. of περικαλλής) 'very beautiful, exceedingly lovely'; ἣν (acc. sg. relative pronoun) 'which'; ἔχʼ = ἔχε (impf. 3rd sg. of ἔχω) 'held, possessed.'

lines.original: Μουσάων θʼ αἳ ἄειδον ἀμειβόμεναι ὀπὶ καλῇ.
lines.english: rob his prizes from any man who contradicts you. You devour your people, for you are king over a feeble folk; otherwise, son of Atreus, henceforward you would insult no man.…
lines.gloss: Μουσάων (gen. pl. of Μοῦσα) 'of the Muses'; αἳ (nom. pl. fem. relative pronoun) 'who'; ἄειδον (impf. 3rd pl. of ἀείδω) 'were singing'; ἀμειβόμεναι (pres. mid. participle, nom. pl. fem.) 'answering one another, singing in turn'; ὀπὶ καλῇ (dat. sg.) 'with beautiful voice.'

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ κατέδυ λαμπρὸν φάος ἠελίοιο,
lines.english: rob his prizes from any man who contradicts you. You devour your people, for you are king over a feeble folk; otherwise, son of Atreus, henceforward you would insult no man.…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ 'but, and' (post-positive conjunction); ἐπεί 'when, after' (temporal conjunction); κατέδυ (3rd sg. aor. of καταδύω) 'sank down, set'; λαμπρόν (nom./acc. sg. neut. of λαμπρός) 'bright, shining'; φάος (nom./acc. sg. neut.) 'light'; ἠελίοιο (gen. sg. of ἠέλιος) 'of the sun'.

lines.original: οἳ μὲν κακκείοντες ἔβαν οἶκον δὲ ἕκαστος,
lines.english: rob his prizes from any man who contradicts you. You devour your people, for you are king over a feeble folk; otherwise, son of Atreus, henceforward you would insult no man.…
lines.gloss: κακκείοντες (pres. part. nom. pl. of κατακείω) 'lying down, going to bed'; ἔβαν (3rd pl. aor. of βαίνω) 'they went'; οἶκον (acc. sg.) 'to home'; ἕκαστος (nom. sg.) 'each one'. The line describes the gods retiring to their respective homes.

lines.original: ἧχι ἑκάστῳ δῶμα περικλυτὸς ἀμφιγυήεις
lines.english: rob his prizes from any man who contradicts you. You devour your people, for you are king over a feeble folk; otherwise, son of Atreus, henceforward you would insult no man.…
lines.gloss: ἧχι (adv.) 'where'; ἑκάστῳ (dat. sg.) 'for each one'; δῶμα (acc. sg. of δῶμα) 'house, dwelling'; περικλυτός (nom. sg.) 'very famous, renowned'; ἀμφιγυήεις (nom. sg.) 'lame in both feet, lame on both sides' (epithet of Hephaestus).

lines.original: Ἥφαιστος ποίησεν ἰδυίῃσι πραπίδεσσι·
lines.english: nor bud anew from the day on which it left its parent stem upon the mountains - for the axe stripped it of leaf and bark, and now the sons of the Achaeans bear it as judges and…
lines.gloss: Ἥφαιστος (nom. sg.) 'Hephaestus'; ποίησεν (aor. ind. act., 3rd sg. of ποιέω) 'made, fashioned'; ἰδυίῃσι (dat. pl. fem. of ἰδυῖα, perfect participle) 'skilled, knowing'; πραπίδεσσι (dat. pl. of πραπίδες) 'with his wits, with his cunning skill.'

lines.original: Ζεὺς δὲ πρὸς ὃν λέχος ἤϊʼ Ὀλύμπιος ἀστεροπητής,
lines.english: nor bud anew from the day on which it left its parent stem upon the mountains - for the axe stripped it of leaf and bark, and now the sons of the Achaeans bear it as judges and…
lines.gloss: Ζεύς (nom. sg.) 'Zeus'; πρός (prep. + acc.) 'to, toward'; ὃν λέχος (acc. sg. of ὅς + λέχος) 'his own bed'; ἤϊε (impf. of εἶμι) 'went, was going'; Ὀλύμπιος (nom. sg. adj.) 'Olympian'; ἀστεροπητής (nom. sg.) 'lightning-wielder, gatherer of clouds.'

lines.original: ἔνθα πάρος κοιμᾶθʼ ὅτε μιν γλυκὺς ὕπνος ἱκάνοι·
lines.english: nor bud anew from the day on which it left its parent stem upon the mountains - for the axe stripped it of leaf and bark, and now the sons of the Achaeans bear it as judges and…
lines.gloss: ἔνθα 'there, in that place'; πάρος (adv.) 'before, previously'; κοιμᾶθʼ (= κοιμᾶτο, imperf. mid./pass.) 'he would sleep, used to sleep'; ὅτε (conj.) 'whenever'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him'; γλυκύς (nom. sg.) 'sweet'; ὕπνος (nom. sg.) 'sleep'; ἱκάνοι (opt., 3rd sg. of ἱκάνω) 'would come upon, reach'.

lines.original: ἔνθα καθεῦδʼ ἀναβάς, παρὰ δὲ χρυσόθρονος Ἥρη.
lines.english: nor bud anew from the day on which it left its parent stem upon the mountains - for the axe stripped it of leaf and bark, and now the sons of the Achaeans bear it as judges and…
lines.gloss: ἔνθα 'there, in that place'; καθεῦδ(ε) (aor. imperative) 'sleep!'; ἀναβάς (aor. ptcp. nom. sg. masc. of ἀναβαίνω) 'having gone up, mounting'; παρά (adv.) 'beside, nearby'; χρυσόθρονος (nom. sg. fem.) 'golden-throned'; Ἥρη (nom. sg.) 'Hera'.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδαι τε καὶ ἄλλοι ἐϋκνήμιδες Ἀχαιοί,
lines.english: nor bud anew from the day on which it left its parent stem upon the mountains - for the axe stripped it of leaf and bark, and now the sons of the Achaeans bear it as judges and…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδαι (nom. pl. of Ἀτρεΐδης) 'sons of Atreus' (i.e., Agamemnon and Menelaus); ἐϋκνήμιδες (nom. pl. adj.) 'well-greaved,' epithet for warriors wearing shin armor; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'Achaeans,' the Greeks.

lines.original: ὑμῖν μὲν θεοὶ δοῖεν Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχοντες
lines.english: that hereafter they shall look fondly for Achilles and shall not find him. In the day of your distress, when your men fall dying by the murderous hand of Hektor, you shall not…
lines.gloss: ὑμῖν (dat. pl. of σύ) 'to you'; δοῖεν (3rd pl. aor. optative of δίδωμι) 'may they grant'; Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχοντες (nom. pl. pres. participle) 'dwelling in Olympian homes,' modifying θεοί; the optative expresses a wish.

lines.original: ἐκπέρσαι Πριάμοιο πόλιν, εὖ δʼ οἴκαδʼ ἱκέσθαι·
lines.english: that hereafter they shall look fondly for Achilles and shall not find him. In the day of your distress, when your men fall dying by the murderous hand of Hektor, you shall not…
lines.gloss: ἐκπέρσαι (aor. inf. of ἐκπέρθω) 'to sack, destroy utterly'; Πριάμοιο (gen. sg.) 'of Priam'; πόλιν (acc. sg.) 'city'; εὖ (adv.) 'safely, well'; οἴκαδε (adv.) 'homeward'; ἱκέσθαι (aor. inf. of ἱκνέομαι) 'to reach, arrive at'.

lines.original: παῖδα δʼ ἐμοὶ λύσαιτε φίλην, τὰ δʼ ἄποινα δέχεσθαι,
lines.english: that hereafter they shall look fondly for Achilles and shall not find him. In the day of your distress, when your men fall dying by the murderous hand of Hektor, you shall not…
lines.gloss: παῖδα (acc. sg. of παῖς) 'child, daughter'; λύσαιτε (aor. opt., 2nd pl. of λύω) 'release, ransom'; φίλην (acc. sg. fem. of φίλος) 'dear, beloved'; ἄποινα (acc. pl. neut. of ἄποινον) 'ransom, payment'; δέχεσθαι (pres. mid. inf. of δέχομαι) 'receive, accept'.

lines.original: ἁζόμενοι Διὸς υἱὸν ἑκηβόλον Ἀπόλλωνα.
lines.english: that hereafter they shall look fondly for Achilles and shall not find him. In the day of your distress, when your men fall dying by the murderous hand of Hektor, you shall not…
lines.gloss: ἁζόμενοι (pres. mid. participle, nom. pl.) 'revering, showing reverence to'; Διὸς υἱόν (acc. sg.) 'son of Zeus'; ἑκηβόλον (acc. sg. adj.) 'far-shooting, who strikes from afar'; Ἀπόλλωνα (acc. sg.) 'Apollo' — the participle modifies the implied subject 'you' (Achaeans), giving the reason for releasing Chryseis and accepting ransom.

lines.original: μή σε γέρον κοίλῃσιν ἐγὼ παρὰ νηυσὶ κιχείω
lines.english: that hereafter they shall look fondly for Achilles and shall not find him. In the day of your distress, when your men fall dying by the murderous hand of Hektor, you shall not…
lines.gloss: μή (with subjunctive) 'lest'; σε (acc. sg. of σύ) 'you'; γέρον (voc. sg. of γέρων) 'old man'; κοίλῃσιν (dat. pl. fem. of κοῖλος) 'hollow'; νηυσί (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships'; κιχείω (1st sg. aor. subjunctive of κιχάνω) 'I find, catch'.

lines.original: ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντʼ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα,
lines.english: With this the son of Peleus dashed his gold-bestudded scepter on the ground and took his seat, while the son of Atreus was beginning fiercely from his place upon the other side.…
lines.gloss: ἢ ... ἢ 'either ... or'; νῦν 'now'; δηθύνοντα (pres. part. acc. sg. masc. of δηθύνω) 'delaying, lingering'; ὕστερον 'later, afterwards'; αὖτις 'again, back again'; ἰόντα (pres. part. acc. sg. masc. of εἶμι) 'going, coming'.

lines.original: μή νύ τοι οὐ χραίσμῃ σκῆπτρον καὶ στέμμα θεοῖο·
lines.english: With this the son of Peleus dashed his gold-bestudded scepter on the ground and took his seat, while the son of Atreus was beginning fiercely from his place upon the other side.…
lines.gloss: μή νύ τοι (emphatic negative warning) 'lest not for you'; χραίσμῃ (aor. subj. of χραίσμω) 'avail, help, protect'; σκῆπτρον (nom. sg.) 'scepter, staff'; στέμμα (nom. sg.) 'fillet, woolen headband' (of the priest); θεοῖο (gen. sg. of θεός, epic form) 'of the god.'

lines.original: τὴν δʼ ἐγὼ οὐ λύσω· πρίν μιν καὶ γῆρας ἔπεισιν
lines.english: With this the son of Peleus dashed his gold-bestudded scepter on the ground and took his seat, while the son of Atreus was beginning fiercely from his place upon the other side.…
lines.gloss: τὴν (acc. sg. of ἡ, demonstrative) 'her'; λύσω (fut. 1st sg. of λύω) 'I will release'; πρίν 'before'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'her'; γῆρας (nom. sg.) 'old age'; ἔπεισιν (fut. 3rd sg. of ἔπειμι) 'will come upon, overtake.'

lines.original: ἡμετέρῳ ἐνὶ οἴκῳ ἐν Ἄργεϊ τηλόθι πάτρης
lines.english: With this the son of Peleus dashed his gold-bestudded scepter on the ground and took his seat, while the son of Atreus was beginning fiercely from his place upon the other side.…
lines.gloss: ἡμετέρῳ (dat. sg. of ἡμέτερος) 'our, my'; ἐνὶ (= ἐν, preposition + dat.) 'in'; οἴκῳ (dat. sg. of οἶκος) 'house, home'; Ἄργεϊ (dat. sg. of Ἄργος) 'Argos'; τηλόθι (adverb) 'far from'; πάτρης (gen. sg. of πάτρη) 'fatherland, native land'.

lines.original: ἱστὸν ἐποιχομένην καὶ ἐμὸν λέχος ἀντιόωσαν·
lines.english: With this the son of Peleus dashed his gold-bestudded scepter on the ground and took his seat, while the son of Atreus was beginning fiercely from his place upon the other side.…
lines.gloss: ἱστὸν (acc. sg. of ἱστός) 'loom, weaving'; ἐποιχομένην (pres. mid. participle, acc. sg. fem.) 'going to, tending, visiting'; λέχος (acc. sg. of λέχος) 'bed, couch'; ἀντιόωσαν (pres. participle, acc. sg. fem. of ἀντιάω) 'coming to meet, approaching'; both participles modify an implied feminine object, likely the woman going to her loom and approaching his bed.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἴθι μή μʼ ἐρέθιζε σαώτερος ὥς κε νέηαι.
lines.english: Two generations of men born and bred inhad passed away under his rule, and he was now reigning over the third. With all sincerity and goodwill, therefore, he addressed them thus:…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but'; ἴθι (pres. imperative of εἶμι) 'go!'; μή 'not' (with imperative = prohibition); ἐρέθιζε (pres. imperative) 'provoke, irritate'; σαώτερος (comparative adj., nom. sg.) 'safer, more unharmed'; ὥς κε νέηαι (2nd sg. pres. subj. of νέομαι with modal particle) 'so that you may return home.'

lines.original: κλῦθί μευ ἀργυρότοξʼ, ὃς Χρύσην ἀμφιβέβηκας
lines.english: Two generations of men born and bred inhad passed away under his rule, and he was now reigning over the third. With all sincerity and goodwill, therefore, he addressed them thus:…
lines.gloss: κλῦθί (aor. imperative, 2nd sg. of κλύω) 'hear!'; μευ (enclitic gen. of ἐγώ) 'of me, my'; ἀργυρότοξε (voc. sg. of ἀργυρότοξος) 'silver-bowed one'; ὅς (rel. pron., nom. sg. masc.) 'who'; Χρύσην (acc. sg.) 'Chryse' (a town); ἀμφιβέβηκας (perf. 2nd sg. of ἀμφιβαίνω) 'you stand over, protect, possess.'

lines.original: Κίλλαν τε ζαθέην Τενέδοιό τε ἶφι ἀνάσσεις,
lines.english: Two generations of men born and bred inhad passed away under his rule, and he was now reigning over the third. With all sincerity and goodwill, therefore, he addressed them thus:…
lines.gloss: Κίλλαν (acc. sg. of Κίλλα) 'Cilla,' a town in the Troad; ζαθέην (acc. sg. fem. of ζαθέος) 'holy, divine'; Τενέδοιό (gen. sg. of Τένεδος) 'of Tenedos,' an island near Troy; ἶφι (adv.) 'mightily, with strength'; ἀνάσσεις (2nd sg. pres. of ἀνάσσω) 'you rule over, are lord of.'

lines.original: Σμινθεῦ εἴ ποτέ τοι χαρίεντʼ ἐπὶ νηὸν ἔρεψα,
lines.english: Two generations of men born and bred inhad passed away under his rule, and he was now reigning over the third. With all sincerity and goodwill, therefore, he addressed them thus:…
lines.gloss: Σμινθεῦ (voc. sg.) epithet of Apollo, possibly 'mouse-god' or tied to a place name; εἴ ποτέ 'if ever'; χαρίεντα (acc. sg. neut. of χαρίεις) 'pleasing, graceful'; νηόν (acc. sg.) 'temple'; ἔρεψα (aor. of ἐρέφω) 'I roofed, built'.

lines.original: ἢ εἰ δή ποτέ τοι κατὰ πίονα μηρίʼ ἔκηα
lines.english: Two generations of men born and bred inhad passed away under his rule, and he was now reigning over the third. With all sincerity and goodwill, therefore, he addressed them thus:…
lines.gloss: ἤ 'or'; εἰ δή 'if indeed' (emphatic particle); κατά (tmesis with ἔκηα) 'down, upon' (here governing the burning); πίονα (acc. pl. neut. of πίων) 'fat, rich'; μηρία (acc. pl.) 'thigh-pieces' (the portions burned in sacrifice); ἔκηα (aor. of καίω) 'I burned'.

lines.original: ταύρων ἠδʼ αἰγῶν, τὸ δέ μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ·
lines.english: Surely Priam with his sons would rejoice, and the Trojans be glad at heart if they could hear this quarrel between you two, who are so excellent in fight and counsel. I am older…
lines.gloss: ταύρων (gen. pl. of ταῦρος) 'of bulls'; ἠδέ (conj.) 'and'; αἰγῶν (gen. pl. of αἴξ) 'of goats'; τό (acc. sg. neut. demonstrative) 'this'; κρήηνον (aor. imperative of κραίνω) 'fulfill, accomplish'; ἐέλδωρ (acc. sg. of ἔλδωρ) 'wish, desire.'

lines.original: τίσειαν Δαναοὶ ἐμὰ δάκρυα σοῖσι βέλεσσιν.
lines.english: Surely Priam with his sons would rejoice, and the Trojans be glad at heart if they could hear this quarrel between you two, who are so excellent in fight and counsel. I am older…
