lines.gloss: τίσειαν (3rd pl. aor. opt. of τίνω) 'may they avenge, requite'; Δαναοί (nom. pl.) 'the Danaans, Greeks'; ἐμὰ δάκρυα (acc. pl. of δάκρυ) 'my tears'; σοῖσι βέλεσσιν (dat. pl. of βέλος) 'with your arrows'.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδη νῦν ἄμμε παλιμπλαγχθέντας ὀΐω
lines.english: Surely Priam with his sons would rejoice, and the Trojans be glad at heart if they could hear this quarrel between you two, who are so excellent in fight and counsel. I am older…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδη (voc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (addressing Agamemnon); νῦν 'now'; ἄμμε (acc. pl., Ionic for ἡμᾶς) 'us'; παλιμπλαγχθέντας (aor. pass. ptc., acc. pl. masc.) 'driven back, wandering back'; ὀΐω (1st sg. pres., Ionic for οἴομαι) 'I think, I suppose'.

lines.original: ἂψ ἀπονοστήσειν, εἴ κεν θάνατόν γε φύγοιμεν,
lines.english: Surely Priam with his sons would rejoice, and the Trojans be glad at heart if they could hear this quarrel between you two, who are so excellent in fight and counsel. I am older…
lines.gloss: ἂψ 'back, homeward'; ἀπονοστήσειν (fut. inf. of ἀπονοστέω) 'to return home'; εἴ κεν introduces a conditional with subjunctive 'if perhaps'; θάνατόν (acc. sg.) 'death'; γε particle emphasizing the preceding word; φύγοιμεν (aor. opt. 1st pl. of φεύγω) 'we should escape, flee.'

lines.original: εἰ δὴ ὁμοῦ πόλεμός τε δαμᾷ καὶ λοιμὸς Ἀχαιούς·
lines.english: Surely Priam with his sons would rejoice, and the Trojans be glad at heart if they could hear this quarrel between you two, who are so excellent in fight and counsel. I am older…
lines.gloss: εἰ δή 'if indeed'; ὁμοῦ 'together, at once'; πόλεμός 'war' (nom. sg.); δαμᾷ (pres. indic. 3rd sg. of δαμάω) 'subdues, overcomes'; λοιμός 'plague, pestilence' (nom. sg.); Ἀχαιούς (acc. pl.) 'the Achaeans, Greeks.'

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγε δή τινα μάντιν ἐρείομεν ἢ ἱερῆα
lines.english: Moreover I have been the familiar friend of men even greater than you are, and they did not disregard my counsels. Never again can I behold such men as Peirithoos and Dryas…
lines.gloss: ἄγε (pres. imperative of ἄγω) 'come now, come!'; δή (particle) emphatic 'indeed, then'; τινα (acc. sg. of τις) 'some, a certain'; μάντιν (acc. sg. of μάντις) 'seer, prophet'; ἐρείομεν (1st pl. aor. subj. of ἐρέω/ἐρωτάω) 'let us ask, consult'; ἱερῆα (acc. sg. of ἱερεύς) 'priest'.

lines.original: ἢ καὶ ὀνειροπόλον, καὶ γάρ τʼ ὄναρ ἐκ Διός ἐστιν,
lines.english: Moreover I have been the familiar friend of men even greater than you are, and they did not disregard my counsels. Never again can I behold such men as Peirithoos and Dryas…
lines.gloss: ὀνειροπόλον (acc. sg. of ὀνειροπόλος) 'interpreter of dreams'; ὄναρ (nom./acc. sg. neut.) 'dream'; ἐκ Διός 'from Zeus' (gen. sg. of Ζεύς); the γάρ τε combination emphasizes the explanatory aside: 'for indeed a dream is from Zeus.'

lines.original: ὅς κʼ εἴποι ὅ τι τόσσον ἐχώσατο Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων,
lines.english: Moreover I have been the familiar friend of men even greater than you are, and they did not disregard my counsels. Never again can I behold such men as Peirithoos and Dryas…
lines.gloss: ὅς κʼ (= ὅς ἄν, relative pronoun with modal particle) 'whoever'; εἴποι (aor. opt. of εἶπον) 'might tell'; ὅ τι 'why' (interrogative); τόσσον (adverbial acc.) 'so much, so greatly'; ἐχώσατο (aor. mid. of χόω) 'grew angry, was angered'; Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων (nom. sg.) 'Phoebus Apollo.'

lines.original: εἴτʼ ἄρʼ ὅ γʼ εὐχωλῆς ἐπιμέμφεται ἠδʼ ἑκατόμβης,
lines.english: Moreover I have been the familiar friend of men even greater than you are, and they did not disregard my counsels. Never again can I behold such men as Peirithoos and Dryas…
lines.gloss: εἴτʼ (elided εἴτε, 'whether...or') introduces alternative; ἄρʼ (elided ἄρα, particle) marks transition; ὅ γʼ (= ὁ γε, 'he,' i.e., Apollo); εὐχωλῆς (gen. sg. of εὐχωλή) 'vow, prayer'; ἐπιμέμφεται (pres. mid. 3rd sg. of ἐπιμέμφομαι) 'finds fault with, blames for lack of'; ἠδʼ (elided ἠδέ, 'and/or'); ἑκατόμβης (gen. sg. of ἑκατόμβη)

lines.original: αἴ κέν πως ἀρνῶν κνίσης αἰγῶν τε τελείων
lines.english: Moreover I have been the familiar friend of men even greater than you are, and they did not disregard my counsels. Never again can I behold such men as Peirithoos and Dryas…
lines.gloss: αἴ κέν (with πως) 'if somehow, if perchance'; ἀρνῶν (gen. pl. of ἀρήν) 'of lambs'; κνίσης (gen. sg. of κνίση) 'savor, smoke of burnt fat'; αἰγῶν (gen. pl. of αἴξ) 'of goats'; τελείων (gen. pl. of τέλειος) 'full-grown, perfect (for sacrifice)'.

lines.original: βούλεται ἀντιάσας ἡμῖν ἀπὸ λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι.
lines.english: and Theseus son of Aegeus, peer of the immortals. These were the mightiest men ever born upon this earth: mightiest were they, and when they fought the fiercest tribes of mountain…
lines.gloss: βούλεται (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. indic. of βούλομαι) 'he wishes, is willing'; ἀντιάσας (aor. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc. of ἀντιάω) 'having encountered, faced'; ἡμῖν (dat. pl. of ἐγώ) 'from us, for us'; ἀπὸ (tmesis with ἀμῦναι) 'away'; λοιγὸν (acc. sg. of λοιγός) 'destruction, plague'; ἀμῦναι (aor. act. inf. of ἀμύνω) 'to ward off, defend against'.

lines.original: ὦ Ἀχιλεῦ κέλεαί με Διῒ φίλε μυθήσασθαι
lines.english: and Theseus son of Aegeus, peer of the immortals. These were the mightiest men ever born upon this earth: mightiest were they, and when they fought the fiercest tribes of mountain…
lines.gloss: ὦ Ἀχιλεῦ (voc. sg.) 'O Achilles'; κέλεαί (2nd sg. pres. indic. of κέλομαι) 'you bid, command'; με (acc. sg. of ἐγώ) 'me'; Διῒ φίλε (voc. sg. of Διὶ φίλος) 'dear to Zeus, beloved of Zeus'; μυθήσασθαι (aor. mid. inf. of μυθέομαι) 'to speak, relate, declare'.

lines.original: μῆνιν Ἀπόλλωνος ἑκατηβελέταο ἄνακτος·
lines.english: and Theseus son of Aegeus, peer of the immortals. These were the mightiest men ever born upon this earth: mightiest were they, and when they fought the fiercest tribes of mountain…
lines.gloss: μῆνιν (acc. sg. of μῆνις) 'wrath, anger'; Ἀπόλλωνος (gen. sg.) 'of Apollo'; ἑκατηβελέταο (gen. sg. epic form of ἑκατηβελέτης) 'the far-shooter'; ἄνακτος (gen. sg. of ἄναξ) 'lord, master' — the compound epithet emphasizes Apollo's power with the bow.

lines.original: τοὶ γὰρ ἐγὼν ἐρέω· σὺ δὲ σύνθεο καί μοι ὄμοσσον
lines.english: and Theseus son of Aegeus, peer of the immortals. These were the mightiest men ever born upon this earth: mightiest were they, and when they fought the fiercest tribes of mountain…
lines.gloss: τοὶ (dat. sg. of σύ, enclitic) 'to you'; ἐρέω (fut. 1st sg. of εἴρω) 'I will speak'; σύνθεο (2nd sg. aor. middle imperative of συντίθημι) 'consider, mark well'; ὄμοσσον (2nd sg. aor. imperative of ὄμνυμι) 'swear!'

lines.original: ἦ μέν μοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν·
lines.english: and Theseus son of Aegeus, peer of the immortals. These were the mightiest men ever born upon this earth: mightiest were they, and when they fought the fiercest tribes of mountain…
lines.gloss: ἦ μέν emphasizes the oath ('truly indeed'); πρόφρων (nom. sg. adj.) 'willing, ready, with goodwill'; ἔπεσιν (dat. pl. of ἔπος) 'with words'; χερσίν (dat. pl. of χείρ) 'with hands'; ἀρήξειν (fut. inf. of ἀρήγω) 'to help, assist' (complementing the oath).

lines.original: ἦ γὰρ ὀΐομαι ἄνδρα χολωσέμεν, ὃς μέγα πάντων
lines.english: for they would have me come, and I fought as it was in me to do. Not a man now living could withstand them, but they heard my words, and were persuaded by them. So be it also with…
lines.gloss: ὀΐομαι (1st sg. pres. mid.) 'I think, I suppose'; χολωσέμεν (aor. inf. of χολόω) 'to anger, enrage'; ὃς (nom. sg. relative pronoun) 'who'; μέγα πάντων (adverbial + gen. of comparison) 'mightiest of all, far above all'.

lines.original: Ἀργείων κρατέει καί οἱ πείθονται Ἀχαιοί·
lines.english: for they would have me come, and I fought as it was in me to do. Not a man now living could withstand them, but they heard my words, and were persuaded by them. So be it also with…
lines.gloss: Ἀργείων (gen. pl. of Ἀργεῖοι) 'of the Argives'; κρατέει (3rd sg. pres. of κρατέω) 'he rules over, has power over' (+ gen.); πείθονται (3rd pl. pres. middle of πείθω) 'they obey'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans.'

lines.original: κρείσσων γὰρ βασιλεὺς ὅτε χώσεται ἀνδρὶ χέρηϊ·
lines.english: for they would have me come, and I fought as it was in me to do. Not a man now living could withstand them, but they heard my words, and were persuaded by them. So be it also with…
lines.gloss: κρείσσων (comparative of κρατύς/ἀγαθός) 'stronger, more powerful'; βασιλεύς (nom. sg.) 'king'; ὅτε (temporal conjunction) 'when'; χώσεται (aor. subj. middle of χόομαι) 'grows angry'; ἀνδρί (dat. sg.) 'against a man'; χέρηϊ (dat. sg. of χείρων) 'inferior, lesser'.

lines.original: εἴ περ γάρ τε χόλον γε καὶ αὐτῆμαρ καταπέψῃ,
lines.english: for they would have me come, and I fought as it was in me to do. Not a man now living could withstand them, but they heard my words, and were persuaded by them. So be it also with…
lines.gloss: εἴ περ γάρ τε: combination of particles, "for even if"; χόλον (acc. sg. of χόλος) "anger, wrath"; γε: emphatic particle; αὐτῆμαρ (adv.) "on the very day, immediately"; καταπέψῃ (aor. subj. 3rd sg. of καταπέσσω) "he digests, swallows down, suppresses."

lines.original: ἀλλά τε καὶ μετόπισθεν ἔχει κότον, ὄφρα τελέσσῃ,
lines.english: for they would have me come, and I fought as it was in me to do. Not a man now living could withstand them, but they heard my words, and were persuaded by them. So be it also with…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, yet'; τε 'indeed' (particle); καὶ μετόπισθεν 'even afterward, later on'; ἔχει (3rd sg. pres.) 'he holds, keeps'; κότον (acc. sg. of κότος) 'grudge, resentment'; ὄφρα (conj.) 'until'; τελέσσῃ (3rd sg. aor. subj. of τελέω) 'he accomplishes, fulfills [it]'.

lines.original: ἐν στήθεσσιν ἑοῖσι· σὺ δὲ φράσαι εἴ με σαώσεις.
lines.english: Therefore, Agamemnon, though you be prestigious, take not this girl away, for the sons of the Achaeans have already given her to Achilles; and you, Achilles, strive not further…
lines.gloss: ἐν στήθεσσιν (dat. pl. of στῆθος) 'in the breast, in the heart'; ἑοῖσι (dat. pl. possessive adj.) 'his own'; φράσαι (aor. mid. imperative of φράζω) 'consider, think whether'; σαώσεις (fut. 2nd sg. of σαόω) 'you will save, protect'.

lines.original: θαρσήσας μάλα εἰπὲ θεοπρόπιον ὅ τι οἶσθα·
lines.english: Therefore, Agamemnon, though you be prestigious, take not this girl away, for the sons of the Achaeans have already given her to Achilles; and you, Achilles, strive not further…
lines.gloss: θαρσήσας (aor. participle of θαρσέω) 'having taken courage, emboldened'; μάλα (adv.) 'very much, utterly'; εἰπέ (aor. imperative of εἶπον) 'speak, tell'; θεοπρόπιον (acc. sg. of θεοπρόπιον) 'divine prophecy, oracle'; ὅ τι (relative pronoun, acc. neut.) 'whatever'; οἶσθα (perf. of οἶδα, functioning as present) 'you know'.

lines.original: οὐ μὰ γὰρ Ἀπόλλωνα Διῒ φίλον, ᾧ τε σὺ Κάλχαν
lines.english: Therefore, Agamemnon, though you be prestigious, take not this girl away, for the sons of the Achaeans have already given her to Achilles; and you, Achilles, strive not further…
lines.gloss: οὐ μὰ (emphatic negative oath) 'no, by…'; Ἀπόλλωνα (acc. sg.) 'Apollo' (object of oath); Διῒ (dat. sg. of Ζεύς) 'to Zeus, dear to Zeus'; φίλον (acc. sg. adj.) 'beloved, dear'; ᾧ (dat. sg. relative pronoun) 'to whom'; Κάλχαν (acc. sg.) 'Calchas' (vocative sense, the seer being addressed).

lines.original: εὐχόμενος Δαναοῖσι θεοπροπίας ἀναφαίνεις,
lines.english: Therefore, Agamemnon, though you be prestigious, take not this girl away, for the sons of the Achaeans have already given her to Achilles; and you, Achilles, strive not further…
lines.gloss: εὐχόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc.) 'praying, making prayers'; Δαναοῖσι (dat. pl. of Δαναοί) 'for/to the Danaans, Greeks'; θεοπροπίας (acc. pl. of θεοπροπία) 'prophecies, divine revelations'; ἀναφαίνεις (pres. act. ind., 2nd sg. of ἀναφαίνω) 'you reveal, bring to light'.

lines.original: οὔ τις ἐμεῦ ζῶντος καὶ ἐπὶ χθονὶ δερκομένοιο
lines.english: Therefore, Agamemnon, though you be prestigious, take not this girl away, for the sons of the Achaeans have already given her to Achilles; and you, Achilles, strive not further…
lines.gloss: οὔ τις 'no one'; ἐμεῦ (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'of me'; ζῶντος (gen. sg. pres. part. of ζάω) 'living'; ἐπὶ χθονί 'upon the earth' (χθονί dat. sg.); δερκομένοιο (gen. sg. pres. mid. part. of δέρκομαι) 'looking upon, seeing' — the phrase means 'while I live and look upon the earth.'

lines.original: σοὶ κοίλῃς παρὰ νηυσί βαρείας χεῖρας ἐποίσει
lines.english: You are strong, and have a goddess for your mother; but Agamemnon is more prestigious than you, for he has more people under him. Son of Atreus, check your anger, I implore you;…
lines.gloss: σοὶ (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to/upon you'; κοίλῃς (dat. pl. fem. of κοῖλος) 'hollow'; νηυσί (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships'; βαρείας (acc. pl. fem. of βαρύς) 'heavy, violent'; χεῖρας (acc. pl. of χείρ) 'hands'; ἐποίσει (fut. 3rd sg. of ἐπιφέρω) 'shall lay upon, bring against.'

lines.original: συμπάντων Δαναῶν, οὐδʼ ἢν Ἀγαμέμνονα εἴπῃς,
lines.english: You are strong, and have a goddess for your mother; but Agamemnon is more prestigious than you, for he has more people under him. Son of Atreus, check your anger, I implore you;…
lines.gloss: συμπάντων (gen. pl. of σύμπας) 'all together, all'; Δαναῶν (gen. pl. of Δαναοί) 'of the Danaans/Greeks'; οὐδέ 'not even'; ἤν (= ἐάν with subj.) 'if'; Ἀγαμέμνονα (acc. sg.) 'Agamemnon'; εἴπῃς (2nd sg. aor. subj. of εἶπον) 'you should say/mention'.

lines.original: ὃς νῦν πολλὸν ἄριστος Ἀχαιῶν εὔχεται εἶναι.
lines.english: You are strong, and have a goddess for your mother; but Agamemnon is more prestigious than you, for he has more people under him. Son of Atreus, check your anger, I implore you;…
lines.gloss: ὃς (relative pronoun, nom. sg.) 'who'; πολλὸν (acc. sg. neut., adverbial) 'by far, much'; ἄριστος (superlative adj., nom. sg. masc.) 'best, mightiest'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans'; εὔχεται (pres. mid./pass., 3rd sg.) 'boasts, claims'; εἶναι (pres. inf.) 'to be'.

lines.original: οὔ τʼ ἄρ ὅ γʼ εὐχωλῆς ἐπιμέμφεται οὐδʼ ἑκατόμβης,
lines.english: You are strong, and have a goddess for your mother; but Agamemnon is more prestigious than you, for he has more people under him. Son of Atreus, check your anger, I implore you;…
lines.gloss: οὔ τʼ ἄρ (negative particle + 'and indeed, and yet'); ὅ γʼ (demonstrative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) 'he' (Apollo); εὐχωλῆς (gen. sg. of εὐχωλή) 'prayer, vow'; ἐπιμέμφεται (pres. mid. of ἐπιμέμφομαι) 'finds fault with, blames for lack of'; οὐδʼ (οὐδέ) 'nor'; ἑκατόμβης (gen. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatomb, great sacrifice'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἕνεκʼ ἀρητῆρος ὃν ἠτίμησʼ Ἀγαμέμνων,
lines.english: You are strong, and have a goddess for your mother; but Agamemnon is more prestigious than you, for he has more people under him. Son of Atreus, check your anger, I implore you;…
lines.gloss: ἕνεκα (+ gen.) 'on account of, because of'; ἀρητῆρος (gen. sg. of ἀρητήρ) 'priest'; ὅν (relative pronoun, acc. sg. masc.) 'whom'; ἠτίμησε (aor. of ἀτιμάζω) 'dishonored, treated with dishonor'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) 'Agamemnon.'

lines.original: οὐδʼ ἀπέλυσε θύγατρα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεδέξατʼ ἄποινα,
lines.english: And Agamemnon answered, "Old sir, all that you have said is true, but this man wants to become our lord and master: he must be lord of all, king of all, and leader of all, and…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ 'nor, and not'; ἀπέλυσε (3rd sg. aor. of ἀπολύω) 'he released, set free'; θύγατρα (acc. sg. of θυγάτηρ) 'daughter'; καί 'and'; οὐκ ἀπεδέξατο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of ἀποδέχομαι) 'he accepted, received'; ἄποινα (acc. pl. neut. of ἄποινον) 'ransom, compensation.'

lines.original: τοὔνεκʼ ἄρʼ ἄλγεʼ ἔδωκεν ἑκηβόλος ἠδʼ ἔτι δώσει·
lines.english: And Agamemnon answered, "Old sir, all that you have said is true, but this man wants to become our lord and master: he must be lord of all, king of all, and leader of all, and…
lines.gloss: τοὔνεκα (crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα) 'for this reason, therefore'; ἄρα (particle) 'indeed, then'; ἄλγεα (acc. pl. of ἄλγος) 'pains, woes'; ἔδωκεν (aor. act. 3rd sg. of δίδωμι) 'gave, has given'; ἑκηβόλος (nom. sg.) 'far-shooter' (epithet of Apollo); ἠδέ 'and'; ἔτι (adv.) 'still, yet'; δώσει (fut. act. 3rd sg. of δίδωμι) 'will give'.

lines.original: οὐδʼ ὅ γε πρὶν Δαναοῖσιν ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἀπώσει
lines.english: And Agamemnon answered, "Old sir, all that you have said is true, but this man wants to become our lord and master: he must be lord of all, king of all, and leader of all, and…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ 'nor, and not'; ὅ γε 'he' (i.e., Apollo); πρίν 'before'; Δαναοῖσιν (dat. pl. of Δαναοί) 'for/from the Danaans'; ἀεικέα (acc. sg. of ἀεικής) 'shameful, ugly'; λοιγόν (acc. sg. of λοιγός) 'plague, destruction'; ἀπώσει (fut. of ἀπωθέω) 'he will drive away, remove.'

lines.original: πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πατρὶ φίλῳ δόμεναι ἑλικώπιδα κούρην
lines.english: And Agamemnon answered, "Old sir, all that you have said is true, but this man wants to become our lord and master: he must be lord of all, king of all, and leader of all, and…
lines.gloss: πρίν (adv.) 'before, until'; ἀπὸ with dative 'to, back to'; πατρί (dat. sg. of πατήρ) 'father'; φίλῳ (dat. sg. of φίλος) 'dear, own'; δόμεναι (aor. inf. of δίδωμι) 'to give'; ἑλικώπιδα (acc. sg. of ἑλικῶπις) 'with rolling/flashing eyes' (epithet); κούρην (acc. sg. of κούρη) 'maiden, girl'.

lines.original: ἀπριάτην ἀνάποινον, ἄγειν θʼ ἱερὴν ἑκατόμβην
lines.english: And Agamemnon answered, "Old sir, all that you have said is true, but this man wants to become our lord and master: he must be lord of all, king of all, and leader of all, and…
lines.gloss: ἀπριάτην (acc. sg. fem. of ἀπρίατος) 'without price, without ransom'; ἀνάποινον (acc. sg. fem. of ἀνάποινος) 'without recompense'; ἄγειν (pres. inf.) 'to bring, lead'; θʼ = τε (enclitic particle) 'and'; ἱερήν (acc. sg. fem. of ἱερός) 'sacred, holy'; ἑκατόμβην (acc. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatomb, sacrifice of one hundred oxen.'

lines.original: ἐς Χρύσην· τότε κέν μιν ἱλασσάμενοι πεπίθοιμεν.
lines.english: Granted that the gods have made him a great warrior, have they also given him the right to speak with railing?" Achilles in turn said to him: "I should be a mean coward," he…
lines.gloss: ἐς Χρύσην 'to Chryse' (acc. sg., town of the priest Chryses); τότε 'then'; κέν (= ἄν) modal particle with opt.; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him' (Apollo); ἱλασσάμενοι (aor. mid. ptc. nom. pl.) 'having propitiated, appeased'; πεπίθοιμεν (aor. opt. 1st pl. of πείθω) 'we might persuade, win over'.

lines.original: μάντι κακῶν οὐ πώ ποτέ μοι τὸ κρήγυον εἶπας·
lines.english: Granted that the gods have made him a great warrior, have they also given him the right to speak with railing?" Achilles in turn said to him: "I should be a mean coward," he…
lines.gloss: μάντι (voc. sg. of μάντις) 'seer, prophet'; κακῶν (gen. pl. of κακός) 'of evils, bad things'; οὐ πώ ποτέ 'not ever yet, never'; κρήγυον (neut. acc. sg. of κρήγυος) 'good thing, favorable matter'; εἶπας (2nd sg. aor. of εἶπον) 'you said, you have spoken'.

lines.original: αἰεί τοι τὰ κάκʼ ἐστὶ φίλα φρεσὶ μαντεύεσθαι,
lines.english: Granted that the gods have made him a great warrior, have they also given him the right to speak with railing?" Achilles in turn said to him: "I should be a mean coward," he…
lines.gloss: αἰεί 'always, ever'; τοι (ethical dative) 'to you, for you'; τὰ κάκʼ (neut. pl. nom., crasis for τὰ κακά) 'evil things, troubles'; φίλα (neut. pl. nom.) 'dear, pleasing'; φρεσί (dat. pl. of φρήν) 'in your mind/heart'; μαντεύεσθαι (pres. mid. inf.) 'to prophesy, divine'.

lines.original: ἐσθλὸν δʼ οὔτέ τί πω εἶπας ἔπος οὔτʼ ἐτέλεσσας·
lines.english: Granted that the gods have made him a great warrior, have they also given him the right to speak with railing?" Achilles in turn said to him: "I should be a mean coward," he…
lines.gloss: ἐσθλὸν (acc. sg. neut. of ἐσθλός) 'good, noble'; οὔτέ τί πω 'not yet ever at all' (intensive negation with enclitic πω); εἶπας (aor. of εἶπον) 'you said'; ἔπος (acc. sg.) 'word, utterance'; ἐτέλεσσας (aor. of τελέω) 'you accomplished, brought to pass.'

lines.original: καὶ νῦν ἐν Δαναοῖσι θεοπροπέων ἀγορεύεις
lines.english: Granted that the gods have made him a great warrior, have they also given him the right to speak with railing?" Achilles in turn said to him: "I should be a mean coward," he…
lines.gloss: νῦν (adv.) 'now'; Δαναοῖσι (dat. pl. of Δαναοί) 'among the Danaans/Greeks'; θεοπροπέων (pres. part. nom. sg. of θεοπροπέω) 'prophesying, speaking as a prophet'; ἀγορεύεις (pres. 2nd sg. of ἀγορεύω) 'you proclaim, you speak publicly'.

lines.original: ὡς δὴ τοῦδʼ ἕνεκά σφιν ἑκηβόλος ἄλγεα τεύχει,
lines.english: Order other people about, not me, for I shall obey no longer. Furthermore I say - and lay my saying to your heart - I shall fight neither you nor any man about this girl, for…
lines.gloss: ὡς (adv.) 'how, that'; δή (particle) 'indeed, certainly' (emphasizing); τοῦδʼ ἕνεκα (gen. sg. demonstrative + postposition) 'for the sake of this, because of this'; σφιν (dat. pl. pronoun) 'for them'; ἑκηβόλος (nom. sg., epithet) 'far-shooter' (Apollo); ἄλγεα (acc. pl. of ἄλγος) 'pains, woes'; τεύχει (pres. ind. 3rd sg. of τεύχω) 'fashions, brings about'.

lines.original: οὕνεκʼ ἐγὼ κούρης Χρυσηΐδος ἀγλάʼ ἄποινα
lines.english: Order other people about, not me, for I shall obey no longer. Furthermore I say - and lay my saying to your heart - I shall fight neither you nor any man about this girl, for…
lines.gloss: οὕνεκα (contr. of οὗ ἕνεκα) 'because, for the reason that'; κούρης (gen. sg. of κούρη) 'of the girl, maiden'; Χρυσηΐδος (gen. sg.) 'of Chryseis' (the girl's name); ἀγλάʼ (= ἀγλαά, neut. pl. acc. of ἀγλαός) 'splendid, glorious'; ἄποινα (neut. pl. acc. of ἄποινον) 'ransom, compensation'.

lines.original: οὐκ ἔθελον δέξασθαι, ἐπεὶ πολὺ βούλομαι αὐτὴν
lines.english: Order other people about, not me, for I shall obey no longer. Furthermore I say - and lay my saying to your heart - I shall fight neither you nor any man about this girl, for…
lines.gloss: οὐκ ἔθελον (1st sg. impf. of ἐθέλω) 'I was not willing'; δέξασθαι (aor. inf. middle of δέχομαι) 'to accept, receive'; ἐπεί (conj.) 'since, because'; πολύ (adv. acc.) 'much, greatly'; βούλομαι (1st sg. pres. mid.) 'I prefer, wish'; αὐτήν (acc. sg. fem. of αὐτός) 'her' (referring to Chryseis).

lines.original: οἴκοι ἔχειν· καὶ γάρ ῥα Κλυταιμνήστρης προβέβουλα
lines.english: Order other people about, not me, for I shall obey no longer. Furthermore I say - and lay my saying to your heart - I shall fight neither you nor any man about this girl, for…
lines.gloss: οἴκοι (adverbial) 'at home'; ἔχειν (pres. inf.) 'to have, keep'; γάρ ῥα (particles) 'for indeed'; Κλυταιμνήστρης (gen. sg.) 'of Clytemnestra' (Agamemnon's wife); προβέβουλα (perf. 1st sg. of προβούλομαι) 'I prefer (her) before.'

lines.original: κουριδίης ἀλόχου, ἐπεὶ οὔ ἑθέν ἐστι χερείων,
lines.english: Order other people about, not me, for I shall obey no longer. Furthermore I say - and lay my saying to your heart - I shall fight neither you nor any man about this girl, for…
lines.gloss: κουριδίης (gen. sg. of κουρίδιος) 'wedded, lawful'; ἀλόχου (gen. sg. of ἄλοχος) 'wife'; ἐπεί 'since'; οὔ (negative adv.) 'not'; ἑθέν (dialectal gen. sg. pronoun) 'than her'; ἐστι (3rd sg. pres. of εἰμί) 'is'; χερείων (comparative adj., nom. sg. fem.) 'worse, inferior'.

lines.original: οὐ δέμας οὐδὲ φυήν, οὔτʼ ἂρ φρένας οὔτέ τι ἔργα.
lines.english: But of all else that is at my ship you shall carry away nothing by force. Try, that others may see; if you do, my spear shall be reddened with your blood." When they had quarreled…
lines.gloss: δέμας (acc. sg. neut.) 'body, stature'; φυήν (acc. sg. of φυή) 'form, appearance'; φρένας (acc. pl. of φρήν) 'mind, wits'; ἔργα (acc. pl. neut. of ἔργον) 'deeds, accomplishments'. The repeated negatives (οὐ...οὐδέ...οὔτε...οὔτε) emphasize "in no respect—not in body, nor in form, nor in mind, nor in deeds."

lines.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ ὧς ἐθέλω δόμεναι πάλιν εἰ τό γʼ ἄμεινον·
lines.english: But of all else that is at my ship you shall carry away nothing by force. Try, that others may see; if you do, my spear shall be reddened with your blood." When they had quarreled…
lines.gloss: ἀλλὰ 'but, yet'; καὶ ὧς 'even so, nevertheless'; ἐθέλω (1st sg. pres.) 'I am willing, I wish'; δόμεναι (aor. inf. of δίδωμι) 'to give (back)'; πάλιν 'back, again'; εἰ 'if'; τό... ἄμεινον (neut. nom./acc. sg. of ἀμείνων) 'the better (course)', with γε (enclitic particle) 'at least, indeed'.

lines.original: βούλομʼ ἐγὼ λαὸν σῶν ἔμμεναι ἢ ἀπολέσθαι·
lines.english: But of all else that is at my ship you shall carry away nothing by force. Try, that others may see; if you do, my spear shall be reddened with your blood." When they had quarreled…
lines.gloss: βούλομαι (1st sg. pres. mid.) 'I wish, desire'; ἐγώ 'I' (emphatic); λαός (gen. sg.) 'of the host, army'; σῶν (gen. sg. of σός) 'your' or possibly corrupt for Ἀχαιῶν 'of the Achaeans'; ἔμμεναι (pres. inf. of εἰμί) 'to be'; ἄνευ 'without' (implied); γέρας 'prize'; ἀπολέσθαι (aor. inf. mid. of ἀπόλλυμι) 'to lose, be deprived of'.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐμοὶ γέρας αὐτίχʼ ἑτοιμάσατʼ ὄφρα μὴ οἶος
lines.english: But of all else that is at my ship you shall carry away nothing by force. Try, that others may see; if you do, my spear shall be reddened with your blood." When they had quarreled…
lines.gloss: αὐτάρ 'but, now'; ἐμοί (dat. sg.) 'for me'; γέρας (acc. sg.) 'prize, honor-gift'; αὐτίχα 'at once, immediately'; ἑτοιμάσατε (2nd pl. aor. imperative of ἑτοιμάζω) 'prepare!'; ὄφρα 'so that'; μή 'not'; οἶος (nom. sg. masc. of οἶος) 'alone, only one'.

lines.original: Ἀργείων ἀγέραστος ἔω, ἐπεὶ οὐδὲ ἔοικε·
lines.english: But of all else that is at my ship you shall carry away nothing by force. Try, that others may see; if you do, my spear shall be reddened with your blood." When they had quarreled…
lines.gloss: Ἀργείων (gen. pl. of Ἀργεῖοι) 'of the Argives'; ἀγέραστος (nom. sg. adj.) 'without honor/prize, unrewarded'; ἔω (pres. subj. 1st sg. of εἰμί) 'I be, I am'; ἐπεὶ οὐδὲ ἔοικε 'since it is not fitting/proper' (ἔοικε 3rd sg. perf. of ἔοικα, used impersonally).

lines.original: λεύσσετε γὰρ τό γε πάντες ὅ μοι γέρας ἔρχεται ἄλλῃ.
lines.english: they rose, and broke up the assembly at the ships of the Achaeans. The son of Peleus went back to his tents and ships with the son of Menoitios and his company, while Agamemnon…
lines.gloss: λεύσσετε (2nd pl. pres. indic. of λεύσσω) 'see, behold'; γάρ 'for'; τό γε 'this indeed' (neut. acc. sg. article + particle); πάντες (nom. pl. masc. of πᾶς) 'all of you'; ὅ (neut. nom./acc. sg. relative pronoun) 'which'; μοι (dat. sg. of ἐγώ) 'my, to me'; γέρας (nom./acc. sg. neut.) 'prize, gift of honor'; ἔρχεται (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass.) 'goes, is going'; ἄλλῃ (dat. sg. fem. of ἄλ

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδη κύδιστε φιλοκτεανώτατε πάντων,
lines.english: they rose, and broke up the assembly at the ships of the Achaeans. The son of Peleus went back to his tents and ships with the son of Menoitios and his company, while Agamemnon…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδη (voc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (addressing Agamemnon); κύδιστε (voc. sg. superl. of κυδρός) 'most glorious'; φιλοκτεανώτατε (voc. sg. superl. of φιλοκτεάνων) 'most greedy, most covetous'; πάντων (gen. pl.) 'of all'.

lines.original: πῶς γάρ τοι δώσουσι γέρας μεγάθυμοι Ἀχαιοί;
lines.english: they rose, and broke up the assembly at the ships of the Achaeans. The son of Peleus went back to his tents and ships with the son of Menoitios and his company, while Agamemnon…
lines.gloss: πῶς 'how?'; γάρ (explanatory particle) 'for'; τοι (ethical dative, second person singular) 'for you'; δώσουσι (fut. 3rd pl. of δίδωμι) 'will give'; γέρας (acc. sg. neut.) 'prize of honor, gift'; μεγάθυμοι (nom. pl. masc. adj.) 'great-hearted, proud-spirited'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans.'

lines.original: οὐδέ τί που ἴδμεν ξυνήϊα κείμενα πολλά·
lines.english: they rose, and broke up the assembly at the ships of the Achaeans. The son of Peleus went back to his tents and ships with the son of Menoitios and his company, while Agamemnon…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ 'nor, and not'; τί που 'in any way, at all' (που is an enclitic particle adding vagueness); ἴδμεν (perf. with pres. meaning, 1st pl.) 'we have seen, we know'; ξυνήϊα (neut. pl. acc., epic for συνηϊα) 'gathered together, collected'; κείμενα (perf. mid. participle) 'lying, stored up'; πολλά (adverbial acc.) 'in abundance, in many places'.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ τὰ μὲν πολίων ἐξεπράθομεν, τὰ δέδασται,
lines.english: He escorted Chryseis on board and sent moreover a hecatomb for the god. And Odysseus went as leader. These, then, went on board and sailed their ways over the sea. But the son of…
lines.gloss: ἐξεπράθομεν (1st pl. aor. of ἐκπέρθω) 'we sacked, plundered utterly'; δέδασται (3rd sg. perf. mid./pass. of δατέομαι) 'has been divided, distributed'; πολίων (gen. pl. of πόλις) 'of cities'; τὰ μὲν ... τὰ (neut. pl. article) 'the things on one hand ... the things' (correlative structure).

lines.original: λαοὺς δʼ οὐκ ἐπέοικε παλίλλογα ταῦτʼ ἐπαγείρειν.
lines.english: He escorted Chryseis on board and sent moreover a hecatomb for the god. And Odysseus went as leader. These, then, went on board and sailed their ways over the sea. But the son of…
lines.gloss: λαοὺς (acc. pl. of λαός) 'the people, troops'; οὐκ ἐπέοικε (3rd sg. perf. of ἐπέοικα) 'it is not fitting, seemly'; παλίλλογα (neut. acc. pl. adj.) 'gathered back again, recollected'; ταῦτα (demonstrative, acc. pl. neut.) 'these things'; ἐπαγείρειν (pres. inf. of ἐπαγείρω) 'to gather together, collect.'

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σὺ μὲν νῦν τήνδε θεῷ πρόες· αὐτὰρ Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: He escorted Chryseis on board and sent moreover a hecatomb for the god. And Odysseus went as leader. These, then, went on board and sailed their ways over the sea. But the son of…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but'; σύ (nom. sg.) 'you' (emphatic); μέν (particle) balancing αὐτάρ; νῦν 'now'; τήνδε (acc. sg. fem. of ὅδε) 'this one/this woman'; θεῷ (dat. sg.) 'to the god'; πρόες (2nd sg. aor. imperative of προΐημι) 'send forth, let go'; αὐτάρ 'but, and'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans'.

lines.original: τριπλῇ τετραπλῇ τʼ ἀποτείσομεν, αἴ κέ ποθι Ζεὺς
lines.english: He escorted Chryseis on board and sent moreover a hecatomb for the god. And Odysseus went as leader. These, then, went on board and sailed their ways over the sea. But the son of…
lines.gloss: τριπλῇ and τετραπλῇ (adverbial datives) 'threefold, fourfold'; ἀποτείσομεν (fut. 1st pl. of ἀποτίνω) 'we shall repay'; αἴ κέ (= ἐάν) 'if ever'; ποθι (enclitic adv.) 'at some time'; Ζεύς (nom. sg.) 'Zeus' (subject of the conditional clause).

lines.original: δῷσι πόλιν Τροίην εὐτείχεον ἐξαλαπάξαι.
lines.english: He escorted Chryseis on board and sent moreover a hecatomb for the god. And Odysseus went as leader. These, then, went on board and sailed their ways over the sea. But the son of…
lines.gloss: δῷσι (3rd sg. aor. subj. of δίδωμι) 'may grant, may give'; πόλιν (acc. sg. of πόλις) 'city'; εὐτείχεον (acc. sg. fem. of εὐτείχης) 'well-walled'; ἐξαλαπάξαι (aor. inf. of ἐξαλαπάζω) 'to sack utterly, to destroy completely.'

lines.original: μὴ δʼ οὕτως ἀγαθός περ ἐὼν θεοείκελʼ Ἀχιλλεῦ
lines.english: Then they offered hecatombs of bulls and goats without blemish on the sea-shore, and the smoke with the savor of their sacrifice rose curling up towards heaven. Thus did they busy…
lines.gloss: μή (negative particle with imperative force) 'do not'; οὕτως (adv.) 'in this way, thus'; ἀγαθός περ (nom. sg. masc. with concessive περ) 'though brave/noble'; ἐών (pres. participle of εἰμί, nom. sg. masc.) 'being'; θεοείκελε (voc. sg. of θεοείκελος) 'godlike'; Ἀχιλλεῦ (voc. sg.) 'Achilles.'

lines.original: κλέπτε νόῳ, ἐπεὶ οὐ παρελεύσεαι οὐδέ με πείσεις.
lines.english: Then they offered hecatombs of bulls and goats without blemish on the sea-shore, and the smoke with the savor of their sacrifice rose curling up towards heaven. Thus did they busy…
lines.gloss: κλέπτε (pres. imperative of κλέπτω) 'deceive, cheat'; νόῳ (dat. sg. of νόος) 'by cunning, by craft'; παρελεύσεαι (fut. 2nd sg. of παρέρχομαι) 'you will get past, you will elude'; πείσεις (fut. 2nd sg. of πείθω) 'you will persuade'.

lines.original: ἦ ἐθέλεις ὄφρʼ αὐτὸς ἔχῃς γέρας, αὐτὰρ ἔμʼ αὔτως
lines.english: Then they offered hecatombs of bulls and goats without blemish on the sea-shore, and the smoke with the savor of their sacrifice rose curling up towards heaven. Thus did they busy…
lines.gloss: ἦ (interrogative particle) 'truly? really?'; ὄφρα (conj.) 'so that, in order that'; αὐτός (nom. sg.) 'you yourself' (emphatic); ἔχῃς (pres. subj. 2nd sg. of ἔχω) 'may have'; γέρας (acc. sg.) 'prize, honor-gift'; αὐτάρ (conj.) 'but, whereas'; ἔμε (acc. sg. of ἐγώ) 'me'; αὔτως (adv.) 'thus, in vain, without recompense.'

lines.original: ἧσθαι δευόμενον, κέλεαι δέ με τήνδʼ ἀποδοῦναι;
lines.english: Then they offered hecatombs of bulls and goats without blemish on the sea-shore, and the smoke with the savor of their sacrifice rose curling up towards heaven. Thus did they busy…
lines.gloss: ἧσθαι (pres. inf. of ἧμαι) 'to sit, remain'; δευόμενον (pres. part. acc. sg. masc. of δέομαι) 'lacking, being in need'; κέλεαι (2nd sg. pres. of κέλομαι) 'you bid, command'; τήνδʼ = τήνδε (acc. sg. fem. demonstrative) 'this one' (referring to Chryseis); ἀποδοῦναι (aor. inf. of ἀποδίδωμι) 'to give back, restore.'

lines.original: ἀλλʼ εἰ μὲν δώσουσι γέρας μεγάθυμοι Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: Then they offered hecatombs of bulls and goats without blemish on the sea-shore, and the smoke with the savor of their sacrifice rose curling up towards heaven. Thus did they busy…
lines.gloss: ἀλλʼ = ἀλλά (adversative conjunction) 'but'; εἰ μέν (conditional particle with μέν answering δέ) 'if indeed'; δώσουσι (fut. indic. 3rd pl. of δίδωμι) 'they will give'; γέρας (acc. sg. neut.) 'prize, gift of honor'; μεγάθυμοι (nom. pl. masc. adj.) 'great-hearted, magnanimous'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans, Greeks.'

lines.original: ἄρσαντες κατὰ θυμὸν ὅπως ἀντάξιον ἔσται·
lines.english: and called his trusty messengers and squires [] Talthybios and Eurybates. "Go," said he, "to the tent of Achilles, son of Peleus; take Briseis by the hand and bring her hither; if…
lines.gloss: ἄρσαντες (aor. part. nom. pl. of ἀραρίσκω/ἀείρω) 'fitting (it), making (it) suitable'; κατὰ θυμόν (prepositional phrase) 'according to (their) heart/spirit,' i.e., 'to (their) liking'; ὅπως (adv.) 'so that, in order that'; ἀντάξιον (adj. nom./acc. sg. neut.) 'worthy in exchange, of equivalent value'; ἔσται (fut. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) 'it will be.'

lines.original: εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι
lines.english: and called his trusty messengers and squires [] Talthybios and Eurybates. "Go," said he, "to the tent of Achilles, son of Peleus; take Briseis by the hand and bring her hither; if…
lines.gloss: εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν: "if they do not give" (δώωσιν = 3rd pl. subj. aor. of δίδωμι, with κε = ἄν); ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι: "I myself will take" (ἕλωμαι = 1st sg. aor. mid. subj. of αἱρέω, with emphatic αὐτός).

lines.original: ἢ τεὸν ἢ Αἴαντος ἰὼν γέρας, ἢ Ὀδυσῆος
lines.english: and called his trusty messengers and squires [] Talthybios and Eurybates. "Go," said he, "to the tent of Achilles, son of Peleus; take Briseis by the hand and bring her hither; if…
lines.gloss: ἤ 'either' (disjunctive conjunction introducing alternatives); τεόν (possessive adj., acc. sg. neut.) 'your, yours'; Αἴαντος (gen. sg.) 'of Ajax'; ἰών (pres. part. of εἶμι) 'going'; γέρας (acc. sg.) 'prize, honor-gift'; Ὀδυσῆος (gen. sg.) 'of Odysseus'. Agamemnon threatens to seize the prize of Achilles, Ajax, or Odysseus.

lines.original: ἄξω ἑλών· ὃ δέ κεν κεχολώσεται ὅν κεν ἵκωμαι.
lines.english: and called his trusty messengers and squires [] Talthybios and Eurybates. "Go," said he, "to the tent of Achilles, son of Peleus; take Briseis by the hand and bring her hither; if…
lines.gloss: ἄξω (fut. of ἄγω) 'I will lead away, carry off'; ἑλών (aor. part. of αἱρέω) 'having taken, seizing'; ὃ δέ 'and he'; κεν (= ἄν, modal particle with subj.); κεχολώσεται (fut. perf. of χολόω) 'will be angered'; ὅν κεν ἵκωμαι (aor. subj. of ἱκνέομαι) 'whomever I come to, approach' — note the indefinite relative construction with κεν/ἄν.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἤτοι μὲν ταῦτα μεταφρασόμεσθα καὶ αὖτις,
lines.english: and called his trusty messengers and squires [] Talthybios and Eurybates. "Go," said he, "to the tent of Achilles, son of Peleus; take Briseis by the hand and bring her hither; if…
lines.gloss: ἤτοι (particle) 'truly, surely'; μέν...καὶ αὖτις 'on the one hand...and later/again'; ταῦτα (acc. pl. neut. of οὗτος) 'these things'; μεταφρασόμεσθα (fut. 1st pl. mid. of μεταφράζομαι) 'we shall consider, ponder later'.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ἄγε νῆα μέλαιναν ἐρύσσομεν εἰς ἅλα δῖαν,
lines.english: with others and take her - which will press him harder." He charged them straightly further and dismissed them, whereon they went their way sorrowfully by the seaside, till they…
lines.gloss: νῦν (adv.) 'now'; ἄγε (pres. imperative of ἄγω) 'come!', used as an interjection to urge action; νῆα (acc. sg. of ναῦς) 'ship'; μέλαιναν (acc. sg. fem. of μέλας) 'black, dark'; ἐρύσσομεν (aor. subjunctive, 1st pl. of ἐρύω) 'let us drag, haul'; εἰς (prep. + acc.) 'into'; ἅλα (acc. sg. of ἅλς) 'sea'; δῖαν (acc. sg. fem. of δῖος) 'bright, shining, divine'.

lines.original: ἐν δʼ ἐρέτας ἐπιτηδὲς ἀγείρομεν, ἐς δʼ ἑκατόμβην
lines.english: with others and take her - which will press him harder." He charged them straightly further and dismissed them, whereon they went their way sorrowfully by the seaside, till they…
lines.gloss: ἐν δέ 'and in (it)'; ἐρέτας (acc. pl. of ἐρέτης) 'rowers, oarsmen'; ἐπιτηδές (adv.) 'suitably, in due order'; ἀγείρομεν (1st pl. pres. subj. of ἀγείρω) 'let us gather, collect'; ἐς δέ 'and into (it)'; ἑκατόμβην (acc. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatomb, sacrifice of animals.'

lines.original: θείομεν, ἂν δʼ αὐτὴν Χρυσηΐδα καλλιπάρῃον
lines.english: with others and take her - which will press him harder." He charged them straightly further and dismissed them, whereon they went their way sorrowfully by the seaside, till they…
lines.gloss: θείομεν (1st pl. pres. subjunctive of τίθημι) 'let us place, put'; ἂν (= ἐν, with crasis) 'in, on'; αὐτήν (acc. sg. fem. pronoun, intensive) 'herself'; Χρυσηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Chryseis' (daughter of Chryses); καλλιπάρῃον (acc. sg. fem. of καλλιπάρῃος) 'fair-cheeked, beautiful-cheeked.'

lines.original: βήσομεν· εἷς δέ τις ἀρχὸς ἀνὴρ βουληφόρος ἔστω,
lines.english: with others and take her - which will press him harder." He charged them straightly further and dismissed them, whereon they went their way sorrowfully by the seaside, till they…
lines.gloss: βήσομεν (1st pl. fut. of βαίνω) 'we shall go'; εἷς (nom. sg. masc. of εἷς) 'one'; ἀρχός (nom. sg.) 'leader, chief'; ἀνήρ (nom. sg.) 'man'; βουληφόρος (nom. sg. adj.) 'counselor, advisor' (lit. 'bearing counsel'); ἔστω (3rd sg. pres. imperative of εἰμί) 'let him be.'

lines.original: ἢ Αἴας ἢ Ἰδομενεὺς ἢ δῖος Ὀδυσσεὺς
lines.english: with others and take her - which will press him harder." He charged them straightly further and dismissed them, whereon they went their way sorrowfully by the seaside, till they…
lines.gloss: ἤ (disjunctive conjunction) 'or'; Αἴας (nom. sg.) 'Ajax'; Ἰδομενεύς (nom. sg.) 'Idomeneus' (king of Crete); δῖος (nom. sg. m. adj.) 'godlike, noble'; Ὀδυσσεύς (nom. sg.) 'Odysseus' — three heroes named as possible leaders for the embassy.

lines.original: ἠὲ σὺ Πηλεΐδη πάντων ἐκπαγλότατʼ ἀνδρῶν,
lines.english: and ill-pleased he was when he beheld them. They stood fearfully and reverently before him, and never a word did they speak, but he knew them and said, "Welcome, heralds,…
lines.gloss: ἠὲ (or) 'or'; σὺ (nom. sg.) 'you'; Πηλεΐδη (voc. sg. of Πηλείδης) 'son of Peleus' (i.e., Achilles); πάντων ἀνδρῶν (gen. pl.) 'of all men'; ἐκπαγλότατʼ (superl. voc. sg. of ἐκπάγλος, elided) 'most terrifying, most formidable'.

lines.original: ὄφρʼ ἥμιν ἑκάεργον ἱλάσσεαι ἱερὰ ῥέξας.
lines.english: and ill-pleased he was when he beheld them. They stood fearfully and reverently before him, and never a word did they speak, but he knew them and said, "Welcome, heralds,…
lines.gloss: ὄφρα (conj.) 'so that, in order that'; ἥμιν (dat. pl. of ἐγώ) 'for us'; ἑκάεργον (acc. sg., epithet of Apollo) 'the far-worker'; ἱλάσσεαι (pres. mid. subj., 2nd sg. of ἱλάσκομαι) 'you may appease, propitiate'; ἱερά (acc. pl. neut. of ἱερός) 'sacred rites, sacrifices'; ῥέξας (aor. act. participle of ῥέζω) 'having performed, offering'.

lines.original: ὤ μοι ἀναιδείην ἐπιειμένε κερδαλεόφρον
lines.english: and ill-pleased he was when he beheld them. They stood fearfully and reverently before him, and never a word did they speak, but he knew them and said, "Welcome, heralds,…
lines.gloss: ὤ μοι (interjection + dat. of exclamation) 'woe to me!', 'alas!'; ἀναιδείην (acc. sg. of ἀναίδεια) 'shamelessness, impudence'; ἐπιειμένε (perf. mid. participle, voc. sg. of ἐπιέννυμι) 'clothed in, clad in'; κερδαλεόφρον (voc. sg. of κερδαλεόφρων) 'crafty-minded, cunning of heart.'

lines.original: πῶς τίς τοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν πείθηται Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: and ill-pleased he was when he beheld them. They stood fearfully and reverently before him, and never a word did they speak, but he knew them and said, "Welcome, heralds,…
lines.gloss: πῶς 'how?'; τίς (nom. sg.) 'anyone, someone'; τοι (dat. sg. enclitic pronoun) 'to you'; πρόφρων (nom. sg. adj.) 'willingly, eagerly'; ἔπεσιν (dat. pl. of ἔπος) 'words, commands'; πείθηται (pres. mid./pass. subj.) 'obey, comply with'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans' (partitive gen. with τίς).

lines.original: ἢ ὁδὸν ἐλθέμεναι ἢ ἀνδράσιν ἶφι μάχεσθαι;
lines.english: and ill-pleased he was when he beheld them. They stood fearfully and reverently before him, and never a word did they speak, but he knew them and said, "Welcome, heralds,…
lines.gloss: ἤ (conj.) 'either...or'; ὁδόν (acc. sg. of ὁδός) 'journey, path'; ἐλθέμεναι (aor. inf. of ἔρχομαι) 'to go, to travel'; ἀνδράσιν (dat. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'against men'; ἶφι (adv.) 'with strength, mightily'; μάχεσθαι (pres. inf. of μάχομαι) 'to fight.'

lines.original: οὐ γὰρ ἐγὼ Τρώων ἕνεκʼ ἤλυθον αἰχμητάων
lines.english: draw near; my quarrel is not with you but with Agamemnon who has sent you for the girl Briseis. Therefore, Patroklos, bring her and give her to them, but let them be witnesses by…
lines.gloss: οὐ γάρ "for not"; ἐγώ (nom. sg.) "I"; Τρώων (gen. pl. of Τρῶες) "of the Trojans"; ἕνεκα/ἕνεκʼ (+ gen.) "on account of, because of"; ἤλυθον (1st sg. aor. of ἔρχομαι) "I came"; αἰχμητάων (gen. pl. of αἰχμητής) "spearmen, warriors."

lines.original: δεῦρο μαχησόμενος, ἐπεὶ οὔ τί μοι αἴτιοί εἰσιν·
lines.english: draw near; my quarrel is not with you but with Agamemnon who has sent you for the girl Briseis. Therefore, Patroklos, bring her and give her to them, but let them be witnesses by…
lines.gloss: δεῦρο (adverb) 'here, hither'; μαχησόμενος (fut. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc.) 'to fight, going to fight'; ἐπεί (conjunction) 'since, because'; οὔ τί (negative adverb with intensifier) 'not at all, in no way'; αἴτιοί (nom. pl. masc. of αἴτιος) 'responsible, guilty, blameworthy'.

lines.original: οὐ γὰρ πώποτʼ ἐμὰς βοῦς ἤλασαν οὐδὲ μὲν ἵππους,
lines.english: draw near; my quarrel is not with you but with Agamemnon who has sent you for the girl Briseis. Therefore, Patroklos, bring her and give her to them, but let them be witnesses by…
lines.gloss: πώποτε (adverbial) 'ever yet, at any time'; ἐμάς (acc. pl. fem. of ἐμός) 'my'; βοῦς (acc. pl. of βοῦς) 'cattle, oxen'; ἤλασαν (3rd pl. aor. of ἐλαύνω) 'drove away, raided'; ἵππους (acc. pl. of ἵππος) 'horses'.

lines.original: οὐδέ ποτʼ ἐν Φθίῃ ἐριβώλακι βωτιανείρῃ
lines.english: draw near; my quarrel is not with you but with Agamemnon who has sent you for the girl Briseis. Therefore, Patroklos, bring her and give her to them, but let them be witnesses by…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ 'nor, and not'; ποτέ 'ever'; Φθίῃ (dat. sg. of Φθίη) 'Phthia' (Achilles' homeland in Thessaly); ἐριβώλακι (dat. sg. of ἐριβῶλαξ, -ακος) 'with rich clods/soil'; βωτιανείρῃ (dat. sg. of βωτιάνειρα) 'nourishing men, man-nourishing' (compound adjective modifying Φθίῃ).

lines.original: καρπὸν ἐδηλήσαντʼ, ἐπεὶ ἦ μάλα πολλὰ μεταξὺ
lines.english: draw near; my quarrel is not with you but with Agamemnon who has sent you for the girl Briseis. Therefore, Patroklos, bring her and give her to them, but let them be witnesses by…
lines.gloss: καρπόν (acc. sg. of καρπός) 'fruit, harvest'; ἐδηλήσαντο (aor. mid. 3rd pl. of δηλέομαι) 'brought to harm, ravaged'; ἐπεί 'since, because'; ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed'; μάλα (adv.) 'very, exceedingly'; πολλά (acc. pl. neut. of πολύς) 'many things'; μεταξύ (adv.) 'between, in the interval'.

lines.original: οὔρεά τε σκιόεντα θάλασσά τε ἠχήεσσα·
lines.english: and by the fierceness of Agamemnon's anger, that if ever again there be need of me to save the people from ruin, they shall seek and they shall not find. Agamemnon is mad with…
lines.gloss: οὔρεά (nom./acc. pl. neut. of ὄρος) 'mountains'; σκιόεντα (nom./acc. pl. neut. of σκιόεις) 'shadowy, shady'; θάλασσα (nom. sg. fem. of θάλασσα) 'sea'; ἠχήεσσα (nom. sg. fem. of ἠχήεις) 'echoing, resounding, loud-sounding'.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σοὶ ὦ μέγʼ ἀναιδὲς ἅμʼ ἑσπόμεθʼ ὄφρα σὺ χαίρῃς,
lines.english: and by the fierceness of Agamemnon's anger, that if ever again there be need of me to save the people from ruin, they shall seek and they shall not find. Agamemnon is mad with…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά (adversative conj.) 'but'; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'for you'; μέγʼ (adverbial acc., crasis for μέγα) 'greatly, utterly'; ἀναιδές (voc. sg. of ἀναιδής) 'shameless one'; ἅμα (adv.) 'together, along with'; ἑσπόμεθα (1st pl. pres. mid. of ἕπομαι) 'we follow'; ὄφρα (conj.) 'so that, in order that'; χαίρῃς (2nd sg. pres. subj. of χαίρω) 'you may rejoice, take pleasure'.

lines.original: τιμὴν ἀρνύμενοι Μενελάῳ σοί τε κυνῶπα
lines.english: and by the fierceness of Agamemnon's anger, that if ever again there be need of me to save the people from ruin, they shall seek and they shall not find. Agamemnon is mad with…
lines.gloss: τιμήν (acc. sg. of τιμή) 'honor, recompense'; ἀρνύμενοι (pres. mid. participle, nom. pl.) 'winning, gaining'; Μενελάῳ (dat. sg.) 'for Menelaus'; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'for you'; κυνῶπα (voc. sg. of κυνώψ) 'dog-face, shameless one' (vocative insult addressed to Agamemnon).

lines.original: πρὸς Τρώων· τῶν οὔ τι μετατρέπῃ οὐδʼ ἀλεγίζεις·
lines.english: and by the fierceness of Agamemnon's anger, that if ever again there be need of me to save the people from ruin, they shall seek and they shall not find. Agamemnon is mad with…
lines.gloss: πρὸς Τρώων 'from the Trojans' (gen. pl. with πρός); τῶν (gen. pl. demonstrative) 'of these things, of them'; οὔ τι 'not at all' (adverbial acc.); μετατρέπῃ (2nd sg. pres. mid. of μετατρέπω) 'you turn (your mind) to, you care about'; ἀλεγίζεις (2nd sg. pres. of ἀλεγίζω) 'you heed, you care for.'

lines.original: καὶ δή μοι γέρας αὐτὸς ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἀπειλεῖς,
lines.english: and by the fierceness of Agamemnon's anger, that if ever again there be need of me to save the people from ruin, they shall seek and they shall not find. Agamemnon is mad with…
lines.gloss: γέρας (acc. sg. of γέρας, neut.) 'prize, honor, gift of honor'; αὐτός (nom. sg., intensive) 'yourself, you personally'; ἀφαιρήσεσθαι (fut. mid. inf. of ἀφαιρέω) 'to take away (for yourself)'; ἀπειλεῖς (2nd sg. pres. indic. of ἀπειλέω) 'you threaten.'

lines.original: ᾧ ἔπι πολλὰ μόγησα, δόσαν δέ μοι υἷες Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: Patroklos did as his dear comrade had bidden him. He brought Briseis from the tent and gave her over to the heralds, who took her with them to the ships of the Achaeans - and the…
lines.gloss: ᾧ (dat. sg. of ὅς) 'for which, on account of which' (antecedent is γέρας); ἔπι = ἐπί 'for, in respect to'; μόγησα (aor. of μογέω) 'I toiled, labored'; δόσαν = ἔδοσαν (aor. of δίδωμι) 'they gave'; υἷες (nom. pl. of υἱός) 'sons'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: οὐ μὲν σοί ποτε ἶσον ἔχω γέρας ὁππότʼ Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: Patroklos did as his dear comrade had bidden him. He brought Briseis from the tent and gave her over to the heralds, who took her with them to the ships of the Achaeans - and the…
lines.gloss: ἶσον (acc. sg. neut. of ἴσος) 'equal'; γέρας (acc. sg. of γέρας) 'prize, honor'; ὁππότε (temporal conjunction) 'whenever'; the phrase means "I never have a prize equal (to yours) whenever the Achaeans..."

lines.original: Τρώων ἐκπέρσωσʼ εὖ ναιόμενον πτολίεθρον·
lines.english: Patroklos did as his dear comrade had bidden him. He brought Briseis from the tent and gave her over to the heralds, who took her with them to the ships of the Achaeans - and the…
lines.gloss: Τρώων (gen. pl. of Τρώς) 'of the Trojans'; ἐκπέρσωσι (aor. subj., 3rd pl. of ἐκπέρθω) 'sack, destroy utterly'; εὖ ναιόμενον (pres. part. acc. sg. neut.) 'well-inhabited'; πτολίεθρον (acc. sg. of πτολίεθρον) 'citadel, city.'

lines.original: ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν πλεῖον πολυάϊκος πολέμοιο
lines.english: Patroklos did as his dear comrade had bidden him. He brought Briseis from the tent and gave her over to the heralds, who took her with them to the ships of the Achaeans - and the…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, yet'; πλεῖον (neut. acc. sg. comparative of πολύς) 'the greater part, more'; πολυάϊκος (gen. sg. of πολυάϊκος) 'loud-shouting, tumultuous'; πολέμοιο (gen. sg. of πόλεμος) 'of war, battle'.

lines.original: χεῖρες ἐμαὶ διέπουσʼ· ἀτὰρ ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται,
lines.english: Patroklos did as his dear comrade had bidden him. He brought Briseis from the tent and gave her over to the heralds, who took her with them to the ships of the Achaeans - and the…
lines.gloss: χεῖρες (nom. pl.) 'hands'; ἐμαί (nom. pl. fem. of ἐμός) 'my'; διέπουσι (3rd pl. pres. of διέπω) 'manage, accomplish'; ἀτάρ (conj.) 'but, yet'; ἤν = ἐάν (conj.) 'if'; ποτέ (adv.) 'at some time, ever'; δασμός (nom. sg.) 'division, distribution (of spoils)'; ἵκηται (3rd sg. aor. mid. subj. of ἱκνέομαι) 'comes, arrives'.

lines.original: σοὶ τὸ γέρας πολὺ μεῖζον, ἐγὼ δʼ ὀλίγον τε φίλον τε
lines.english: by the side of the hoar sea [], weeping and looking out upon the boundless waste of waters. He raised his hands in prayer to his immortal mother, "Mother," he cried, "you bore me…
lines.gloss: σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to you'; γέρας (nom./acc. sg.) 'prize, honor-gift'; μεῖζον (comparative of μέγας) 'greater'; ὀλίγον (acc. sg. of ὀλίγος) 'small, little'; φίλον (acc. sg. of φίλος) 'dear, cherished' (both modifying an implied γέρας).

lines.original: ἔρχομʼ ἔχων ἐπὶ νῆας, ἐπεί κε κάμω πολεμίζων.
lines.english: by the side of the hoar sea [], weeping and looking out upon the boundless waste of waters. He raised his hands in prayer to his immortal mother, "Mother," he cried, "you bore me…
lines.gloss: ἔρχομ(αι) (pres. ind. 1st sg.) 'I am going'; ἔχων (pres. participle nom. sg. masc.) 'having, taking'; ἐπὶ νῆας (acc. pl. of ναῦς) 'to the ships'; ἐπεί κε (with subjunctive) 'whenever'; κάμω (aor. subjunctive 1st sg. of κάμνω) 'I grow weary, toil'; πολεμίζων (pres. participle) 'fighting, making war.'

lines.original: νῦν δʼ εἶμι Φθίην δʼ, ἐπεὶ ἦ πολὺ φέρτερόν ἐστιν
lines.english: by the side of the hoar sea [], weeping and looking out upon the boundless waste of waters. He raised his hands in prayer to his immortal mother, "Mother," he cried, "you bore me…
lines.gloss: νῦν δέ 'but now'; εἶμι (fut. of εἶμι) 'I shall go'; Φθίην δέ (acc. sg.) 'to Phthia' (Achilles' homeland); ἐπεί 'since'; ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed'; πολύ (adv. acc.) 'much, far'; φέρτερον (comparative neut. of φέρτερος) 'better, more profitable'; ἐστίν 'it is'.

lines.original: οἴκαδʼ ἴμεν σὺν νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν, οὐδέ σʼ ὀΐω
lines.english: by the side of the hoar sea [], weeping and looking out upon the boundless waste of waters. He raised his hands in prayer to his immortal mother, "Mother," he cried, "you bore me…
lines.gloss: οἴκαδε (adverbial acc.) 'homeward'; ἴμεν (pres. inf. of εἶμι) 'to go'; σὺν νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν 'with curved ships' (κορωνίς 'curved, beaked', dat. pl. agreeing with νηυσί); ὀΐω (1st sg. pres. mid. of οἴομαι) 'I think, suppose'; σέ (acc. sg. pronoun) 'you'.

lines.original: ἐνθάδʼ ἄτιμος ἐὼν ἄφενος καὶ πλοῦτον ἀφύξειν.
lines.english: by the side of the hoar sea [], weeping and looking out upon the boundless waste of waters. He raised his hands in prayer to his immortal mother, "Mother," he cried, "you bore me…
lines.gloss: ἐνθάδε (adv.) 'here'; ἄτιμος (nom. sg. masc.) 'dishonored, without honor'; ἐών (pres. participle of εἰμί) 'being'; ἄφενος (acc. sg.) 'wealth, riches'; πλοῦτον (acc. sg.) 'wealth, abundance'; ἀφύξειν (fut. inf. of ἀφύσσω) 'to heap up, accumulate'.

lines.original: φεῦγε μάλʼ εἴ τοι θυμὸς ἐπέσσυται, οὐδέ σʼ ἔγωγε
lines.english: Agamemnon, son of Atreus, has done me dishonor, and has robbed me of my prize by force." As he spoke he wept aloud, and his mother heard him where she was sitting in the depths of…
lines.gloss: φεῦγε (pres. imperative) 'flee!'; μάλα 'very much, exceedingly'; εἴ 'if'; τοι (ethical dative particle) adds personal interest; θυμός (nom. sg.) 'heart, spirit'; ἐπέσσυται (pres. mid./pass.) 'urges on, impels'; οὐδέ 'and not, nor'; σʼ = σε (acc. sg. of σύ) 'you'; ἔγωγε (emphatic nom. sg.) 'I at least, I for my part'.

lines.original: λίσσομαι εἵνεκʼ ἐμεῖο μένειν· πάρʼ ἔμοιγε καὶ ἄλλοι
lines.english: Agamemnon, son of Atreus, has done me dishonor, and has robbed me of my prize by force." As he spoke he wept aloud, and his mother heard him where she was sitting in the depths of…
lines.gloss: λίσσομαι (pres. mid./pass. 1st sg.) 'I beseech, I beg'; εἵνεκα (+ gen.) 'for the sake of'; ἐμεῖο (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'of me'; μένειν (pres. inf.) 'to remain, to stay'; πάρ (adv./prep.) 'beside, near' (here 'at hand'); ἔμοιγε (dat. sg. of ἐγώ with γε) 'for me indeed'; ἄλλοι (nom. pl. masc. of ἄλλος) 'others'.

lines.original: οἵ κέ με τιμήσουσι, μάλιστα δὲ μητίετα Ζεύς.
lines.english: Agamemnon, son of Atreus, has done me dishonor, and has robbed me of my prize by force." As he spoke he wept aloud, and his mother heard him where she was sitting in the depths of…
lines.gloss: οἵ (nom. pl. relative pronoun) 'who'; κέ (particle) = ἄν, marking potential condition; τιμήσουσι (fut. indic. 3rd pl. of τιμάω) 'will honor'; μάλιστα (adv. superlative) 'most of all, especially'; μητίετα (voc. sg. epithet) 'counselor, wise one', modifying Ζεύς.

lines.original: ἔχθιστος δέ μοί ἐσσι διοτρεφέων βασιλήων·
lines.english: Agamemnon, son of Atreus, has done me dishonor, and has robbed me of my prize by force." As he spoke he wept aloud, and his mother heard him where she was sitting in the depths of…
lines.gloss: ἔχθιστος (superlative adj., nom. sg. masc.) 'most hateful'; δέ 'but, and'; μοί (dat. sg. of ἐγώ) 'to me'; ἐσσι (2nd sg. pres. of εἰμί) 'you are'; διοτρεφέων (gen. pl. of διοτρεφής) 'Zeus-nurtured' or 'god-nourished'; βασιλήων (gen. pl. of βασιλεύς) 'of kings.'

lines.original: αἰεὶ γάρ τοι ἔρις τε φίλη πόλεμοί τε μάχαι τε·
lines.english: Agamemnon, son of Atreus, has done me dishonor, and has robbed me of my prize by force." As he spoke he wept aloud, and his mother heard him where she was sitting in the depths of…
lines.gloss: αἰεί 'always, ever'; τοι (ethical dative particle) 'to you, for you'; ἔρις (nom. sg.) 'strife, quarreling'; φίλη (nom. sg. fem. adj.) 'dear, beloved'; πόλεμοί τε μάχαι τε (nom. pl.) 'wars and battles' (the τε ... τε construction links repeated items in a series).

lines.original: εἰ μάλα καρτερός ἐσσι, θεός που σοὶ τό γʼ ἔδωκεν·
lines.english: sat down before him as he stood weeping, caressed him with her hand, and said, "My son, why are you weeping? What is it that gives you grief []? Keep it not from my thinking [],…
lines.gloss: εἰ 'if'; μάλα 'very, exceedingly'; καρτερός (nom. sg. masc.) 'strong, mighty'; ἐσσι (2nd sg. pres. of εἰμί) 'you are'; θεός (nom. sg.) 'a god'; που (enclitic particle) 'I suppose, no doubt'; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to you'; τό (acc. sg. neut. of ὁ, article or demonstrative) 'this, that'; γʼ (enclitic particle γε) 'at least, indeed'; ἔδωκεν (3rd sg. aor. of δίδωμι) 'gave, granted'.

lines.original: οἴκαδʼ ἰὼν σὺν νηυσί τε σῇς καὶ σοῖς ἑτάροισι
lines.english: sat down before him as he stood weeping, caressed him with her hand, and said, "My son, why are you weeping? What is it that gives you grief []? Keep it not from my thinking [],…
lines.gloss: οἴκαδε (adverbial acc.) 'homeward, to home'; ἰών (pres. participle nom. sg. masc. of εἶμι) 'going'; νηυσί (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'with ships'; σῇς (possessive adj. dat. pl. fem.) 'your own'; ἑτάροισι (dat. pl. of ἑταῖρος) 'with companions'.

lines.original: Μυρμιδόνεσσιν ἄνασσε, σέθεν δʼ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀλεγίζω,
lines.english: sat down before him as he stood weeping, caressed him with her hand, and said, "My son, why are you weeping? What is it that gives you grief []? Keep it not from my thinking [],…
lines.gloss: Μυρμιδόνεσσιν (dat. pl. of Μυρμιδόνες) 'over the Myrmidons'; ἄνασσε (pres. imperative of ἀνάσσω) 'be lord, rule!'; σέθεν (gen. sg. of σύ) 'of you' (archaic form); ἀλεγίζω (pres. indic. 1st sg. of ἀλεγίζω) 'I care about, heed'.

lines.original: οὐδʼ ὄθομαι κοτέοντος· ἀπειλήσω δέ τοι ὧδε·
lines.english: sat down before him as he stood weeping, caressed him with her hand, and said, "My son, why are you weeping? What is it that gives you grief []? Keep it not from my thinking [],…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ 'nor, not even'; ὄθομαι (1st sg. fut. mid. of ὀθέομαι) 'I shall care for, heed'; κοτέοντος (gen. sg. pres. part. of κοτέω) 'being angry, wrathful'; ἀπειλήσω (1st sg. fut. of ἀπειλέω) 'I shall threaten'; τοι (ethical dat. of σύ) 'to you, I tell you'; ὧδε 'thus, as follows.'

lines.original: ὡς ἔμʼ ἀφαιρεῖται Χρυσηΐδα Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων,
lines.english: sat down before him as he stood weeping, caressed him with her hand, and said, "My son, why are you weeping? What is it that gives you grief []? Keep it not from my thinking [],…
lines.gloss: ὡς (conj.) 'since, as'; ἔμʼ = ἐμέ (acc. sg. of ἐγώ) 'me'; ἀφαιρεῖται (3rd sg. pres. mid.) 'takes away from'; Χρυσηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Chryseis' (the captive girl); Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων (nom. sg.) 'Phoebus Apollo' (subject of the verb).

lines.original: τὴν μὲν ἐγὼ σὺν νηΐ τʼ ἐμῇ καὶ ἐμοῖς ἑτάροισι
lines.english: "You know it; why tell you what you know well already? We went to Thebe the strong city of Eetion, sacked it, and brought hither the spoil. The sons of the Achaeans shared it duly…
lines.gloss: τὴν μέν (acc. sg. fem. of ὁ ἡ τό) 'her' (i.e., Chryseis), correlative with δέ in next line; σὺν νηΐ (dat. sg. of ναῦς) 'with (my) ship'; ἐμῇ (dat. sg. fem. possessive) 'my'; ἑτάροισι (dat. pl. of ἑταῖρος) 'companions, comrades'.

lines.original: πέμψω, ἐγὼ δέ κʼ ἄγω Βρισηΐδα καλλιπάρῃον
lines.english: "You know it; why tell you what you know well already? We went to Thebe the strong city of Eetion, sacked it, and brought hither the spoil. The sons of the Achaeans shared it duly…
lines.gloss: πέμψω (fut. 1st sg. of πέμπω) 'I will send'; ἄγω (fut. 1st sg. of ἄγω, with κε/ἄν) 'I will take/lead away'; Βρισηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Briseis' (Achilles' captive prize); καλλιπάρῃον (acc. sg. fem. adj.) 'fair-cheeked, with beautiful cheeks'.

lines.original: αὐτὸς ἰὼν κλισίην δὲ τὸ σὸν γέρας ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδῇς
lines.english: "You know it; why tell you what you know well already? We went to Thebe the strong city of Eetion, sacked it, and brought hither the spoil. The sons of the Achaeans shared it duly…
lines.gloss: αὐτὸς (nom. sg. masc.) 'myself, in person'; ἰών (pres. participle of εἶμι) 'going'; κλισίην (acc. sg.) 'hut, tent'; τὸ σὸν γέρας (acc. sg.) 'your prize of honor'; ὄφρα (conjunction) 'so that, in order that'; ἐῢ (adv.) 'well'; εἰδῇς (2nd sg. pres. subj. of οἶδα) 'you may know'.

lines.original: ὅσσον φέρτερός εἰμι σέθεν, στυγέῃ δὲ καὶ ἄλλος
lines.english: "You know it; why tell you what you know well already? We went to Thebe the strong city of Eetion, sacked it, and brought hither the spoil. The sons of the Achaeans shared it duly…
lines.gloss: ὅσσον (acc. of extent, relative) 'how much, by how much'; φέρτερός (comparative adj., nom. sg. masc.) 'stronger, mightier'; εἰμι (1st sg. pres. of εἰμί) 'I am'; σέθεν (gen. sg. of σύ) 'than you'; στυγέῃ (3rd sg. pres. subj. of στυγέω) 'may shudder, may shrink from'; ἄλλος (nom. sg. masc.) 'another (man)'.

lines.original: ἶσον ἐμοὶ φάσθαι καὶ ὁμοιωθήμεναι ἄντην.
lines.english: "You know it; why tell you what you know well already? We went to Thebe the strong city of Eetion, sacked it, and brought hither the spoil. The sons of the Achaeans shared it duly…
lines.gloss: ἶσον (adj. acc. sg. neut.) 'equal'; φάσθαι (pres. mid. inf.) 'to claim, assert oneself'; ὁμοιωθήμεναι (aor. pass. inf.) 'to be made equal, likened'; ἄντην (adv.) 'face to face, directly' or 'openly'.

lines.original: τίπτʼ αὖτʼ αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς τέκος εἰλήλουθας;
lines.english: but Chryses, priest of Apollo, came to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the scepter of Apollo,…
lines.gloss: τίπτε (crasis of τί πτε) 'why?'; αὖτε 'again, now'; αἰγιόχοιο (gen. sg. of αἰγίοχος) 'aegis-bearing'; Διὸς (gen. sg. of Ζεύς) 'of Zeus'; τέκος (nom./acc. sg.) 'child'; εἰλήλουθας (2nd sg. perf. of ἔρχομαι) 'have you come?'

lines.original: ἦ ἵνα ὕβριν ἴδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονος Ἀτρεΐδαο;
lines.english: but Chryses, priest of Apollo, came to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the scepter of Apollo,…
lines.gloss: ἦ (interrogative particle) 'is it?' or 'surely?'; ἵνα (conjunction with subj.) 'in order that, so that'; ὕβριν (acc. sg. of ὕβρις) 'outrage, insolence'; ἴδῃ (2nd sg. aor. subj. of ὁράω) 'you may see'; Ἀγαμέμνονος (gen. sg.) 'of Agamemnon'; Ἀτρεΐδαο (gen. sg. patronymic) 'son of Atreus'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἔκ τοι ἐρέω, τὸ δὲ καὶ τελέεσθαι ὀΐω·
lines.english: but Chryses, priest of Apollo, came to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the scepter of Apollo,…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but'; ἔκ τοι (= ἐκ σοί, dat. of interest) 'to you, for you'; ἐρέω (fut. of εἴρω/λέγω) 'I will speak, tell'; τό (acc. sg. neut. article, object of ὀΐω) 'this'; δέ 'and, moreover'; καί 'also, even'; τελέεσθαι (pres. mid./pass. inf. of τελέω) 'to be fulfilled, accomplished'; ὀΐω (1st sg. pres. of οἴομαι) 'I think, expect'.

lines.original: ᾗς ὑπεροπλίῃσι τάχʼ ἄν ποτε θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ.
lines.english: but Chryses, priest of Apollo, came to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the scepter of Apollo,…
lines.gloss: ᾗς (gen. sg. of ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, here feminine) 'her, whose'; ὑπεροπλίῃσι (dat. pl. of ὑπεροπλίη) 'acts of arrogance, insolence'; τάχα 'soon, perhaps'; ἄν (modal particle) with subjunctive expressing potential action; ποτε 'someday, at some time'; θυμόν (acc. sg. of θυμός) 'life, spirit'; ὀλέσσῃ (aor. subj. 3rd sg. of ὄλλυμι) 'destroy, lose.'

lines.original: ἦλθον ἐγὼ παύσουσα τὸ σὸν μένος, αἴ κε πίθηαι,
lines.english: but Chryses, priest of Apollo, came to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the scepter of Apollo,…
lines.gloss: ἦλθον (1st sg. aor. of ἔρχομαι) 'I came'; παύσουσα (fut. fem. participle of παύω) 'to stop, check' (expressing purpose); τὸ σὸν μένος (acc. sg.) 'your wrath, fury'; αἴ κε πίθηαι (aor. subj. of πείθομαι with conditional particle) 'if you should obey, be persuaded.'

lines.original: οὐρανόθεν· πρὸ δέ μʼ ἧκε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη
lines.english: but most of all the two sons of Atreus who were their chiefs. On this the rest of the Achaeans with one voice were for respecting the priest and taking the ransom that he offered;…
lines.gloss: οὐρανόθεν (adv.) 'from heaven'; πρὸ (adv.) 'forth, forward'; ἧκε (aor. of ἵημι) 'sent'; θεὰ (nom. sg.) 'goddess'; λευκώλενος (nom. sg. f., compound adj.) 'white-armed'; Ἥρη (nom. sg.) 'Hera.'

lines.original: ἄμφω ὁμῶς θυμῷ φιλέουσά τε κηδομένη τε·
lines.english: but most of all the two sons of Atreus who were their chiefs. On this the rest of the Achaeans with one voice were for respecting the priest and taking the ransom that he offered;…
lines.gloss: ἄμφω (acc. dual) 'both [of you]'; ὁμῶς (adv.) 'equally, alike'; θυμῷ (dat. sg. of θυμός) 'in heart/spirit'; φιλέουσα (pres. fem. participle nom. sg.) 'loving'; κηδομένη (pres. mid. participle fem. nom. sg.) 'caring for, being concerned about'; both participles agree with the subject (Hera) and govern ἄμφω.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγε λῆγʼ ἔριδος, μηδὲ ξίφος ἕλκεο χειρί·
lines.english: but most of all the two sons of Atreus who were their chiefs. On this the rest of the Achaeans with one voice were for respecting the priest and taking the ransom that he offered;…
lines.gloss: ἄγε (pres. imperative of ἄγω) 'come!, come now!'; λῆγʼ (2nd sg. aor. imperative of λήγω) 'cease, stop!'; ἔριδος (gen. sg. of ἔρις) 'strife, quarrel'; μηδέ 'and not, nor'; ξίφος (acc. sg. neut.) 'sword'; ἕλκεο (2nd sg. pres. imperative middle of ἕλκω) 'draw'; χειρί (dat. sg. of χείρ) 'with your hand'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἤτοι ἔπεσιν μὲν ὀνείδισον ὡς ἔσεταί περ·
lines.english: but most of all the two sons of Atreus who were their chiefs. On this the rest of the Achaeans with one voice were for respecting the priest and taking the ransom that he offered;…
lines.gloss: ἤτοι (particle) 'indeed, truly'; ἔπεσιν (dat. pl. of ἔπος) 'with words'; ὀνείδισον (aor. imperative of ὀνειδίζω) 'reproach, insult'; ὡς ἔσεταί περ (fut. of εἰμί + περ) 'as it will be indeed' or 'as will surely happen.'

lines.original: ὧδε γὰρ ἐξερέω, τὸ δὲ καὶ τετελεσμένον ἔσται·
lines.english: but most of all the two sons of Atreus who were their chiefs. On this the rest of the Achaeans with one voice were for respecting the priest and taking the ransom that he offered;…
lines.gloss: ὧδε (adv.) 'thus, in this way'; ἐξερέω (fut. 1st sg. of ἐξεῖπον) 'I will speak out, declare'; τὸ δέ 'and this thing'; τετελεσμένον (perf. pass. part. neut. nom./acc. sg. of τελέω) 'accomplished, fulfilled'; ἔσται (fut. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) 'will be'.

lines.original: καί ποτέ τοι τρὶς τόσσα παρέσσεται ἀγλαὰ δῶρα
lines.english: So he went back in anger, and Apollo, who loved him dearly, heard his prayer. Then the god sent a deadly dart upon the Argives, and the people died thick on one another, for the…
lines.gloss: καί "and, even"; ποτέ "someday, at some time"; τοι (dat. sg. enclitic pronoun) "to you"; τρίς "three times, thrice"; τόσσα (nom./acc. pl. neut. of τόσος) "so many, as many"; παρέσσεται (fut. mid. of πάρειμι) "will be present, be at hand"; ἀγλαά (nom./acc. pl. neut. of ἀγλαός) "splendid, glorious"; δῶρα (nom./acc. pl. neut. of δῶρον) "gifts."

lines.original: ὕβριος εἵνεκα τῆσδε· σὺ δʼ ἴσχεο, πείθεο δʼ ἡμῖν.
lines.english: So he went back in anger, and Apollo, who loved him dearly, heard his prayer. Then the god sent a deadly dart upon the Argives, and the people died thick on one another, for the…
lines.gloss: ὕβριος (gen. sg. of ὕβρις) 'outrage, insult'; εἵνεκα 'for the sake of, because of' (+ gen.); τῆσδε (gen. sg. fem. demonstrative) 'this'; ἴσχεο (2nd sg. pres. mid. imperative of ἴσχω) 'hold back, restrain yourself'; πείθεο (2nd sg. pres. mid. imperative of πείθω) 'obey, be persuaded'; ἡμῖν (dat. pl. of ἐγώ) 'us.'

lines.original: χρὴ μὲν σφωΐτερόν γε θεὰ ἔπος εἰρύσσασθαι
lines.english: So he went back in anger, and Apollo, who loved him dearly, heard his prayer. Then the god sent a deadly dart upon the Argives, and the people died thick on one another, for the…
lines.gloss: χρή (impers. verb) 'it is necessary, one must'; σφωΐτερόν (acc. sg. neuter dual possessive) 'of you two, your (dual)'; γε (particle) 'at least, indeed'; θεά (nom. sg.) 'goddess'; ἔπος (acc. sg. of ἔπος) 'word, speech'; εἰρύσσασθαι (aor. mid. inf. of ἐρύω) 'to protect, defend, ward off'.

lines.original: καὶ μάλα περ θυμῷ κεχολωμένον· ὧς γὰρ ἄμεινον·
lines.english: So he went back in anger, and Apollo, who loved him dearly, heard his prayer. Then the god sent a deadly dart upon the Argives, and the people died thick on one another, for the…
lines.gloss: καὶ μάλα περ "even very much, although exceedingly"; θυμῷ (dat. sg. of θυμός) "in spirit, in heart"; κεχολωμένον (perf. pass. participle, acc. sg. masc. of χολόω) "having been angered, being angry"; ὧς "thus, in this way"; γὰρ "for"; ἄμεινον (comparative neut. sg. of ἀγαθός) "better, more profitable."

lines.original: ὅς κε θεοῖς ἐπιπείθηται μάλα τʼ ἔκλυον αὐτοῦ.
lines.english: So he went back in anger, and Apollo, who loved him dearly, heard his prayer. Then the god sent a deadly dart upon the Argives, and the people died thick on one another, for the…
lines.gloss: ὅς κε (relative pronoun with κε modal particle) 'whoever'; θεοῖς (dat. pl. of θεός) 'to the gods'; ἐπιπείθηται (pres. mid. subjunctive, 3rd sg. of ἐπιπείθομαι) 'obeys, heeds'; μάλα (adverb) 'very much, greatly'; ἔκλυον (aor. act. ind., 3rd pl. of κλύω) 'they heard, they hearkened to'; αὐτοῦ (gen. sg. of αὐτός) 'him, his (words)'.

lines.original: οἰνοβαρές, κυνὸς ὄμματʼ ἔχων, κραδίην δʼ ἐλάφοιο,
lines.english: in the fullness of his knowledge declared to us the oracles of Apollo, and I was myself first to say that we should appease him. Whereon the son of Atreus rose in anger, and…
lines.gloss: οἰνοβαρές (voc. sg. adj.) 'heavy with wine, wine-sodden'; κυνὸς (gen. sg. of κύων) 'of a dog'; ὄμματ' = ὄμματα (acc. pl. of ὄμμα) 'eyes'; ἔχων (pres. part. nom. sg. of ἔχω) 'having'; κραδίην (acc. sg. of κραδίη) 'heart'; ἐλάφοιο (gen. sg. of ἔλαφος) 'of a deer'.

lines.original: οὔτέ ποτʼ ἐς πόλεμον ἅμα λαῷ θωρηχθῆναι
lines.english: in the fullness of his knowledge declared to us the oracles of Apollo, and I was myself first to say that we should appease him. Whereon the son of Atreus rose in anger, and…
lines.gloss: οὔτέ 'nor'; ποτέ (enclitic) 'ever'; ἐς = εἰς 'into'; πόλεμον (acc. sg.) 'battle, war'; ἅμα (adv.) 'together with'; λαῷ (dat. sg. of λαός) 'the host, army'; θωρηχθῆναι (aor. pass. inf. of θωρήσσω) 'to arm oneself, be armed for battle.'

lines.original: οὔτε λόχον δʼ ἰέναι σὺν ἀριστήεσσιν Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: in the fullness of his knowledge declared to us the oracles of Apollo, and I was myself first to say that we should appease him. Whereon the son of Atreus rose in anger, and…
lines.gloss: οὔτε (conj.) 'nor'; λόχον (acc. sg. of λόχος) 'ambush, raiding party'; δʼ = δέ (particle) marks continuation; ἰέναι (pres. inf. of εἶμι) 'to go'; σὺν (prep. + dat.) 'with'; ἀριστήεσσιν (dat. pl. of ἀριστεύς) 'the best men, the champions'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: τέτληκας θυμῷ· τὸ δέ τοι κὴρ εἴδεται εἶναι.
lines.english: in the fullness of his knowledge declared to us the oracles of Apollo, and I was myself first to say that we should appease him. Whereon the son of Atreus rose in anger, and…
lines.gloss: τέτληκας (2nd sg. perf. of τλάω) 'you have dared, endured'; θυμῷ (dat. sg. of θυμός) 'in spirit/heart'; τὸ δέ 'and that'; τοι (dat. ethical) 'for you, I tell you'; κὴρ (nom. sg.) 'death, doom'; εἴδεται (3rd sg. perf. mid./pass. of *εἴδω) 'seems'; εἶναι (pres. inf. of εἰμί) 'to be'.

lines.original: ἦ πολὺ λώϊόν ἐστι κατὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: in the fullness of his knowledge declared to us the oracles of Apollo, and I was myself first to say that we should appease him. Whereon the son of Atreus rose in anger, and…
lines.gloss: ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed'; πολὺ (adv.) 'much, far'; λώϊόν (neut. comparative of ἀγαθός) 'better, more profitable'; κατά (prep. + acc.) 'throughout, along'; στρατόν (acc. sg.) 'army, host'; εὐρύν (acc. sg. masc. of εὐρύς) 'wide, broad'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: δῶρʼ ἀποαιρεῖσθαι ὅς τις σέθεν ἀντίον εἴπῃ·
lines.english: to, and sending gifts of sacrifice to the god; but the heralds have just taken from my tent the daughter of Briseus, whom the Achaeans had awarded to myself. Help your brave son,…
lines.gloss: δῶρα (acc. pl. of δῶρον) 'gifts, prizes'; ἀποαιρεῖσθαι (pres. mid. inf. of ἀποαιρέω) 'to take away, seize'; ὅς τις 'whoever, anyone who'; σέθεν (gen. of σύ) 'from you, against you'; ἀντίον (adv.) 'in opposition, against'; εἴπῃ (aor. subj. of εἶπον) 'should speak'.

lines.original: δημοβόρος βασιλεὺς ἐπεὶ οὐτιδανοῖσιν ἀνάσσεις·
lines.english: to, and sending gifts of sacrifice to the god; but the heralds have just taken from my tent the daughter of Briseus, whom the Achaeans had awarded to myself. Help your brave son,…
lines.gloss: δημοβόρος (nom. sg. masc.) 'devourer of the people, preying upon the people'; βασιλεύς (nom. sg.) 'king'; ἐπεί 'since, because'; οὐτιδανοῖσιν (dat. pl. of οὐτιδανός) 'worthless men, nobodies'; ἀνάσσεις (2nd sg. pres.) 'you rule over, you are lord of.'

lines.original: ἦ γὰρ ἂν Ἀτρεΐδη νῦν ὕστατα λωβήσαιο.
lines.english: to, and sending gifts of sacrifice to the god; but the heralds have just taken from my tent the daughter of Briseus, whom the Achaeans had awarded to myself. Help your brave son,…
lines.gloss: ἦ γὰρ ἄν (modal particle combination) 'truly then, surely'; Ἀτρεΐδη (voc. sg.) 'son of Atreus'; νῦν 'now'; ὕστατα (adv., superlative of ὕστερος) 'for the last time'; λωβήσαιο (aor. opt. middle, 2nd sg. of λωβάομαι) 'you would commit outrage, do violence.'

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἔκ τοι ἐρέω καὶ ἐπὶ μέγαν ὅρκον ὀμοῦμαι·
lines.english: to, and sending gifts of sacrifice to the god; but the heralds have just taken from my tent the daughter of Briseus, whom the Achaeans had awarded to myself. Help your brave son,…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά (strong adversative) 'but'; ἔκ = ἐκ (prefix with τοι) 'forth, openly'; τοι (ethical dative, emphasizing personal involvement) 'to you, I tell you'; ἐρέω (fut. of εἴρω/ἐννέπω) 'I shall speak'; ἐπί (+ acc.) 'upon, with'; μέγαν (acc. sg. of μέγας) 'great, mighty'; ὅρκον (acc. sg. of ὅρκος) 'oath'; ὀμοῦμαι (fut. of ὄμνυμι) 'I shall swear'.

lines.original: ναὶ μὰ τόδε σκῆπτρον, τὸ μὲν οὔ ποτε φύλλα καὶ ὄζους
lines.english: to, and sending gifts of sacrifice to the god; but the heralds have just taken from my tent the daughter of Briseus, whom the Achaeans had awarded to myself. Help your brave son,…
lines.gloss: ναὶ μά (emphatic affirmative with intensifying particle) 'yes, verily'; τόδε (demonstrative acc. sg. neut.) 'this'; σκῆπτρον (acc. sg.) 'scepter, staff'; τὸ μέν (relative pronoun acc. sg. neut. with μέν) 'which indeed'; οὔ ποτε (negative adverb with ποτε) 'never'; φύλλα (acc. pl. neut. of φύλλον) 'leaves'; ὄζους (acc. pl. masc. of ὄζος) 'branches, shoots'.

lines.original: φύσει, ἐπεὶ δὴ πρῶτα τομὴν ἐν ὄρεσσι λέλοιπεν,
lines.english: done him service in word or deed, implore the aid of Zeus. Ofttimes in my father's house have I heard you glory in that you alone of the immortals saved the son of Kronos from…
lines.gloss: φύσει (fut. 3rd sg. of φύω) 'will grow, will produce'; ἐπεί 'since, after'; πρῶτα (adv.) 'first, once'; τομήν (acc. sg. of τομή) 'the cutting'; ὄρεσσι (dat. pl. of ὄρος) 'in the mountains'; λέλοιπεν (perf. 3rd sg. of λείπω) 'it has left'.

lines.original: οὐδʼ ἀναθηλήσει· περὶ γάρ ῥά ἑ χαλκὸς ἔλεψε
lines.english: done him service in word or deed, implore the aid of Zeus. Ofttimes in my father's house have I heard you glory in that you alone of the immortals saved the son of Kronos from…
lines.gloss: οὐδέ "nor, and not"; ἀναθηλήσει (fut. 3rd sg. of ἀναθηλέω) "will bloom again, will sprout anew"; περί (adv.) "around, all around"; γάρ ῥά (particles) "for indeed"; ἑ (acc. sg. of μιν, pronoun) "it" (referring to the scepter); χαλκός (nom. sg.) "bronze, bronze blade"; ἔλεψε (aor. 3rd sg. of λέπω) "stripped, peeled."

lines.original: φύλλά τε καὶ φλοιόν· νῦν αὖτέ μιν υἷες Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: done him service in word or deed, implore the aid of Zeus. Ofttimes in my father's house have I heard you glory in that you alone of the immortals saved the son of Kronos from…
lines.gloss: φύλλά (acc. pl. of φύλλον) 'leaves'; φλοιόν (acc. sg. of φλοιός) 'bark'; νῦν 'now'; αὖτε 'again, moreover'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'it' (referring to the scepter); υἷες (nom. pl. of υἱός) 'sons'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί) 'of the Achaeans'.

lines.original: ἐν παλάμῃς φορέουσι δικασπόλοι, οἵ τε θέμιστας
lines.english: done him service in word or deed, implore the aid of Zeus. Ofttimes in my father's house have I heard you glory in that you alone of the immortals saved the son of Kronos from…
lines.gloss: ἐν παλάμῃς (dat. pl. of παλάμη) 'in (their) hands'; φορέουσι (pres. indic. 3rd pl.) 'carry, bear'; δικασπόλοι (nom. pl.) 'judges, administrators of justice'; οἵ τε (nom. pl. relative pronoun + particle) 'who indeed'; θέμιστας (acc. pl. of θέμις) 'laws, ordinances, judgments.'

lines.original: πρὸς Διὸς εἰρύαται· ὃ δέ τοι μέγας ἔσσεται ὅρκος·
lines.english: done him service in word or deed, implore the aid of Zeus. Ofttimes in my father's house have I heard you glory in that you alone of the immortals saved the son of Kronos from…
lines.gloss: πρὸς Διὸς (gen. sg.) 'from Zeus'; εἰρύαται (perf. mid./pass.) 'are guarded, protected'; ὃ δέ (nom. sg. neut. demonstrative) 'and this'; τοι (ethical dat. pronoun) 'I tell you'; μέγας ὅρκος (nom. sg.) 'great oath'; ἔσσεται (fut. of εἰμί) 'will be'.

lines.original: ἦ ποτʼ Ἀχιλλῆος ποθὴ ἵξεται υἷας Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: with Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena would have put him in bonds. It was you, goddess, who delivered him by calling tothe hundred-handed one whom gods call Briareus, but men…
lines.gloss: ποθὴ (nom. sg. of ποθή) 'longing, yearning'; ἵξεται (fut. mid. of ἱκνέομαι) 'will come upon, will reach'; υἷας (acc. pl. of υἱός) 'sons' — here 'the sons of the Achaeans' means 'the Achaeans' collectively.

lines.original: σύμπαντας· τότε δʼ οὔ τι δυνήσεαι ἀχνύμενός περ
lines.english: with Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena would have put him in bonds. It was you, goddess, who delivered him by calling tothe hundred-handed one whom gods call Briareus, but men…
lines.gloss: σύμπαντας (acc. pl. of σύμπας) 'all together, all at once'; τότε 'then'; δʼ (δέ) postpositive particle 'and, but'; οὔ τι 'not at all, in no way'; δυνήσεαι (fut. 2nd sg. of δύναμαι) 'you will be able'; ἀχνύμενός (pres. mid. ptc. nom. sg.) 'grieving, being distressed'; περ intensive particle 'though, even'.

lines.original: χραισμεῖν, εὖτʼ ἂν πολλοὶ ὑφʼ Ἕκτορος ἀνδροφόνοιο
lines.english: with Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena would have put him in bonds. It was you, goddess, who delivered him by calling tothe hundred-handed one whom gods call Briareus, but men…
lines.gloss: χραισμεῖν (pres. inf. of χραίσμω) 'to help, avail, be of use'; εὖτʼ ἄν (εὖτε + ἄν) 'whenever'; πολλοί (nom. pl. masc.) 'many'; ὑφʼ (ὑπό + elision) 'by, at the hands of'; Ἕκτορος (gen. sg.) 'of Hector'; ἀνδροφόνοιο (gen. sg. of ἀνδροφόνος) 'man-slaying, murderous'.

lines.original: θνήσκοντες πίπτωσι· σὺ δʼ ἔνδοθι θυμὸν ἀμύξεις
lines.english: with Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena would have put him in bonds. It was you, goddess, who delivered him by calling tothe hundred-handed one whom gods call Briareus, but men…
lines.gloss: θνήσκοντες (pres. part. nom. pl. masc. of θνῄσκω) 'dying'; πίπτωσι (pres. subj. 3rd pl. of πίπτω) 'fall'; ἔνδοθι (adv.) 'within, inwardly'; θυμόν (acc. sg. of θυμός) 'heart, spirit'; ἀμύξεις (fut. 2nd sg. of ἀμύσσω) 'will tear, lacerate' (in grief or anguish).

lines.original: χωόμενος ὅ τʼ ἄριστον Ἀχαιῶν οὐδὲν ἔτισας.
lines.english: with Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena would have put him in bonds. It was you, goddess, who delivered him by calling tothe hundred-handed one whom gods call Briareus, but men…
lines.gloss: χωόμενος (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg.) 'being angry, in anger'; ὅ τʼ (relative pronoun + particle) 'that, because'; ἄριστον (superlative adj., acc. sg.) 'the best, noblest'; οὐδὲν ἔτισας (aor. act. ind., 2nd sg. of τίω) 'you honored not at all, you did not honor in any way'.
