lines.original: ὦ πόποι ἦ μέγα πένθος Ἀχαιΐδα γαῖαν ἱκάνει·
lines.english: when therefore he took his seat all-glorious beside the son of Kronos, the other gods were afraid, and did not bind him. Go, then, to him, remind him of all this, clasp his knees,…
lines.gloss: ὦ πόποι (exclamation) 'alas! oh!'; ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed'; πένθος (nom. sg. neut.) 'grief, sorrow'; Ἀχαιΐδα (acc. sg. fem. adj.) 'Achaean'; γαῖαν (acc. sg. of γαῖα) 'land, earth'; ἱκάνει (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. of ἱκνέομαι) 'comes to, reaches'.

lines.original: ἦ κεν γηθήσαι Πρίαμος Πριάμοιό τε παῖδες
lines.english: when therefore he took his seat all-glorious beside the son of Kronos, the other gods were afraid, and did not bind him. Go, then, to him, remind him of all this, clasp his knees,…
lines.gloss: ἦ κεν (particle + modal particle) 'truly would'; γηθήσαι (aor. inf. of γηθέω) 'rejoice'; Πρίαμος (nom. sg.) 'Priam' (king of Troy); Πριάμοιό τε παῖδες (gen. sg. + particle + nom. pl.) 'and the sons of Priam.'

lines.original: ἄλλοι τε Τρῶες μέγα κεν κεχαροίατο θυμῷ
lines.english: when therefore he took his seat all-glorious beside the son of Kronos, the other gods were afraid, and did not bind him. Go, then, to him, remind him of all this, clasp his knees,…
lines.gloss: ἄλλοι τε (nom. pl. masc.) 'the others also/and'; Τρῶες (nom. pl.) 'Trojans'; μέγα (adv.) 'greatly'; κεν (particle) = ἄν, with optative expressing potential condition; κεχαροίατο (3rd pl. aor. opt. mid. of χαίρω) 'would rejoice'; θυμῷ (dat. sg. of θυμός) 'in heart/spirit', dat. of respect.

lines.original: εἰ σφῶϊν τάδε πάντα πυθοίατο μαρναμένοιϊν,
lines.english: when therefore he took his seat all-glorious beside the son of Kronos, the other gods were afraid, and did not bind him. Go, then, to him, remind him of all this, clasp his knees,…
lines.gloss: εἰ 'if'; σφῶϊν (gen. dual of σύ) 'of you two'; τάδε (acc. pl. neut. of ὅδε) 'these things'; πάντα (acc. pl. neut.) 'all'; πυθοίατο (3rd pl. aor. opt. mid. of πυνθάνομαι) 'should learn, hear of'; μαρναμένοιϊν (gen. dual pres. part. of μάρναμαι) 'of (you two) quarreling, fighting'.

lines.original: οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν, περὶ δʼ ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι.
lines.english: when therefore he took his seat all-glorious beside the son of Kronos, the other gods were afraid, and did not bind him. Go, then, to him, remind him of all this, clasp his knees,…
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. relative pronoun) 'who'; περὶ μέν… περὴ δέ 'both... and' (correlative adverbs); βουλήν (acc. sg.) 'in counsel'; Δαναῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Danaans/Greeks'; ἐστέ (2nd pl. pres. of εἰμί) 'you are'; μάχεσθαι (pres. mid./pass. inf.) 'to fight'.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ πίθεσθʼ· ἄμφω δὲ νεωτέρω ἐστὸν ἐμεῖο·
lines.english: that they may reap what joy they may of their king, and that Agamemnon may rue his derangement [] in offering insult to the best [] of the Achaeans." Thetis wept and answered, "My…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, rather'; πίθεσθε (aor. mid. imperative, 2nd pl.) 'obey!'; ἄμφω (nom. dual) 'both (of you)'; νεωτέρω (nom. dual comparative of νέος) 'younger'; ἐστόν (2nd dual of εἰμί) 'you two are'; ἐμεῖο (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'than me'.

lines.original: ἤδη γάρ ποτʼ ἐγὼ καὶ ἀρείοσιν ἠέ περ ὑμῖν
lines.english: that they may reap what joy they may of their king, and that Agamemnon may rue his derangement [] in offering insult to the best [] of the Achaeans." Thetis wept and answered, "My…
lines.gloss: ἤδη 'already, before now'; γάρ 'for' (explanatory); ποτέ 'once, at some time'; ἀρείοσιν (dat. pl. comparative of ἀγαθός) 'better men, mightier warriors'; ἠέ 'than'; περ (intensive particle) 'even'; ὑμῖν (dat. pl. of σύ) 'than you'.

lines.original: ἀνδράσιν ὡμίλησα, καὶ οὔ ποτέ μʼ οἵ γʼ ἀθέριζον.
lines.english: that they may reap what joy they may of their king, and that Agamemnon may rue his derangement [] in offering insult to the best [] of the Achaeans." Thetis wept and answered, "My…
lines.gloss: ἀνδράσιν (dat. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'with men'; ὡμίλησα (aor. indic. of ὁμιλέω) 'I associated with, conversed with'; ἀθέριζον (imperf. of ἀθερίζω) 'they disregarded, scorned'; μʼ = με (acc. sg. personal pronoun) 'me'.

lines.original: οὐ γάρ πω τοίους ἴδον ἀνέρας οὐδὲ ἴδωμαι,
lines.english: that they may reap what joy they may of their king, and that Agamemnon may rue his derangement [] in offering insult to the best [] of the Achaeans." Thetis wept and answered, "My…
lines.gloss: οὐ γάρ πω: "for never yet"; τοίους (acc. pl. masc. of τοῖος) "such (men)"; ἴδον (2nd aor. of ὁράω) "I saw"; ἀνέρας (acc. pl. of ἀνήρ) "men"; οὐδὲ ἴδωμαι (1st sg. aor. mid. subj. of ὁράω) "nor shall I see," expressing emphatic negation extending to the future.

lines.original: οἷον Πειρίθοόν τε Δρύαντά τε ποιμένα λαῶν
lines.english: that they may reap what joy they may of their king, and that Agamemnon may rue his derangement [] in offering insult to the best [] of the Achaeans." Thetis wept and answered, "My…
lines.gloss: οἷον (acc. sg. of οἷος) 'such as, of such a kind'; Πειρίθοόν (acc. sg.) 'Pirithous' (legendary Lapith hero); Δρύαντά (acc. sg.) 'Dryas' (another hero); ποιμένα λαῶν (acc. sg., common epic formula) 'shepherd of the people' (epithet for a leader or chieftain).

lines.original: Καινέα τʼ Ἐξάδιόν τε καὶ ἀντίθεον Πολύφημον
lines.english: Would indeed that you had lived your span free from all sorrow at your ships, for it is all too brief; alas, that you should be at once short of life and long of sorrow above your…
lines.gloss: Καινέα (acc. sg. of Καινεύς) 'Caeneus,' a Lapith hero; Ἐξάδιον (acc. sg. of Ἐξάδιος) 'Exadius'; ἀντίθεον (acc. sg. adj.) 'godlike, equal to the gods,' modifying Πολύφημον (acc. sg. of Πολύφημος) 'Polyphemus' (here the Lapith, not the Cyclops).

lines.original: Θησέα τʼ Αἰγεΐδην, ἐπιείκελον ἀθανάτοισιν·
lines.english: Would indeed that you had lived your span free from all sorrow at your ships, for it is all too brief; alas, that you should be at once short of life and long of sorrow above your…
lines.gloss: Θησέα (acc. sg.) 'Theseus'; Αἰγεΐδην (acc. sg., patronymic) 'son of Aegeus'; ἐπιείκελον (acc. sg. masc. of ἐπιείκελος) 'like, resembling' (+ dat.); ἀθανάτοισιν (dat. pl. of ἀθάνατος) 'the immortals, gods'.

lines.original: κάρτιστοι δὴ κεῖνοι ἐπιχθονίων τράφεν ἀνδρῶν·
lines.english: Would indeed that you had lived your span free from all sorrow at your ships, for it is all too brief; alas, that you should be at once short of life and long of sorrow above your…
lines.gloss: κάρτιστοι (nom. pl. masc. superlative of καρτερός) 'strongest, mightiest'; δή (particle) emphasizing 'indeed, truly'; κεῖνοι (nom. pl. demonstrative) 'those men'; ἐπιχθονίων (gen. pl. of ἐπιχθόνιος) 'of earth-dwelling, of mortal'; τράφεν (3rd sg. aor. pass. of τρέφω) 'were reared, grew up'; ἀνδρῶν (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'of men'.

lines.original: κάρτιστοι μὲν ἔσαν καὶ καρτίστοις ἐμάχοντο
lines.english: Would indeed that you had lived your span free from all sorrow at your ships, for it is all too brief; alas, that you should be at once short of life and long of sorrow above your…
lines.gloss: κάρτιστοι (nom. pl. masc. of κάρτιστος, superlative of κρατερός) 'strongest, mightiest'; μέν 'indeed' (correlating with following contrast); ἔσαν (3rd pl. impf. of εἰμί) 'they were'; καρτίστοις (dat. pl. masc. of κάρτιστος) 'with/against the mightiest'; ἐμάχοντο (3rd pl. impf. mid.) 'they fought'.

lines.original: φηρσὶν ὀρεσκῴοισι καὶ ἐκπάγλως ἀπόλεσσαν.
lines.english: Would indeed that you had lived your span free from all sorrow at your ships, for it is all too brief; alas, that you should be at once short of life and long of sorrow above your…
lines.gloss: φηρσὶν (dat. pl. of φήρ) 'wild beasts, monsters' (referring to the Centaurs); ὀρεσκῴοισι (dat. pl. of ὀρεσκῷος) 'mountain-dwelling'; ἐκπάγλως (adv.) 'exceedingly, utterly'; ἀπόλεσσαν (3rd pl. aor. of ἀπόλλυμι) 'they destroyed'.

lines.original: καὶ μὲν τοῖσιν ἐγὼ μεθομίλεον ἐκ Πύλου ἐλθὼν
lines.english: nevertheless I will go to the snowy heights of, and tell this tale to Zeus, if he will hear our prayer: meanwhile stay where you are with your ships, nurse your anger [] against…
lines.gloss: τοῖσιν (dat. pl. of ὁ, ἡ, τό) 'with them, among them'; μεθομίλεον (impf. of μεθομιλέω) 'I joined in combat, I fought alongside'; ἐκ Πύλου 'from Pylos'; ἐλθών (aor. part. of ἔρχομαι) 'having come, coming'.

lines.original: τηλόθεν ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης· καλέσαντο γὰρ αὐτοί·
lines.english: nevertheless I will go to the snowy heights of, and tell this tale to Zeus, if he will hear our prayer: meanwhile stay where you are with your ships, nurse your anger [] against…
lines.gloss: τηλόθεν (adv.) 'from afar'; ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης (gen. sg. of ἀπαῖος γαῖα) 'from a distant land'; καλέσαντο (aor. mid. 3rd pl. of καλέω) 'they summoned (me)'; αὐτοί (nom. pl. masc., intensive) 'themselves, of their own accord'.

lines.original: καὶ μαχόμην κατʼ ἔμʼ αὐτὸν ἐγώ· κείνοισι δʼ ἂν οὔ τις
lines.english: nevertheless I will go to the snowy heights of, and tell this tale to Zeus, if he will hear our prayer: meanwhile stay where you are with your ships, nurse your anger [] against…
lines.gloss: μαχόμην (imperf. mid.) 'I fought'; κατ' ἔμ' αὐτόν (= κατὰ ἐμὲ αὐτόν) 'by myself alone, on my own'; κείνοισι (dat. pl. demonstrative) 'against those men'; ἄν … τις 'anyone (could fight)' with modal particle ἄν suggesting potential or counterfactual sense.

lines.original: τῶν οἳ νῦν βροτοί εἰσιν ἐπιχθόνιοι μαχέοιτο·
lines.english: nevertheless I will go to the snowy heights of, and tell this tale to Zeus, if he will hear our prayer: meanwhile stay where you are with your ships, nurse your anger [] against…
lines.gloss: τῶν (gen. pl. of ὁ, partitive) 'of those'; οἳ (nom. pl. relative pronoun) 'who'; νῦν (adv.) 'now'; βροτοί (nom. pl. of βροτός) 'mortals, men'; ἐπιχθόνιοι (nom. pl. adj.) 'upon the earth, earthly'; μαχέοιτο (3rd sg. pres. opt. middle of μάχομαι) 'could fight,' potential optative expressing a counterfactual possibility.

lines.original: καὶ μέν μευ βουλέων ξύνιεν πείθοντό τε μύθῳ·
lines.english: nevertheless I will go to the snowy heights of, and tell this tale to Zeus, if he will hear our prayer: meanwhile stay where you are with your ships, nurse your anger [] against…
lines.gloss: μευ (enclitic gen. of ἐγώ) 'of me, my'; βουλέων (gen. pl. of βουλή) 'counsels, plans'; ξύνιεν (imperfect of ξυνίημι) 'understood, comprehended'; πείθοντό (imperfect middle/passive) 'obeyed, were persuaded'; μύθῳ (dat. sg. of μῦθος) 'by my word, speech.'

lines.original: ἀλλὰ πίθεσθε καὶ ὔμμες, ἐπεὶ πείθεσθαι ἄμεινον·
lines.english: He will return totwelve days hence; I will then go to his mansion paved with bronze and will beseech him; nor do I doubt that I shall be able to persuade him." On this she left…
lines.gloss: πίθεσθε (2nd pl. aor. mid. imperative of πείθομαι) 'obey!'; ὔμμες (nom. pl., Epic/Ionic form of ὑμεῖς) 'you'; ἄμεινον (neuter comparative of ἀγαθός) 'better, more advantageous'; the line urges collective obedience with ἐπεί introducing the causal clause 'since it is better to obey.'

lines.original: μήτε σὺ τόνδʼ ἀγαθός περ ἐὼν ἀποαίρεο κούρην,
lines.english: He will return totwelve days hence; I will then go to his mansion paved with bronze and will beseech him; nor do I doubt that I shall be able to persuade him." On this she left…
lines.gloss: μήτε (prohibitive particle with subj.) 'do not'; ἀγαθός περ ἐών (concessive participle, nom. sg. masc.) 'although being noble/brave'; ἀποαίρεο (2nd sg. pres. mid. subjunctive of ἀποαιρέω) 'take away'; κούρην (acc. sg. of κούρη) 'girl, maiden'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἔα ὥς οἱ πρῶτα δόσαν γέρας υἷες Ἀχαιῶν·
lines.english: He will return totwelve days hence; I will then go to his mansion paved with bronze and will beseech him; nor do I doubt that I shall be able to persuade him." On this she left…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά (strong adversative) 'but'; ἔα (pres. imperative of ἐάω) 'allow, let be'; ὥς (adv.) 'as, just as'; οἱ (dat. sg. pronoun) 'to him'; πρῶτα (adv.) 'at first, originally'; δόσαν (3rd pl. aor. of δίδωμι) 'gave'; γέρας (acc. sg.) 'prize of honor'; υἷες Ἀχαιῶν (nom. pl., gen. pl.) 'sons of the Achaeans.'

lines.original: μήτε σὺ Πηλείδη ἔθελʼ ἐριζέμεναι βασιλῆϊ
lines.english: He will return totwelve days hence; I will then go to his mansion paved with bronze and will beseech him; nor do I doubt that I shall be able to persuade him." On this she left…
lines.gloss: μήτε (prohibitive) 'and do not'; Πηλείδη (voc. sg.) 'son of Peleus' (addressing Achilles); ἔθελε (2nd sg. pres. imperative of ἐθέλω) 'wish, desire'; ἐριζέμεναι (pres. infinitive) 'to contend, quarrel'; βασιλῆϊ (dat. sg.) 'with the king' (Agamemnon).

lines.original: ἀντιβίην, ἐπεὶ οὔ ποθʼ ὁμοίης ἔμμορε τιμῆς
lines.english: He will return totwelve days hence; I will then go to his mansion paved with bronze and will beseech him; nor do I doubt that I shall be able to persuade him." On this she left…
lines.gloss: ἀντιβίην (adv.) 'face to face, in opposition, directly'; ἐπεὶ 'since, because'; οὔ ποθʼ (= οὔ ποτε) 'never, not ever'; ὁμοίης (gen. sg. of ὁμοῖος) 'equal, like'; ἔμμορε (aor. of μείρομαι) 'obtained (as one's portion), had a share of'; τιμῆς (gen. sg. of τιμή) 'honor, privilege'.

lines.original: σκηπτοῦχος βασιλεύς, ᾧ τε Ζεὺς κῦδος ἔδωκεν.
lines.english: that had been taken by force [] from him. Meanwhile Odysseus reachedwith the hecatomb. When they had come inside the harbor they furled the sails and laid them in the ship's hold;…
lines.gloss: σκηπτοῦχος (nom. sg. adj.) 'scepter-bearing'; βασιλεύς (nom. sg.) 'king'; ᾧ (dat. sg. relative pron.) 'to whom'; Ζεύς (nom. sg.) 'Zeus'; κῦδος (acc. sg. neut.) 'glory, renown'; ἔδωκεν (aor. indic. 3rd sg. of δίδωμι) 'gave, has given'.

lines.original: εἰ δὲ σὺ καρτερός ἐσσι θεὰ δέ σε γείνατο μήτηρ,
lines.english: that had been taken by force [] from him. Meanwhile Odysseus reachedwith the hecatomb. When they had come inside the harbor they furled the sails and laid them in the ship's hold;…
lines.gloss: εἰ δέ "but if" (conditional); καρτερός (nom. sg. m.) "strong, mighty"; ἐσσι (2nd sg. pres. of εἰμί) "you are"; θεά (nom. sg.) "goddess"; γείνατο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of γίγνομαι) "bore, gave birth to"; μήτηρ (nom. sg.) "mother."

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅ γε φέρτερός ἐστιν ἐπεὶ πλεόνεσσιν ἀνάσσει.
lines.english: that had been taken by force [] from him. Meanwhile Odysseus reachedwith the hecatomb. When they had come inside the harbor they furled the sails and laid them in the ship's hold;…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, yet'; ὅ γε (demonstrative + particle) 'he at least, that one'; φέρτερος (comparative adj., nom. sg.) 'stronger, superior'; ἐπεί 'since, because'; πλεόνεσσιν (dat. pl. of πλείων) 'over more (men)'; ἀνάσσει (pres. indic. 3rd sg. of ἀνάσσω) 'rules, is lord'.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδη σὺ δὲ παῦε τεὸν μένος· αὐτὰρ ἔγωγε
lines.english: that had been taken by force [] from him. Meanwhile Odysseus reachedwith the hecatomb. When they had come inside the harbor they furled the sails and laid them in the ship's hold;…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδη (voc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (addressing Agamemnon); παῦε (aor. imperative of παύω) 'stop, cease'; τεὸν μένος (acc.) 'your wrath/anger'; αὐτὰρ ἔγωγε 'but I (for my part)' (emphatic first person).

lines.original: λίσσομʼ Ἀχιλλῆϊ μεθέμεν χόλον, ὃς μέγα πᾶσιν
lines.english: that had been taken by force [] from him. Meanwhile Odysseus reachedwith the hecatomb. When they had come inside the harbor they furled the sails and laid them in the ship's hold;…
lines.gloss: λίσσομαι (1st sg. pres. mid.) 'I beseech, entreat'; μεθέμεν (aor. inf. of μεθίημι) 'to let go, give up'; χόλον (acc. sg.) 'wrath, anger'; ὃς (relative pronoun, nom. sg.) 'who'; μέγα (adverbial acc.) 'greatly'; πᾶσιν (dat. pl. of πᾶς) 'for all'.

lines.original: ἕρκος Ἀχαιοῖσιν πέλεται πολέμοιο κακοῖο.
lines.english: and rowed the ship to the place where they would have her lie; there they cast out their mooring-stones and made fast the hawsers. They then got out upon the sea-shore and landed…
lines.gloss: ἕρκος (nom. sg. of ἕρκος) 'bulwark, wall, defense'; Ἀχαιοῖσιν (dat. pl.) 'for the Achaeans'; πέλεται (pres. mid. 3rd sg. of πέλομαι) 'he is, proves to be'; πολέμοιο κακοῖο (gen. sg. of πόλεμος κακός) 'of evil war, of destructive battle.'

lines.original: ναὶ δὴ ταῦτά γε πάντα γέρον κατὰ μοῖραν ἔειπες·
lines.english: and rowed the ship to the place where they would have her lie; there they cast out their mooring-stones and made fast the hawsers. They then got out upon the sea-shore and landed…
lines.gloss: ναὶ (particle) 'yes, indeed'; δή (emphatic particle) 'surely, certainly'; ταῦτά (acc. pl. neut. of οὗτος) 'these things'; γε (enclitic particle) 'at least, indeed'; κατὰ μοῖραν (idiom, acc. sg. of μοῖρα) 'fittingly, according to proper measure'; γέρον (voc. sg. of γέρων) 'old man'; ἔειπες (2nd sg. aor. of εἶπον) 'you spoke'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅδʼ ἀνὴρ ἐθέλει περὶ πάντων ἔμμεναι ἄλλων,
lines.english: and rowed the ship to the place where they would have her lie; there they cast out their mooring-stones and made fast the hawsers. They then got out upon the sea-shore and landed…
lines.gloss: ἀλλʼ = ἀλλά (adversative conjunction) 'but'; ὅδʼ = ὅδε (demonstrative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) 'this man'; ἐθέλει (pres. indic. 3rd sg.) 'wishes, desires'; περὶ πάντων (gen. pl. with preposition) 'above all others'; ἔμμεναι (pres. infinitive of εἰμί) 'to be'; ἄλλων (gen. pl. of ἄλλος) 'of others'.

lines.original: πάντων μὲν κρατέειν ἐθέλει, πάντεσσι δʼ ἀνάσσειν,
lines.english: and rowed the ship to the place where they would have her lie; there they cast out their mooring-stones and made fast the hawsers. They then got out upon the sea-shore and landed…
lines.gloss: πάντων (gen. pl. of πᾶς) 'of all'; κρατέειν (pres. inf. of κρατέω) 'to rule, have power over' (governs genitive); ἐθέλει (pres. ind.) 'he wishes, desires'; πάντεσσι (dat. pl. of πᾶς) 'over all'; ἀνάσσειν (pres. inf. of ἀνάσσω) 'to be lord, hold sway' (governs dative).

lines.original: πᾶσι δὲ σημαίνειν, ἅ τινʼ οὐ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω·
lines.english: and rowed the ship to the place where they would have her lie; there they cast out their mooring-stones and made fast the hawsers. They then got out upon the sea-shore and landed…
lines.gloss: πᾶσι (dat. pl. of πᾶς) 'to all'; σημαίνειν (pres. inf. of σημαίνω) 'to give orders, command'; ἅ (acc. pl. neut. relative pronoun) 'which things'; τινʼ = τινά (acc. sg. of τις) 'someone, anyone'; οὐ πείσεσθαι (fut. inf. mid. of πείθομαι) 'will not obey'; ὀΐω (1st sg. pres. of οἴομαι) 'I think, suppose.'

lines.original: εἰ δέ μιν αἰχμητὴν ἔθεσαν θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες
lines.english: and Odysseus led her to the altar to deliver her into the hands of her father. "Chryses," said he, "King Agamemnon has sent me to bring you back your child, and to offer sacrifice…
lines.gloss: **εἰ** (conj.) 'if'; **μιν** (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him'; **αἰχμητήν** (acc. sg. of αἰχμητής) 'spearman, warrior'; **ἔθεσαν** (3rd pl. aor. of τίθημι) 'made, appointed'; **θεοί** (nom. pl.) 'gods'; **αἰὲν ἐόντες** (pres. ptc. nom. pl. of εἰμί with adverb) 'being forever, eternal gods'.

lines.original: τοὔνεκά οἱ προθέουσιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι;
lines.english: and Odysseus led her to the altar to deliver her into the hands of her father. "Chryses," said he, "King Agamemnon has sent me to bring you back your child, and to offer sacrifice…
lines.gloss: τοὔνεκα (crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα) 'for this reason, on account of this'; προθέουσιν (3rd pl. pres. indic. of προθέω) 'rush forward, are eager'; ὀνείδεα (acc. pl. of ὄνειδος) 'reproaches, taunts'; μυθήσασθαι (aor. mid. inf. of μυθέομαι) 'to speak, utter.'

lines.original: ἦ γάρ κεν δειλός τε καὶ οὐτιδανὸς καλεοίμην
lines.english: and Odysseus led her to the altar to deliver her into the hands of her father. "Chryses," said he, "King Agamemnon has sent me to bring you back your child, and to offer sacrifice…
lines.gloss: δειλός 'cowardly, base'; οὐτιδανός 'worthless, of no account'; καλεοίμην (pres. opt. mid., 1st sg.) 'I would be called'. The optative expresses potential condition: "for indeed I would be called cowardly and worthless."

lines.original: εἰ δὴ σοὶ πᾶν ἔργον ὑπείξομαι ὅττί κεν εἴπῃς·
lines.english: and Odysseus led her to the altar to deliver her into the hands of her father. "Chryses," said he, "King Agamemnon has sent me to bring you back your child, and to offer sacrifice…
lines.gloss: εἰ 'if'; δή (particle) emphasizing condition; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to you'; πᾶν (acc. sg. neut. of πᾶς) 'every'; ἔργον (acc. sg.) 'deed, matter'; ὑπείξομαι (fut. mid. of ὑπείκω) 'I shall yield, submit'; ὅττι (neut. relative pronoun, = ὅ τι) 'whatever'; κεν (= ἄν, modal particle with subjunctive); εἴπῃς (2nd sg. aor. subj. of εἶπον) 'you should say.'

lines.original: ἄλλοισιν δὴ ταῦτʼ ἐπιτέλλεο, μὴ γὰρ ἔμοιγε
lines.english: and Odysseus led her to the altar to deliver her into the hands of her father. "Chryses," said he, "King Agamemnon has sent me to bring you back your child, and to offer sacrifice…
lines.gloss: ἄλλοισιν (dat. pl. of ἄλλος) 'to others'; ταῦτα (acc. pl. neut. demonstrative) 'these things'; ἐπιτέλλεο (pres. mid. imperative 2nd sg. of ἐπιτέλλω) 'give orders, command'; ἔμοιγε (dat. sg. 1st person pronoun + enclitic γε) 'to me at least, as for me'.

lines.original: σήμαινʼ· οὐ γὰρ ἔγωγʼ ἔτι σοὶ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω.
lines.english: who has now brought sorrow upon the Argives." So saying he gave the girl over to her father, who received her gladly, and they ranged the holy hecatomb all orderly round the altar…
lines.gloss: σήμαινʼ (pres. imperative of σημαίνω) 'mark this, take note'; ἔγωγʼ (emphatic first person pronoun) 'I for my part'; πείσεσθαι (fut. infinitive of πείθομαι) 'to obey, be persuaded'; ὀΐω (first sg. pres. of ὀΐομαι) 'I think, I suppose'.

lines.original: ἄλλο δέ τοι ἐρέω, σὺ δʼ ἐνὶ φρεσὶ βάλλεο σῇσι·
lines.english: who has now brought sorrow upon the Argives." So saying he gave the girl over to her father, who received her gladly, and they ranged the holy hecatomb all orderly round the altar…
lines.gloss: ἄλλο (acc. sg. neut. of ἄλλος) 'another thing'; ἐρέω (fut. of εἴρω/λέγω) 'I shall tell'; ἐνὶ = ἐν 'in'; φρεσὶ (dat. pl. of φρήν) 'mind, heart, wits'; βάλλεο (2nd sg. aor. mid. imperative of βάλλω) 'place, put!'; σῇσι (dat. pl. fem. of σός) 'your (own).'

lines.original: χερσὶ μὲν οὔ τοι ἔγωγε μαχήσομαι εἵνεκα κούρης
lines.english: who has now brought sorrow upon the Argives." So saying he gave the girl over to her father, who received her gladly, and they ranged the holy hecatomb all orderly round the altar…
lines.gloss: χερσί (dat. pl. of χείρ) 'with hands, in combat'; μέν (particle) introduces contrast; οὔ (adv.) 'not'; τοι (ethical dative, 2nd sg. pronoun) 'I tell you'; ἔγωγε (1st sg. pronoun, emphatic) 'I for my part'; μαχήσομαι (fut. mid. of μάχομαι) 'will fight'; εἵνεκα (prep. + gen.) 'for the sake of, on account of'; κούρης (gen. sg. of κούρη) 'girl, maiden'.

lines.original: οὔτε σοὶ οὔτέ τῳ ἄλλῳ, ἐπεί μʼ ἀφέλεσθέ γε δόντες·
lines.english: who has now brought sorrow upon the Argives." So saying he gave the girl over to her father, who received her gladly, and they ranged the holy hecatomb all orderly round the altar…
lines.gloss: οὔτε... οὔτε 'neither... nor'; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to you'; τῳ (dat. sg. of τις) 'to anyone'; ἄλλῳ (dat. sg. of ἄλλος) 'other, else'; ἀφέλεσθε (2nd pl. aor. mid. of ἀφαιρέω) 'you took away'; δόντες (nom. pl. masc. aor. part. of δίδωμι) 'having given', concessive 'though you gave'.

lines.original: τῶν δʼ ἄλλων ἅ μοί ἐστι θοῇ παρὰ νηῒ μελαίνῃ
lines.english: who has now brought sorrow upon the Argives." So saying he gave the girl over to her father, who received her gladly, and they ranged the holy hecatomb all orderly round the altar…
lines.gloss: τῶν δʼ ἄλλων (gen. pl. of ἄλλος) 'of the other things'; ἅ (neut. pl. rel. pronoun) 'which'; μοί (dat. sg. of ἐγώ) 'to me, mine'; ἐστι (3rd sg. pres. of εἰμί) 'is, are'; θοῇ (dat. sg. fem. of θοός) 'swift'; παρά (prep. + dat.) 'beside, by'; νηΐ (dat. sg. of ναῦς) 'ship'; μελαίνῃ (dat. sg. fem. of μέλας) 'black, dark'.

lines.original: τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι φέροις ἀνελὼν ἀέκοντος ἐμεῖο·
lines.english: while Chryses lifted up his hands and prayed aloud on their behalf. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla, and rulewith your might. Even as…
lines.gloss: τῶν (gen. pl. of ὁ, ἡ, τό) 'of those things'; οὐκ ἄν signals a potential construction with negative ('you would not'); φέροις (2nd sg. pres. opt. of φέρω) 'carry off, take away'; ἀνελών (aor. participle of ἀναιρέω) 'having taken up'; ἀέκοντος (gen. sg. pres. participle of ἀέκων) 'unwilling'; ἐμεῖο (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'of me' — "you would not take away any of these things against my will."

lines.original: εἰ δʼ ἄγε μὴν πείρησαι ἵνα γνώωσι καὶ οἵδε·
lines.english: while Chryses lifted up his hands and prayed aloud on their behalf. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla, and rulewith your might. Even as…
lines.gloss: εἰ δ' ἄγε μήν: emphatic combination "but come now indeed!"; πείρησαι (aor. mid. imperative of πειράω) "try, make trial"; ἵνα (conj.) "in order that"; γνώωσι (aor. subj., 3rd pl. of γιγνώσκω) "may know, recognize"; καὶ οἵδε "these men too" (nom. pl. demonstrative).

lines.original: αἶψά τοι αἷμα κελαινὸν ἐρωήσει περὶ δουρί.
lines.english: while Chryses lifted up his hands and prayed aloud on their behalf. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla, and rulewith your might. Even as…
lines.gloss: αἶψα 'straightway, quickly'; αἷμα (nom./acc. sg.) 'blood'; κελαινόν (adj. acc. sg.) 'dark, black'; ἐρωήσει (fut. 3rd sg. of ἐρωέω) 'will flow, drip'; περί (prep. + dat.) 'around, about'; δουρί (dat. sg. of δόρυ) 'spear, spear-shaft'.

lines.original: ἔρχεσθον κλισίην Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος·
lines.english: while Chryses lifted up his hands and prayed aloud on their behalf. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla, and rulewith your might. Even as…
lines.gloss: ἔρχεσθον (pres. imperative dual of ἔρχομαι) 'go!', addressed to two heralds; κλισίην (acc. sg. of κλισίη) 'hut, shelter'; Πηληϊάδεω (gen. sg. patronymic) 'of the son of Peleus'; Ἀχιλῆος (gen. sg.) 'of Achilles.'

lines.original: χειρὸς ἑλόντʼ ἀγέμεν Βρισηΐδα καλλιπάρῃον·
lines.english: while Chryses lifted up his hands and prayed aloud on their behalf. "Hear me," he cried, "O god of the silver bow, you who protectand holy Cilla, and rulewith your might. Even as…
lines.gloss: χειρὸς (gen. sg. of χείρ) 'by the hand'; ἑλόντʼ = ἑλόντα (aor. act. ptc. acc. sg. of αἱρέω) 'having taken, seizing'; ἀγέμεν = ἄγειν (pres. inf.) 'to lead, bring'; Βρισηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Briseis,' Achilles' prize; καλλιπάρῃον (acc. sg. adj.) 'fair-cheeked, beautiful-cheeked.'

lines.original: εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώῃσιν ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι
lines.english: so hear me yet again, and stay this fearful pestilence from the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his prayer. When they had done praying and sprinkling the barley-meal,…
lines.gloss: εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώῃσιν (3rd sg. aor. subj. of δίδωμι, with κε = ἄν) 'if he should not give (her)'; ἐγὼ δέ 'but I'; κεν (= ἄν) with ἕλωμαι (1st sg. aor. subj. mid. of αἱρέω) 'I myself will take'; αὐτός 'myself' (emphatic).

lines.original: ἐλθὼν σὺν πλεόνεσσι· τό οἱ καὶ ῥίγιον ἔσται.
lines.english: so hear me yet again, and stay this fearful pestilence from the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his prayer. When they had done praying and sprinkling the barley-meal,…
lines.gloss: ἐλθὼν (aor. part. nom. sg. masc. of ἔρχομαι) 'having gone, going'; σὺν πλεόνεσσι (dat. pl. of πλέων) 'with more men, with a larger force'; τό (nom./acc. sg. neut. demonstrative) 'that (thing)'; οἱ (dat. sg. pronoun) 'for him'; ῥίγιον (comparative neut. of ῥίγιος) 'more chilling, more dreadful'; ἔσται (fut. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) 'will be.'

lines.original: χαίρετε κήρυκες Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν,
lines.english: so hear me yet again, and stay this fearful pestilence from the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his prayer. When they had done praying and sprinkling the barley-meal,…
lines.gloss: χαίρετε (pres. imperative, 2nd pl. of χαίρω) 'greetings!' or 'hail!'; κήρυκες (nom. pl. of κῆρυξ) 'heralds'; Διὸς (gen. sg. of Ζεύς) 'of Zeus'; ἄγγελοι (nom. pl. of ἄγγελος) 'messengers'; ἠδὲ καί 'and also'; ἀνδρῶν (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'of men'.

lines.original: ἆσσον ἴτʼ· οὔ τί μοι ὔμμες ἐπαίτιοι ἀλλʼ Ἀγαμέμνων,
lines.english: so hear me yet again, and stay this fearful pestilence from the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his prayer. When they had done praying and sprinkling the barley-meal,…
lines.gloss: ἆσσον (comparative adv.) 'nearer, closer'; ἴτʼ = ἴτε (pres. imperative, 2nd pl. of εἶμι) 'come!'; ὔμμες (nom. pl., dual/plural pronoun) 'you two'; ἐπαίτιοι (nom. pl. masc. of ἐπαίτιος) 'responsible, to blame'; ἀλλʼ = ἀλλά 'but rather'; the construction οὔ τί … ἀλλʼ marks emphatic negation with contrast: 'not at all you, but Agamemnon.'

lines.original: ὃ σφῶϊ προΐει Βρισηΐδος εἵνεκα κούρης.
lines.english: so hear me yet again, and stay this fearful pestilence from the Danaans." Thus did he pray, and Apollo heard his prayer. When they had done praying and sprinkling the barley-meal,…
lines.gloss: ὃ (rel. pron., nom. sg. masc.) 'who'; σφῶϊ (dual acc./dat. of σφώ) 'you two'; προΐει (3rd sg. pres. of προΐημι) 'sends forth'; Βρισηΐδος (gen. sg. of Βρισηΐς) 'of Briseis'; εἵνεκα (prep. + gen.) 'on account of, for the sake of'; κούρης (gen. sg. of κούρη) 'girl, maiden'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγε διογενὲς Πατρόκλεες ἔξαγε κούρην
lines.english: They cut out the thigh-bones, wrapped them round in two layers of fat, set some pieces of raw meat on the top of them, and then Chryses laid them on the wood fire and poured wine…
lines.gloss: ἄγε (pres. imperative of ἄγω) 'come, come now'; διογενές (voc. sg. adj.) 'Zeus-born, sprung from Zeus'; Πατρόκλεες (voc. sg.) 'Patroclus'; ἔξαγε (aor. imperative of ἐξάγω) 'bring out, lead forth'; κούρην (acc. sg. of κούρη) 'girl, maiden' (referring to Briseis).

lines.original: καί σφωϊν δὸς ἄγειν· τὼ δʼ αὐτὼ μάρτυροι ἔστων
lines.english: They cut out the thigh-bones, wrapped them round in two layers of fat, set some pieces of raw meat on the top of them, and then Chryses laid them on the wood fire and poured wine…
lines.gloss: σφωϊν (dat. dual) 'to/for the two of them'; δός (aor. imperative of δίδωμι) 'give!'; ἄγειν (pres. inf.) 'to lead away'; τώ (nom. dual demonstrative) 'these two'; αὐτώ (nom. dual intensive) 'themselves'; μάρτυροι (nom. pl.) 'witnesses'; ἔστων (3rd pl. pres. imperative of εἰμί) 'let them be'.

lines.original: πρός τε θεῶν μακάρων πρός τε θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων
lines.english: They cut out the thigh-bones, wrapped them round in two layers of fat, set some pieces of raw meat on the top of them, and then Chryses laid them on the wood fire and poured wine…
lines.gloss: πρός (preposition + gen.) 'before, in the presence of'; θεῶν μακάρων (gen. pl.) 'blessed gods'; θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων (gen. pl.) 'mortal men'. The anaphoric πρός τε...πρός τε emphasizes the dual witness invoked, divine and human alike.

lines.original: καὶ πρὸς τοῦ βασιλῆος ἀπηνέος εἴ ποτε δʼ αὖτε
lines.english: They cut out the thigh-bones, wrapped them round in two layers of fat, set some pieces of raw meat on the top of them, and then Chryses laid them on the wood fire and poured wine…
lines.gloss: καὶ πρὸς τοῦ βασιλῆος (gen. sg. of βασιλεύς) 'from the king'; ἀπηνέος (gen. sg. of ἀπηνής) 'cruel, harsh, pitiless'; εἴ ποτε δʼ αὖτε 'if ever again' (εἴ 'if'; ποτε 'ever, at some time'; δέ (elided) 'and, but'; αὖτε 'again, in turn').

lines.original: χρειὼ ἐμεῖο γένηται ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι
lines.english: they cut the rest up small, put the pieces upon the spits, roasted them till they were done, and drew them off: then, when they had finished their work [] and the feast was ready,…
lines.gloss: χρειώ (nom. sg. of χρειώ) 'need, necessity'; ἐμεῖο (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'of me'; γένηται (aor. subj. mid. of γίγνομαι) 'should arise, come to be'; ἀεικέα (acc. sg. of ἀεικής) 'shameful, unseemly'; λοιγόν (acc. sg. of λοιγός) 'ruin, destruction'; ἀμῦναι (aor. inf. of ἀμύνω) 'to ward off, defend against.'

lines.original: τοῖς ἄλλοις· ἦ γὰρ ὅ γʼ ὀλοιῇσι φρεσὶ θύει,
lines.english: they cut the rest up small, put the pieces upon the spits, roasted them till they were done, and drew them off: then, when they had finished their work [] and the feast was ready,…
lines.gloss: τοῖς ἄλλοις (dat. pl. of ἄλλος) 'for the others'; ἦ γάρ 'for indeed, truly'; ὅ γε (nom. sg.) 'he' (emphatic); ὀλοιῇσι (dat. pl. of ὀλοός) 'with destructive, ruinous'; φρεσί (dat. pl. of φρήν) 'in his mind, with thoughts'; θύει (pres. indic.) 'rages, rushes furiously'.

lines.original: οὐδέ τι οἶδε νοῆσαι ἅμα πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω,
lines.english: they cut the rest up small, put the pieces upon the spits, roasted them till they were done, and drew them off: then, when they had finished their work [] and the feast was ready,…
lines.gloss: οἶδε (perf. with pres. meaning) 'he knows (how)'; νοῆσαι (aor. inf. of νοέω) 'to think, to plan'; ἅμα 'at once, together'; πρόσσω (adv.) 'forward, ahead'; ὀπίσσω (adv.) 'backward, behind' — the phrase means 'to plan both ahead and behind,' i.e., to think strategically in both directions.

lines.original: ὅππως οἱ παρὰ νηυσὶ σόοι μαχέοιντο Ἀχαιοί.
lines.english: they cut the rest up small, put the pieces upon the spits, roasted them till they were done, and drew them off: then, when they had finished their work [] and the feast was ready,…
lines.gloss: ὅππως (rel. adv.) 'how, in what way'; οἱ (dat. sg. pronoun) 'for him/to him' (ethical dative); παρὰ νηυσί (prep. + dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'beside the ships'; σόοι (nom. pl. masc. of σόος/σῶος) 'safe, unharmed'; μαχέοιντο (3rd pl. pres. opt. mid. of μάχομαι) 'might fight'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans.'

lines.original: μῆτερ ἐπεί μʼ ἔτεκές γε μινυνθάδιόν περ ἐόντα,
lines.english: they cut the rest up small, put the pieces upon the spits, roasted them till they were done, and drew them off: then, when they had finished their work [] and the feast was ready,…
lines.gloss: μῆτερ (voc. sg. of μήτηρ) 'mother'; ἐπεί (conj.) 'since'; ἔτεκες (2nd sg. aor. of τίκτω) 'you bore, gave birth to'; γε (particle) 'at least, indeed'; μινυνθάδιον (acc. sg. of μινυνθάδιος) 'short-lived'; περ (particle, concessive with participle) 'though, although'; ἐόντα (pres. participle acc. sg. of εἰμί) 'being'.

lines.original: τιμήν πέρ μοι ὄφελλεν Ὀλύμπιος ἐγγυαλίξαι
lines.english: pages filled the mixing-bowl with wine and water and handed it round, after giving every man his drink-offering. Thus all day long the young men worshipped the god with song,…
lines.gloss: τιμήν (acc. sg. of τιμή) 'honor, recompense'; ὄφελλεν (impf. of ὀφέλλω) 'ought to have, was obliged to'; Ὀλύμπιος 'the Olympian' (epithet of Zeus); ἐγγυαλίξαι (aor. inf. of ἐγγυαλίζω) 'to grant, bestow'.

lines.original: Ζεὺς ὑψιβρεμέτης· νῦν δʼ οὐδέ με τυτθὸν ἔτισεν·
lines.english: pages filled the mixing-bowl with wine and water and handed it round, after giving every man his drink-offering. Thus all day long the young men worshipped the god with song,…
lines.gloss: Ζεὺς ὑψιβρεμέτης (nom. sg.) 'high-thundering Zeus'; νῦν δέ 'but now'; οὐδέ 'not even'; με (acc. sg.) 'me'; τυτθὸν (adverbial acc.) 'a little, at all'; ἔτισεν (aor. indic. 3rd sg. of τίω) 'honored, valued'.

lines.original: ἦ γάρ μʼ Ἀτρεΐδης εὐρὺ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: pages filled the mixing-bowl with wine and water and handed it round, after giving every man his drink-offering. Thus all day long the young men worshipped the god with song,…
lines.gloss: ἦ (particle) 'truly, indeed' (emphatic); γάρ (particle) 'for'; μʼ = με (acc. sg. of ἐγώ) 'me'; Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Atreus'; εὐρὺ κρείων (nom. sg. participle phrase) 'wide-ruling, ruling over a broad domain'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) 'Agamemnon' (in apposition).

lines.original: ἠτίμησεν· ἑλὼν γὰρ ἔχει γέρας αὐτὸς ἀπούρας.
lines.english: pages filled the mixing-bowl with wine and water and handed it round, after giving every man his drink-offering. Thus all day long the young men worshipped the god with song,…
lines.gloss: ἠτίμησεν (aor. act. indic., 3rd sg. of ἀτιμάω) 'dishonored, treated without honor'; ἑλών (aor. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. of αἱρέω) 'having taken, seized'; γέρας (acc. sg. neut.) 'prize of honor, war-prize'; ἀπούρας (aor. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. of ἀπαυράω) 'having taken away, deprived'.

lines.original: τέκνον τί κλαίεις; τί δέ σε φρένας ἵκετο πένθος;
lines.english: pages filled the mixing-bowl with wine and water and handed it round, after giving every man his drink-offering. Thus all day long the young men worshipped the god with song,…
lines.gloss: τέκνον (voc. sg. of τέκνον) 'child'; τί (interrog. acc.) 'why?'; κλαίεις (2nd sg. pres. indic. of κλαίω) 'are you weeping?'; φρένας (acc. pl. of φρήν) 'heart, mind' (object of ἵκετο); ἵκετο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of ἱκνέομαι) 'has come to, reached'; πένθος (nom. sg. of πένθος) 'grief, sorrow.'

lines.original: ἐξαύδα, μὴ κεῦθε νόῳ, ἵνα εἴδομεν ἄμφω.
lines.english: but when the sun went down, and it came on dark, they laid themselves down to sleep by the stern cables of the ship, and when the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared…
lines.gloss: ἐξαύδα (pres. imperative of ἐξαυδάω) 'speak out, declare'; κεῦθε (pres. imperative of κεύθω) 'hide, conceal'; νόῳ (dat. sg. of νόος) 'in mind/heart'; ἵνα 'so that' (purpose clause); εἴδομεν (1st pl. perf. subjunctive of οἶδα) 'we may know'; ἄμφω 'both (of us)'.

lines.original: οἶσθα· τί ἤ τοι ταῦτα ἰδυίῃ πάντʼ ἀγορεύω;
lines.english: but when the sun went down, and it came on dark, they laid themselves down to sleep by the stern cables of the ship, and when the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared…
lines.gloss: οἶσθα (2nd sg. perf. of οἶδα) 'you know'; τί (acc. sg. neut. of τίς) 'why?'; ἤ (particle) 'indeed, truly'; τοι (ethical dative of σύ) 'I tell you'; ἰδυίῃ (fem. dat. sg. pres. participle of ἴδμεν) 'to you who know'; πάντʼ (acc. pl. neut. of πᾶς, elided) 'all things'; ἀγορεύω (1st sg. pres.) 'do I speak, relate'.

lines.original: ᾠχόμεθʼ ἐς Θήβην ἱερὴν πόλιν Ἠετίωνος,
lines.english: but when the sun went down, and it came on dark, they laid themselves down to sleep by the stern cables of the ship, and when the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared…
lines.gloss: ᾠχόμεθα (1st pl. aor. of οἴχομαι) 'we went, we came'; ἐς (+ acc.) 'to, toward'; Θήβην (acc. sg.) 'Thebe' (Cilician city); ἱερήν (acc. sg. fem. of ἱερός) 'holy, sacred'; πόλιν (acc. sg. of πόλις) 'city'; Ἠετίωνος (gen. sg.) 'of Eëtion' (Andromache's father).

lines.original: τὴν δὲ διεπράθομέν τε καὶ ἤγομεν ἐνθάδε πάντα·
lines.english: but when the sun went down, and it came on dark, they laid themselves down to sleep by the stern cables of the ship, and when the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared…
lines.gloss: τὴν (acc. sg. fem. demonstrative pronoun) 'that [city]'; διεπράθομεν (1st pl. aor. of διαπέρθω) 'we sacked, utterly destroyed'; ἤγομεν (1st pl. impf. of ἄγω) 'we brought, led'; ἐνθάδε (adv.) 'hither, here'; πάντα (acc. pl. neut.) 'all things, everything [plundered]'.

lines.original: καὶ τὰ μὲν εὖ δάσσαντο μετὰ σφίσιν υἷες Ἀχαιῶν,
lines.english: but when the sun went down, and it came on dark, they laid themselves down to sleep by the stern cables of the ship, and when the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared…
lines.gloss: τὰ μέν (neut. pl. acc.) 'those things' (the spoils); εὖ (adverb) 'well, fairly'; δάσσαντο (3rd pl. aor. mid. of δατέομαι) 'they divided, apportioned'; μετὰ σφίσιν 'among themselves' (σφίσιν reflexive dat. pl.); υἷες Ἀχαιῶν 'sons of the Achaeans' (nominative subject).

lines.original: ἐκ δʼ ἕλον Ἀτρεΐδῃ Χρυσηΐδα καλλιπάρῃον.
lines.english: so they raised their mast and hoisted their white sails aloft. As the sail bellied with the wind the ship flew through the seething deep water, and the foam hissed against her…
lines.gloss: ἐκ δ(έ) 'out, from among (the spoils)'; ἕλον (3rd pl. aor. of αἱρέω) 'they took, chose'; Ἀτρεΐδῃ (dat. sg.) 'for the son of Atreus (Agamemnon)'; Χρυσηΐδα (acc. sg.) 'Chryseis (daughter of Chryses)'; καλλιπάρῃον (acc. sg. f. of καλλιπάρῃος) 'fair-cheeked, lovely-cheeked'.

lines.original: Χρύσης δʼ αὖθʼ ἱερεὺς ἑκατηβόλου Ἀπόλλωνος
lines.english: so they raised their mast and hoisted their white sails aloft. As the sail bellied with the wind the ship flew through the seething deep water, and the foam hissed against her…
lines.gloss: Χρύσης (nom. sg.) 'Chryses' (a priest, father of Chryseis); ἱερεύς (nom. sg.) 'priest'; ἑκατηβόλου (gen. sg. of ἑκατηβόλος) 'far-shooting, far-darting,' epithet of Apollo; Ἀπόλλωνος (gen. sg.) 'of Apollo.'

lines.original: ἦλθε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων
lines.english: so they raised their mast and hoisted their white sails aloft. As the sail bellied with the wind the ship flew through the seething deep water, and the foam hissed against her…
lines.gloss: ἦλθε (3rd sg. aor. of ἔρχομαι) 'came, went'; θοὰς (acc. pl. fem. of θοός) 'swift'; ἐπί (prep. + acc.) 'to, toward'; νῆας (acc. pl. of ναῦς) 'ships'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans/Greeks'; χαλκοχιτώνων (gen. pl. of χαλκοχίτων) 'bronze-armored' (lit. 'bronze-tunicked').

lines.original: λυσόμενός τε θύγατρα φέρων τʼ ἀπερείσιʼ ἄποινα,
lines.english: so they raised their mast and hoisted their white sails aloft. As the sail bellied with the wind the ship flew through the seething deep water, and the foam hissed against her…
lines.gloss: λυσόμενος (fut. mid. participle of λύω) 'intending to ransom, about to release'; θύγατρα (acc. sg. of θυγάτηρ) 'daughter'; φέρων (pres. participle of φέρω) 'bringing, carrying'; ἀπερείσι᾽ (acc. pl. neut. of ἀπερείσιος) 'countless, boundless'; ἄποινα (acc. pl. neut. of ἄποινον) 'ransom-gifts, recompense'.

lines.original: στέμματʼ ἔχων ἐν χερσὶν ἑκηβόλου Ἀπόλλωνος
lines.english: so they raised their mast and hoisted their white sails aloft. As the sail bellied with the wind the ship flew through the seething deep water, and the foam hissed against her…
lines.gloss: στέμματα (acc. pl. of στέμμα) 'fillets, sacred headbands'; ἔχων (pres. participle) 'holding'; ἐν χερσίν (dat. pl.) 'in his hands'; ἑκηβόλου (gen. sg. epithet) 'far-shooting'; Ἀπόλλωνος (gen. sg.) 'of Apollo' — the priest holds Apollo's sacred fillets to signify his religious authority.

lines.original: χρυσέῳ ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ, καὶ λίσσετο πάντας Ἀχαιούς,
lines.english: they drew the vessel ashore, high and dry upon the sands, set her strong props beneath her, and went their ways to their own tents and ships. But Achilles stayed at his ships and…
lines.gloss: χρυσέῳ (dat. sg. of χρύσεος) 'golden'; ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ (dat. sg. of σκῆπτρον with ἀνά) 'on/upon a staff, scepter'; λίσσετο (imperf. mid. of λίσσομαι) 'he beseeched, entreated'; πάντας Ἀχαιούς (acc. pl.) 'all the Achaeans.'

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδα δὲ μάλιστα δύω κοσμήτορε λαῶν.
lines.english: they drew the vessel ashore, high and dry upon the sands, set her strong props beneath her, and went their ways to their own tents and ships. But Achilles stayed at his ships and…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδα (acc. dual of Ἀτρεΐδης) 'the two sons of Atreus' (Agamemnon and Menelaus); δύω (acc. dual) 'two'; κοσμήτορε (acc. dual of κοσμήτωρ) 'marshals, commanders'; λαῶν (gen. pl. of λαός) 'of the hosts, of the people.'

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ἄλλοι μὲν πάντες ἐπευφήμησαν Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: they drew the vessel ashore, high and dry upon the sands, set her strong props beneath her, and went their ways to their own tents and ships. But Achilles stayed at his ships and…
lines.gloss: ἔνθα 'then, thereupon'; ἄλλοι μὲν πάντες 'all the others' (nom. pl., contrasted with following δέ clause); ἐπευφήμησαν (aor. ind. of ἐπιφημίζω) 'shouted assent, approved'; Ἀχαιοί (nom. pl.) 'the Achaeans, Greeks'.

lines.original: αἰδεῖσθαί θʼ ἱερῆα καὶ ἀγλαὰ δέχθαι ἄποινα·
lines.english: they drew the vessel ashore, high and dry upon the sands, set her strong props beneath her, and went their ways to their own tents and ships. But Achilles stayed at his ships and…
lines.gloss: αἰδεῖσθαί (pres. mid./pass. infin. of αἰδέομαι) 'to respect, revere'; θʼ (= τε) enclitic conjunction 'and'; ἱερῆα (acc. sg. of ἱερεύς) 'priest'; ἀγλαὰ (acc. pl. neut. of ἀγλαός) 'splendid, glorious'; δέχθαι (aor. mid. infin. of δέχομαι) 'to accept, receive'; ἄποινα (acc. pl. neut. of ἄποινον) 'ransom'.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ οὐκ Ἀτρεΐδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονι ἥνδανε θυμῷ,
lines.english: they drew the vessel ashore, high and dry upon the sands, set her strong props beneath her, and went their ways to their own tents and ships. But Achilles stayed at his ships and…
lines.gloss: ἀλλʼ (conjunction) 'but'; οὐκ (negative particle) 'not'; Ἀτρεΐδῃ (dat. sg. of Ἀτρεΐδης) 'to the son of Atreus'; Ἀγαμέμνονι (dat. sg.) 'to Agamemnon' (in apposition); ἥνδανε (3rd sg. impf. of ἁνδάνω) 'it pleased'; θυμῷ (dat. sg. of θυμός) 'in his heart/spirit' (dat. of respect).

lines.original: ἀλλὰ κακῶς ἀφίει, κρατερὸν δʼ ἐπὶ μῦθον ἔτελλε·
lines.english: He went not to the honorable assembly, and sallied not forth to fight, but gnawed at his own heart, pining for battle and the war-cry. Now after twelve days the immortal gods came…
lines.gloss: ἀφίει (3rd sg. impf. of ἀφίημι) 'he sent away, dismissed'; κακῶς (adv.) 'harshly, rudely'; κρατερόν (acc. sg. masc. of κρατερός) 'strong, harsh'; μῦθον (acc. sg. of μῦθος) 'word, speech'; ἔτελλε (3rd sg. impf. of τέλλω) 'he laid upon, commanded'.

lines.original: χωόμενος δʼ ὁ γέρων πάλιν ᾤχετο· τοῖο δʼ Ἀπόλλων
lines.english: He went not to the honorable assembly, and sallied not forth to fight, but gnawed at his own heart, pining for battle and the war-cry. Now after twelve days the immortal gods came…
lines.gloss: χωόμενος (pres. middle participle, nom. sg.) 'being angry, enraged'; γέρων (nom. sg.) 'old man' (i.e., Chryses); πάλιν 'back, again'; ᾤχετο (aor. indic. 3rd sg. of οἴχομαι) 'he went, departed'; τοῖο (gen. sg. demonstrative/possessive pronoun) 'his, of him'; Ἀπόλλων (nom. sg.) 'Apollo.'

lines.original: εὐξαμένου ἤκουσεν, ἐπεὶ μάλα οἱ φίλος ἦεν,
lines.english: He went not to the honorable assembly, and sallied not forth to fight, but gnawed at his own heart, pining for battle and the war-cry. Now after twelve days the immortal gods came…
lines.gloss: εὐξαμένου (aor. mid. participle, gen. sg.) 'having prayed, of the one praying' (Chryses); ἤκουσεν (aor. of ἀκούω) 'heard'; ἐπεὶ 'since, because'; μάλα 'very much, greatly'; οἱ (dat. sg. pronoun) 'to him'; φίλος (nom. sg.) 'dear, beloved'; ἦεν (impf. of εἰμί) 'he was.'

lines.original: ἧκε δʼ ἐπʼ Ἀργείοισι κακὸν βέλος· οἳ δέ νυ λαοὶ
lines.english: He went not to the honorable assembly, and sallied not forth to fight, but gnawed at his own heart, pining for battle and the war-cry. Now after twelve days the immortal gods came…
lines.gloss: ἧκε (aor. of ἵημι) 'he sent, hurled'; ἐπί (+ dat.) 'against, upon'; Ἀργείοισι (dat. pl.) 'the Argives, Greeks'; κακὸν βέλος (acc. sg.) 'evil arrow/shaft'; οἳ δέ (nom. pl.) 'and they'; νυ (particle) 'now, then' (often enclitic, adds emphasis); λαοὶ (nom. pl.) 'people, warriors.'

lines.original: θνῇσκον ἐπασσύτεροι, τὰ δʼ ἐπῴχετο κῆλα θεοῖο
lines.english: He went not to the honorable assembly, and sallied not forth to fight, but gnawed at his own heart, pining for battle and the war-cry. Now after twelve days the immortal gods came…
lines.gloss: θνῇσκον (impf. 3rd pl. of θνῄσκω) 'were dying'; ἐπασσύτεροι (nom. pl. masc., comparative of ἐπασσύτερος) 'one after another, in quick succession'; τά (nom./acc. pl. neut. of ὁ) 'the things' (article); ἐπῴχετο (impf. 3rd sg. of ἐποίχομαι) 'went to and fro, ranged over'; κῆλα (nom./acc. pl. neut. of κῆλον) 'arrows, shafts'; θεοῖο (gen. sg. of θεός, epic form) 'of the god'.

lines.original: πάντῃ ἀνὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν· ἄμμι δὲ μάντις
lines.english: and Zeus led the way. Thetis was not unmindful of the charge her son had laid upon her, so she rose from under the sea and went, enveloped in mist, through great heaven with early…
lines.gloss: πάντῃ (adv.) 'everywhere, in all directions'; ἀνὰ στρατόν (acc. sg. with ἀνά) 'throughout the camp'; εὐρύν (acc. sg. of εὐρύς) 'wide, broad'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans'; ἄμμι (dat. pl., equivalent to ἡμῖν) 'to/for us'; δέ 'and, but'; μάντις (nom. sg.) 'seer, prophet.'

lines.original: εὖ εἰδὼς ἀγόρευε θεοπροπίας ἑκάτοιο.
lines.english: and Zeus led the way. Thetis was not unmindful of the charge her son had laid upon her, so she rose from under the sea and went, enveloped in mist, through great heaven with early…
lines.gloss: εὖ (adverb) 'well, clearly'; εἰδώς (perfect active participle of οἶδα, nom. sg. masc.) 'knowing'; ἀγόρευε (imperfect, 3rd sg.) 'spoke, declared'; θεοπροπίας (acc. pl. of θεοπροπίη) 'divine prophecies, oracles'; ἑκάτοιο (gen. sg. of ἑκάτος, epithet of Apollo) 'of the far-shooter'.

lines.original: αὐτίκʼ ἐγὼ πρῶτος κελόμην θεὸν ἱλάσκεσθαι·
lines.english: and Zeus led the way. Thetis was not unmindful of the charge her son had laid upon her, so she rose from under the sea and went, enveloped in mist, through great heaven with early…
lines.gloss: αὐτίκα (adv.) 'immediately, at once'; πρῶτος (nom. sg. masc.) 'first'; κελόμην (aor. mid. 1st sg. of κέλομαι) 'I urged, commanded'; ἱλάσκεσθαι (pres. mid./pass. inf. of ἱλάσκομαι) 'to propitiate, appease' (the god, Apollo).

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐωνα δʼ ἔπειτα χόλος λάβεν, αἶψα δʼ ἀναστὰς
lines.english: and Zeus led the way. Thetis was not unmindful of the charge her son had laid upon her, so she rose from under the sea and went, enveloped in mist, through great heaven with early…
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐωνα (acc. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (i.e., Agamemnon); χόλος (nom. sg.) 'wrath, anger'; λάβεν (aor. of λαμβάνω) 'seized'; ἀναστάς (aor. participle of ἀνίστημι) 'rising up, standing up'.

lines.original: ἠπείλησεν μῦθον ὃ δὴ τετελεσμένος ἐστί·
lines.english: and Zeus led the way. Thetis was not unmindful of the charge her son had laid upon her, so she rose from under the sea and went, enveloped in mist, through great heaven with early…
lines.gloss: ἠπείλησεν (aor. indic. 3rd sg. of ἀπειλέω) 'he threatened, made a threat'; μῦθον (acc. sg. of μῦθος) 'speech, word'; ὃ δή (relative pronoun + particle) 'which indeed'; τετελεσμένος (perf. pass. participle of τελέω) 'having been fulfilled, accomplished'; ἐστί (pres. indic. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) 'is.'

lines.original: τὴν μὲν γὰρ σὺν νηῒ θοῇ ἑλίκωπες Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: She sat herself down before him, and with her left hand seized his knees, while with her right she caught him under the chin, and besought him, saying - "Father Zeus, if I ever…
lines.gloss: τὴν μέν (acc. sg. fem. demonstrative pronoun) 'her' (i.e., Chryseis); σὺν νηῒ θοῇ (dat. sg.) 'with/in a swift ship'; ἑλίκωπες (nom. pl. adj.) 'with rolling/flashing eyes,' epithet of Ἀχαιοί 'the Achaeans.' The μέν ... δέ construction (continued in the next line) contrasts her departure with what follows.

lines.original: ἐς Χρύσην πέμπουσιν, ἄγουσι δὲ δῶρα ἄνακτι·
lines.english: She sat herself down before him, and with her left hand seized his knees, while with her right she caught him under the chin, and besought him, saying - "Father Zeus, if I ever…
lines.gloss: ἐς Χρύσην: "to Chryse" (acc., town of the priest Chryses); πέμπουσιν (3rd pl. pres.) "they are sending"; ἄγουσι (3rd pl. pres.) "they bring/lead"; δῶρα (acc. pl. neut. of δῶρον) "gifts"; ἄνακτι (dat. sg. of ἄναξ) "to the lord" (i.e., Apollo).

lines.original: τὴν δὲ νέον κλισίηθεν ἔβαν κήρυκες ἄγοντες
lines.english: She sat herself down before him, and with her left hand seized his knees, while with her right she caught him under the chin, and besought him, saying - "Father Zeus, if I ever…
lines.gloss: τὴν (acc. sg. fem. of ὁ, ἡ, τό) 'her'; νέον (adv.) 'just now, recently'; κλισίηθεν (adv. from κλισίη) 'from the hut/shelter'; ἔβαν (3rd pl. aor. of βαίνω) 'they went'; κήρυκες (nom. pl. of κῆρυξ) 'heralds'; ἄγοντες (pres. part. nom. pl. masc. of ἄγω) 'leading, taking'.

lines.original: κούρην Βρισῆος τήν μοι δόσαν υἷες Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: She sat herself down before him, and with her left hand seized his knees, while with her right she caught him under the chin, and besought him, saying - "Father Zeus, if I ever…
lines.gloss: κούρην (acc. sg. of κούρη) 'girl, maiden'; Βρισῆος (gen. sg.) 'of Briseus' (patronymic, referring to Briseis); τήν (acc. sg. fem. relative pronoun) 'whom'; δόσαν (3rd pl. aorist of δίδωμι) 'gave'; υἷες Ἀχαιῶν 'sons of the Achaeans' (i.e., the Greek leaders).

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σὺ εἰ δύνασαί γε περίσχεο παιδὸς ἑῆος·
lines.english: She sat herself down before him, and with her left hand seized his knees, while with her right she caught him under the chin, and besought him, saying - "Father Zeus, if I ever…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but, yet' (transition); σύ (nom.) 'you' (emphatic); εἰ δύνασαι 'if you are able' (pres. mid. indic.); γε (enclitic particle) 'at least, indeed' (emphasizing the condition); περίσχεο (aor. mid. imperative, 2nd sg. of περιέχω) 'protect, embrace, stand by'; παιδὸς ἑῆος (gen. sg.) 'your child' (objective gen.).

lines.original: ἐλθοῦσʼ Οὔλυμπον δὲ Δία λίσαι, εἴ ποτε δή τι
lines.english: and do honor to my son, whose life is to be cut short so early. King Agamemnon has dishonored him by taking his prize and keeping her. Honor him then yourself, Olympian lord of…
lines.gloss: ἐλθοῦσα (aor. participle, nom. sg. fem. of ἔρχομαι) 'having gone, going'; Οὔλυμπον (acc. sg.) 'Olympus'; λίσαι (aor. infinitive of λίσσομαι) 'to beseech, supplicate'; εἴ ποτε δή τι 'if ever at all in anything' (a common collocation expressing past benefaction).

lines.original: ἢ ἔπει ὤνησας κραδίην Διὸς ἠὲ καὶ ἔργῳ.
lines.english: and do honor to my son, whose life is to be cut short so early. King Agamemnon has dishonored him by taking his prize and keeping her. Honor him then yourself, Olympian lord of…
lines.gloss: ἢ (conj.) 'either'; ἔπει (dat. sg. of ἔπος) 'by word, with a word'; ὤνησας (aor. of ὀνίνημι) 'you helped, benefited'; κραδίην (acc. sg. of κραδίη) 'heart'; Διός (gen. sg. of Ζεύς) 'of Zeus'; ἠέ (conj.) 'or'; ἔργῳ (dat. sg. of ἔργον) 'by deed, with action.'

lines.original: πολλάκι γάρ σεο πατρὸς ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν ἄκουσα
lines.english: and do honor to my son, whose life is to be cut short so early. King Agamemnon has dishonored him by taking his prize and keeping her. Honor him then yourself, Olympian lord of…
lines.gloss: πολλάκι (adv.) 'often, many times'; γάρ (particle) 'for'; σεο (gen. sg. of σύ) 'of you, your'; πατρὸς (gen. sg. of πατήρ) 'of (my) father'; ἐνὶ (= ἐν, preposition + dat.) 'in'; μεγάροισιν (dat. pl. of μέγαρον) 'in the halls, palace'; ἄκουσα (1st sg. aor. of ἀκούω) 'I heard'.

lines.original: εὐχομένης ὅτʼ ἔφησθα κελαινεφέϊ Κρονίωνι
lines.english: and do honor to my son, whose life is to be cut short so early. King Agamemnon has dishonored him by taking his prize and keeping her. Honor him then yourself, Olympian lord of…
lines.gloss: εὐχομένης (pres. mid. participle, gen. sg. fem.) 'boasting, praying' (agrees with an implied "her," Thetis); ὅτʼ = ὅτε 'when'; ἔφησθα (2nd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί) 'you claimed, you said'; κελαινεφέϊ (dat. sg. masc. of κελαινεφής) 'dark-clouded,' an epithet; Κρονίωνι (dat. sg. of Κρονίων) 'son of Kronos,' i.e., Zeus.

lines.original: οἴη ἐν ἀθανάτοισιν ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι,
lines.english: and do honor to my son, whose life is to be cut short so early. King Agamemnon has dishonored him by taking his prize and keeping her. Honor him then yourself, Olympian lord of…
lines.gloss: οἴη (fem. nom. sg. of οἶος) 'alone, only'; ἐν ἀθανάτοισιν (dat. pl. of ἀθάνατος) 'among the immortals'; ἀεικέα (acc. sg. of ἀεικής) 'unseemly, shameful'; λοιγόν (acc. sg. of λοιγός) 'ruin, destruction'; ἀμῦναι (aor. inf. of ἀμύνω) 'to ward off, avert.'

lines.original: ὁππότε μιν ξυνδῆσαι Ὀλύμπιοι ἤθελον ἄλλοι
lines.english: give my son his due and load him with riches in requital []." Zeus sat for a while silent, and without a word, but Thetis still kept firm hold of his knees, and besought him a…
lines.gloss: ὁππότε (temporal conjunction) 'when, at the time when'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him' (referring to Zeus); ξυνδῆσαι (aor. inf. of συνδέω) 'to bind together, fetter'; Ὀλύμπιοι (nom. pl. adj.) 'the Olympian gods'; ἤθελον (imperf. of ἐθέλω) 'wished, wanted'; ἄλλοι (nom. pl.) 'the others, the rest'.

lines.original: Ἥρη τʼ ἠδὲ Ποσειδάων καὶ Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: give my son his due and load him with riches in requital []." Zeus sat for a while silent, and without a word, but Thetis still kept firm hold of his knees, and besought him a…
lines.gloss: Ἥρη (nom. sg.) 'Hera'; τ(ε)... ἠδὲ... καί 'both... and... and' (correlative conjunctions linking three subjects); Ποσειδάων (nom. sg.) 'Poseidon'; Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη (nom. sg.) 'Pallas Athena' (the three Olympian gods who attempted to bind Zeus).

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σὺ τόν γʼ ἐλθοῦσα θεὰ ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν,
lines.english: give my son his due and load him with riches in requital []." Zeus sat for a while silent, and without a word, but Thetis still kept firm hold of his knees, and besought him a…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but'; σύ (nom. sg.) 'you' (Thetis); τόν (acc. sg. masc.) 'him' (Zeus); ἐλθοῦσα (aor. fem. nom. sg. participle of ἔρχομαι) 'having come, going'; θεά (voc. sg.) 'goddess'; ὑπελύσαο (aor. mid. 2nd sg. of ὑπολύω) 'you released, freed'; δεσμῶν (gen. pl. of δεσμός) 'from bonds, fetters.'

lines.original: ὦχʼ ἑκατόγχειρον καλέσασʼ ἐς μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον,
lines.english: give my son his due and load him with riches in requital []." Zeus sat for a while silent, and without a word, but Thetis still kept firm hold of his knees, and besought him a…
lines.gloss: ὦχʼ (= ᾤχετο, aor. of οἴχομαι) 'she went'; ἑκατόγχειρον (acc. sg. of ἑκατόγχειρος) 'the hundred-handed one'; καλέσασʼ (= καλέσασα, aor. fem. participle of καλέω) 'having summoned'; μακρόν (acc. sg. of μακρός, here as adverbial adjective with Ὄλυμπον) 'lofty, high.'

lines.original: ὃν Βριάρεων καλέουσι θεοί, ἄνδρες δέ τε πάντες
lines.english: give my son his due and load him with riches in requital []." Zeus sat for a while silent, and without a word, but Thetis still kept firm hold of his knees, and besought him a…
lines.gloss: ὃν (acc. sg. relative pronoun) 'whom'; Βριάρεων (acc. sg.) 'Briareus' (proper name); καλέουσι (3rd pl. pres. act.) 'call'; θεοί (nom. pl.) 'the gods'; ἄνδρες (nom. pl.) 'men'; δέ τε 'but/and indeed'; πάντες (nom. pl. masc.) 'all'.

lines.original: Αἰγαίωνʼ, ὃ γὰρ αὖτε βίην οὗ πατρὸς ἀμείνων·
lines.english: or else deny me - for you have nothing to fear - that I may learn how greatly you disdain me." At this Zeus was much troubled and answered, "I shall have trouble if you set me…
lines.gloss: Αἰγαίωνα (acc. sg.) 'Aegaeon,' the mortal name for Briareus; αὖτε 'in turn, moreover'; βίην (acc. sg. of βίη) 'strength, might'; οὗ πατρός (gen. sg.) 'than his father'; ἀμείνων (comparative adj., nom. sg.) 'stronger, better.'

lines.original: ὅς ῥα παρὰ Κρονίωνι καθέζετο κύδεϊ γαίων·
lines.english: or else deny me - for you have nothing to fear - that I may learn how greatly you disdain me." At this Zeus was much troubled and answered, "I shall have trouble if you set me…
lines.gloss: ὅς (nom. sg. relative pronoun) 'who'; ῥα (particle) emphasizing narrative; παρά (+ dat.) 'beside'; Κρονίωνι (dat. sg. of Κρονίων) 'son of Kronos' (Zeus); καθέζετο (3rd sg. aor. mid. of καθέζομαι) 'sat down'; κύδεϊ (dat. sg. of κῦδος) 'in glory, with pride'; γαίων (nom. sg. pres. participle of γαίω) 'exulting, rejoicing'.

lines.original: τὸν καὶ ὑπέδεισαν μάκαρες θεοὶ οὐδʼ ἔτʼ ἔδησαν.
lines.english: or else deny me - for you have nothing to fear - that I may learn how greatly you disdain me." At this Zeus was much troubled and answered, "I shall have trouble if you set me…
lines.gloss: ὑπέδεισαν (3rd pl. aor. of ὑποδείδω) 'feared, stood in awe of'; μάκαρες (nom. pl. masc. of μάκαρ) 'blessed, happy' (epithet of gods); ἔδησαν (3rd pl. aor. of δέω) 'bound, fettered'; the negative οὐδέ 'nor, and not' with ἔτι 'further, any longer' emphasizes they did not proceed to bind him.

lines.original: τῶν νῦν μιν μνήσασα παρέζεο καὶ λαβὲ γούνων
lines.english: or else deny me - for you have nothing to fear - that I may learn how greatly you disdain me." At this Zeus was much troubled and answered, "I shall have trouble if you set me…
lines.gloss: τῶν (gen. pl. of ὅδε/οὗτος) 'of these things'; μιν (acc. sg. of ἕ, enclitic personal pronoun) 'him'; μνήσασα (aor. participle fem. of μιμνῄσκω) 'reminding, calling to mind'; παρέζεο (aor. imperative of παρέζομαι) 'sit beside'; λαβὲ (aor. imperative of λαμβάνω) 'grasp, take hold of'; γούνων (gen. pl. of γόνυ) 'knees' (the gesture of supplication).

lines.original: αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι,
lines.english: or else deny me - for you have nothing to fear - that I may learn how greatly you disdain me." At this Zeus was much troubled and answered, "I shall have trouble if you set me…
lines.gloss: αἴ κέν (with subj.) 'if perhaps, if perchance'; ἐθέλῃσιν (pres. subj. 3rd sg. of ἐθέλω) 'he may be willing'; ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν (dat. pl.) 'for/on behalf of the Trojans'; ἀρῆξαι (aor. inf. of ἀρήγω) 'to aid, to help'.

lines.original: τοὺς δὲ κατὰ πρύμνας τε καὶ ἀμφʼ ἅλα ἔλσαι Ἀχαιοὺς
lines.english: even now she is always railing at me before the other gods and accusing me of giving aid to the Trojans. Go back now, lest she should find out. I will consider the matter, and…
lines.gloss: τοὺς δέ (acc. pl. masc., resumptive) 'them, the Achaeans'; κατὰ πρύμνας 'to/at the sterns (of the ships)'; ἔλσαι (aor. inf. of εἴλω/ἐλάω) 'to pen in, compress, drive'; ἀμφ᾽ ἅλα 'around/beside the sea'; the line depicts the Achaeans being hemmed in at their ships' sterns, along the shoreline.

lines.original: κτεινομένους, ἵνα πάντες ἐπαύρωνται βασιλῆος,
lines.english: even now she is always railing at me before the other gods and accusing me of giving aid to the Trojans. Go back now, lest she should find out. I will consider the matter, and…
lines.gloss: κτεινομένους (pres. pass. participle, acc. pl. masc.) 'being slain'; ἵνα (conj.) 'so that, in order that' (purpose clause); πάντες (nom. pl. masc. of πᾶς) 'all'; ἐπαύρωνται (pres. mid. subj., 3rd pl.) 'may enjoy, benefit from'; βασιλῆος (gen. sg. of βασιλεύς) 'of the king' (i.e., Agamemnon).

lines.original: γνῷ δὲ καὶ Ἀτρεΐδης εὐρὺ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: even now she is always railing at me before the other gods and accusing me of giving aid to the Trojans. Go back now, lest she should find out. I will consider the matter, and…
lines.gloss: γνῷ (3rd sg. aor. subj. of γιγνώσκω) 'may know, recognize'; Ἀτρεΐδης (nom. sg.) 'son of Atreus' (= Agamemnon); εὐρὺ κρείων (nom. sg. masc. participle phrase) 'ruling widely, wide-ruling'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) proper name in apposition.

lines.original: ἣν ἄτην ὅ τʼ ἄριστον Ἀχαιῶν οὐδὲν ἔτισεν.
lines.english: even now she is always railing at me before the other gods and accusing me of giving aid to the Trojans. Go back now, lest she should find out. I will consider the matter, and…
lines.gloss: ἣν ἄτην (acc. sg. of ἄτη) 'the folly, ruinous delusion'; ὅ τ(ε) (relative pronoun) 'which'; ἄριστον (acc. sg. superlative) 'the best man'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl.) 'of the Achaeans'; οὐδὲν 'not at all, in no way'; ἔτισεν (aor. of τίω) 'he honored, made amends for'.

lines.original: ὤ μοι τέκνον ἐμόν, τί νύ σʼ ἔτρεφον αἰνὰ τεκοῦσα;
lines.english: even now she is always railing at me before the other gods and accusing me of giving aid to the Trojans. Go back now, lest she should find out. I will consider the matter, and…
lines.gloss: ὤ μοι 'woe is me!' (exclamation of grief); τέκνον (voc. sg. of τέκνον) 'child'; ἐμόν (possessive adj., voc. sg.) 'my'; τί (interrogative adv.) 'why?'; νύ (enclitic particle) emphasizing the question; σʼ = σε (acc. of σύ) 'you'; ἔτρεφον (1st sg. aor. of τρέφω) 'did I rear, nourish'; αἰνὰ τεκοῦσα (nom. sg. fem. aor. participle of τίκτω) 'having borne [you] to sorrow/misery,' with αἰνά (acc.

lines.original: αἴθʼ ὄφελες παρὰ νηυσὶν ἀδάκρυτος καὶ ἀπήμων
lines.english: See, I nod my head that you believe me. This is the most solemn act that I can offer to any god. I never recall my word, or deceive, or fail to do what I say, when I have nodded…
lines.gloss: αἴθε (particle) 'would that, if only' (expressing unfulfilled wish); ὄφελες (2nd sg. aor. of ὀφείλω used as imperfect in wishes) 'you ought to have been, would that you were'; ἀδάκρυτος (nom. sg. masc.) 'without tears, unwept'; ἀπήμων (nom. sg. masc.) 'without suffering, unharmed.'

lines.original: ἧσθαι, ἐπεί νύ τοι αἶσα μίνυνθά περ οὔ τι μάλα δήν·
lines.english: See, I nod my head that you believe me. This is the most solemn act that I can offer to any god. I never recall my word, or deceive, or fail to do what I say, when I have nodded…
lines.gloss: ἧσθαι (pres. inf. of ἧμαι) 'to sit, remain'; ἐπεί 'since'; νύ (intensifying particle) 'indeed'; τοι (dat. sg. of σύ, ethical dative) 'for you'; αἶσα (nom. sg.) 'fate, destiny'; μίνυνθά (adv.) 'short-lived, brief'; περ (particle, with concessive force) 'although, even'; οὔ τι μάλα δήν (adverbial phrase) 'not at all for long, not very long'.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ἅμα τʼ ὠκύμορος καὶ ὀϊζυρὸς περὶ πάντων
lines.english: See, I nod my head that you believe me. This is the most solemn act that I can offer to any god. I never recall my word, or deceive, or fail to do what I say, when I have nodded…
lines.gloss: νῦν 'now'; δέ (postpositive particle) 'but, and'; ἅμα 'at once, together'; τε (enclitic particle) 'and'; ὠκύμορος (nom. sg. adj.) 'short-lived, swift-fated'; καί 'and'; ὀϊζυρός (nom. sg. adj.) 'wretched, miserable'; περὶ πάντων (gen. pl.) 'beyond all others, more than all'.

lines.original: ἔπλεο· τώ σε κακῇ αἴσῃ τέκον ἐν μεγάροισι.
lines.english: See, I nod my head that you believe me. This is the most solemn act that I can offer to any god. I never recall my word, or deceive, or fail to do what I say, when I have nodded…
lines.gloss: ἔπλεο (2nd sg. aor. mid. of πέλομαι) 'you have become/are'; τώ (demonstrative adv.) 'therefore, for this reason'; κακῇ αἴσῃ (dat. sg. of κακὴ αἶσα) 'to an evil fate/doom'; τέκον (1st sg. aor. of τίκτω) 'I bore, gave birth to'; ἐν μεγάροισι (dat. pl.) 'in the halls/palace'.

lines.original: τοῦτο δέ τοι ἐρέουσα ἔπος Διὶ τερπικεραύνῳ
lines.english: See, I nod my head that you believe me. This is the most solemn act that I can offer to any god. I never recall my word, or deceive, or fail to do what I say, when I have nodded…
lines.gloss: τοῦτο (acc. sg. neut. of οὗτος) 'this'; δέ 'and, but'; τοι (ethical dative of σύ) 'I tell you'; ἐρέουσα (fut. participle fem. of ἐρέω/εἴρω) 'going to speak, saying'; ἔπος (acc. sg.) 'word, request'; Διὶ (dat. sg. of Ζεύς) 'to Zeus'; τερπικεραύνῳ (dat. sg. adj.) 'delighting in thunder' or 'who delights in the thunderbolt'.

lines.original: εἶμʼ αὐτὴ πρὸς Ὄλυμπον ἀγάννιφον αἴ κε πίθηται.
lines.english: on his immortal head, till vastreeled. When the pair had thus laid their plans, they parted - Zeus to his mansion, while the goddess left the splendor of, and plunged into the…
lines.gloss: εἶμ' (= εἶμι, fut. of εἰμί) 'I shall go'; αὐτή (nom. sg. fem., intensive) 'myself, in person'; Ὄλυμπον (acc. sg.) 'Olympus'; ἀγάννιφον (acc. sg. adj.) 'snow-capped, snowy'; αἴ κε (= ἐάν, conditional particle + κε) 'if'; πίθηται (3rd sg. aor. subjunctive of πείθομαι) 'he might be persuaded, obey.'

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σὺ μὲν νῦν νηυσὶ παρήμενος ὠκυπόροισι
lines.english: on his immortal head, till vastreeled. When the pair had thus laid their plans, they parted - Zeus to his mansion, while the goddess left the splendor of, and plunged into the…
lines.gloss: ἀλλά 'but' (transitional); σὺ μέν 'you (indeed)' (emphatic pronoun + particle); νῦν 'now'; νηυσί (dat. pl. of ναῦς) 'by/beside the ships'; παρήμενος (pres. middle participle) 'sitting beside, staying near'; ὠκυπόροισι (dat. pl. adj.) 'swift-faring, sea-swift' (modifying ships).

lines.original: μήνιʼ Ἀχαιοῖσιν, πολέμου δʼ ἀποπαύεο πάμπαν·
lines.english: on his immortal head, till vastreeled. When the pair had thus laid their plans, they parted - Zeus to his mansion, while the goddess left the splendor of, and plunged into the…
lines.gloss: μήνιε (pres. imperative of μηνίω) 'be wrathful, nurse your wrath'; Ἀχαιοῖσιν (dat. pl.) 'against the Achaeans'; πολέμου (gen. sg.) 'from war'; ἀποπαύεο (pres. mid. imperative of ἀποπαύω) 'cease, refrain'; πάμπαν (adv.) 'utterly, entirely.'

lines.original: Ζεὺς γὰρ ἐς Ὠκεανὸν μετʼ ἀμύμονας Αἰθιοπῆας
lines.english: on his immortal head, till vastreeled. When the pair had thus laid their plans, they parted - Zeus to his mansion, while the goddess left the splendor of, and plunged into the…
lines.gloss: Ζεύς (nom. sg.) 'Zeus'; ἐς = εἰς 'to, into'; Ὠκεανόν (acc. sg.) 'Ocean' (the great river encircling the earth); μετά (+ acc.) 'among, to'; ἀμύμονας (acc. pl. of ἀμύμων) 'blameless, noble'; Αἰθιοπῆας (acc. pl.) 'Ethiopians' (a distant people often visited by the gods).

lines.original: χθιζὸς ἔβη κατὰ δαῖτα, θεοὶ δʼ ἅμα πάντες ἕποντο·
lines.english: on his immortal head, till vastreeled. When the pair had thus laid their plans, they parted - Zeus to his mansion, while the goddess left the splendor of, and plunged into the…
lines.gloss: χθιζὸς (adv.) 'yesterday'; ἔβη (3rd sg. aor. of βαίνω) 'went, departed'; κατὰ δαῖτα 'for a feast' (δαῖτα acc. sg. of δαίς); ἅμα (adv.) 'together, along with'; πάντες (nom. pl. masc. of πᾶς) 'all'; ἕποντο (3rd pl. impf. mid. of ἕπομαι) 'followed, accompanied'.

lines.original: δωδεκάτῃ δέ τοι αὖτις ἐλεύσεται Οὔλυμπον δέ,
lines.english: to remain sitting, but all stood up as he came among them. There, then, he took his seat. But Hera, when she saw him, knew that he and silver-footed Thetis, the daughter of the…
lines.gloss: δωδεκάτῃ (dat. sg. of δωδέκατος) 'on the twelfth (day)'; αὖτις (adv.) 'back again, in return'; ἐλεύσεται (fut. 3rd sg. of ἔρχομαι) 'he/she will come'; Οὔλυμπον δέ 'and to Olympus' (acc. sg. of place to which).

lines.original: καὶ τότʼ ἔπειτά τοι εἶμι Διὸς ποτὶ χαλκοβατὲς δῶ,
lines.english: to remain sitting, but all stood up as he came among them. There, then, he took his seat. But Hera, when she saw him, knew that he and silver-footed Thetis, the daughter of the…
lines.gloss: τότε (adv.) 'then, at that time'; ἔπειτα (adv.) 'thereafter, next'; εἶμι (fut. of εἶμι) 'I shall go'; ποτί (prep. + acc.) 'to, toward'; χαλκοβατές (adj. nom./acc. sg.) 'bronze-floored, with bronze threshold'; δῶ (acc. sg. of δῶμα) 'house, dwelling.'

lines.original: καί μιν γουνάσομαι καί μιν πείσεσθαι ὀΐω.
lines.english: to remain sitting, but all stood up as he came among them. There, then, he took his seat. But Hera, when she saw him, knew that he and silver-footed Thetis, the daughter of the…
lines.gloss: μιν (acc. sg. of third-person pronoun) 'him' (referring to Zeus); γουνάσομαι (fut. mid. of γουνάομαι) 'I will clasp the knees of, supplicate'; πείσεσθαι (fut. mid. inf. of πείθω) 'to be persuaded, to obey'; ὀΐω (pres. of οἴομαι) 'I think, I expect'.

lines.original: ὦ Χρύση, πρό μʼ ἔπεμψεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: to remain sitting, but all stood up as he came among them. There, then, he took his seat. But Hera, when she saw him, knew that he and silver-footed Thetis, the daughter of the…
lines.gloss: ὦ Χρύση (voc. sg.) 'O Chryses'; πρό (adverb) 'forth, forward'; μʼ = με (acc. sg. pronoun) 'me'; ἔπεμψεν (aor. indic. 3rd sg. of πέμπω) 'sent'; ἄναξ (nom. sg.) 'lord, king'; ἀνδρῶν (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ) 'of men'; Ἀγαμέμνων (nom. sg.) proper name.

lines.original: παῖδά τε σοὶ ἀγέμεν, Φοίβῳ θʼ ἱερὴν ἑκατόμβην
lines.english: to remain sitting, but all stood up as he came among them. There, then, he took his seat. But Hera, when she saw him, knew that he and silver-footed Thetis, the daughter of the…
lines.gloss: παῖδά (acc. sg. of παῖς) 'daughter, child'; σοί (dat. sg. of σύ) 'to you'; ἀγέμεν (aor. infinitive of ἄγω) 'to bring, lead back'; Φοίβῳ (dat. sg.) 'to Phoebus (Apollo)'; ἱερήν (acc. sg. fem. of ἱερός) 'sacred, holy'; ἑκατόμβην (acc. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) 'hecatomb, great sacrifice (originally 100 oxen)'.

lines.original: ῥέξαι ὑπὲρ Δαναῶν ὄφρʼ ἱλασόμεσθα ἄνακτα,
lines.english: "Trickster," she cried, "which of the gods have you been taking into your counsels now? You are always settling matters in secret behind my back, and have never yet told me, if…
lines.gloss: ῥέξαι (aor. inf. of ῥέζω) 'to sacrifice, perform sacred rites'; ὑπὲρ with gen. 'on behalf of'; Δαναῶν (gen. pl. of Δαναοί) 'the Danaans, Greeks'; ὄφρα (conj.) 'so that, in order that'; ἱλασόμεσθα (fut. mid. 1st pl. of ἱλάσκομαι) 'we may propitiate, appease'; ἄνακτα (acc. sg. of ἄναξ) 'lord' (here Apollo).

lines.original: ὃς νῦν Ἀργείοισι πολύστονα κήδεʼ ἐφῆκεν.
lines.english: "Trickster," she cried, "which of the gods have you been taking into your counsels now? You are always settling matters in secret behind my back, and have never yet told me, if…
lines.gloss: ὃς (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) 'who'; νῦν (adv.) 'now'; Ἀργείοισι (dat. pl. of Ἀργεῖος) 'upon/for the Argives'; πολύστονα (acc. pl. neut. of πολύστονος) 'causing many groans, much-lamented'; κήδεʼ (acc. pl. of κῆδος, elided) 'griefs, troubles, woes'; ἐφῆκεν (3rd sg. aor. of ἐφίημι) 'has sent upon, inflicted'.

lines.original: κλῦθί μευ ἀργυρότοξʼ, ὃς Χρύσην ἀμφιβέβηκας
lines.english: "Trickster," she cried, "which of the gods have you been taking into your counsels now? You are always settling matters in secret behind my back, and have never yet told me, if…
lines.gloss: κλῦθί (aor. imperative) 'hear!'; μευ (enclitic gen. of ἐγώ) 'of me, my'; ἀργυρότοξε (voc. sg.) 'silver-bowed one'; ὃς (rel. pron.) 'who'; Χρύσην (acc. sg.) proper name, town in the Troad; ἀμφιβέβηκας (pf. 2nd sg. of ἀμφιβαίνω) 'you stand over, protect'.

lines.original: Κίλλαν τε ζαθέην Τενέδοιό τε ἶφι ἀνάσσεις·
lines.english: "Trickster," she cried, "which of the gods have you been taking into your counsels now? You are always settling matters in secret behind my back, and have never yet told me, if…
lines.gloss: Κίλλαν (acc. sg. of Κίλλα) 'Cilla,' a town in the Troad; ζαθέην (acc. sg. fem. of ζαθέος) 'holy, sacred'; Τενέδοιο (gen. sg. of Τένεδος) 'of Tenedos,' an island near Troy; ἶφι (adv.) 'mightily, with strength'; ἀνάσσεις (2nd sg. pres. of ἀνάσσω) 'you rule over, you are lord of.'

lines.original: ἦ μὲν δή ποτʼ ἐμεῦ πάρος ἔκλυες εὐξαμένοιο,
lines.english: "Trickster," she cried, "which of the gods have you been taking into your counsels now? You are always settling matters in secret behind my back, and have never yet told me, if…
lines.gloss: ἦ μέν 'truly, indeed' (asseverative particles); δή 'now, surely' (intensive); ποτέ 'once, before' (enclitic adverb); ἐμεῦ (gen. sg. of ἐγώ) 'of me'; πάρος 'formerly, earlier' (adverb); ἔκλυες (2nd sg. aor. of κλύω) 'you heard, listened to'; εὐξαμένοιο (gen. sg. aor. mid. participle of εὔχομαι) 'praying, making a vow.'

lines.original: τίμησας μὲν ἐμέ, μέγα δʼ ἴψαο λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν·
lines.english: "Hera," replied the sire of gods and men, "you must not expect to be informed of all my counsels. You are my wife, but you would find it hard to understand them. When it is proper…
lines.gloss: τίμησας (2nd sg. aor. of τιμάω) 'you honored'; μέν... δέ 'on the one hand... on the other hand' (correlatives); ἐμέ (acc. sg. of ἐγώ) 'me'; ἴψαο (2nd sg. aor. mid. of ἰάπτω) 'you struck down, smote'; λαόν (acc. sg. of λαός) 'the people, host'; Ἀχαιῶν (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί) 'of the Achaeans'.

lines.original: ἠδʼ ἔτι καὶ νῦν μοι τόδʼ ἐπικρήηνον ἐέλδωρ·
lines.english: "Hera," replied the sire of gods and men, "you must not expect to be informed of all my counsels. You are my wife, but you would find it hard to understand them. When it is proper…
lines.gloss: ἠδέ (conj.) 'and'; ἔτι (adv.) 'still, yet'; καὶ νῦν 'even now'; μοι (dat. sg. of ἐγώ) 'for me'; τόδε (acc. sg. of ὅδε) 'this'; ἐπικρήηνον (aor. imperative of ἐπικραίνω) 'fulfill, accomplish'; ἐέλδωρ (acc. sg. of ἔλδωρ) 'wish, desire.'

lines.original: ἤδη νῦν Δαναοῖσιν ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἄμυνον.
lines.english: "Hera," replied the sire of gods and men, "you must not expect to be informed of all my counsels. You are my wife, but you would find it hard to understand them. When it is proper…
lines.gloss: ἤδη νῦν (adverbial) 'now at once, right now'; Δαναοῖσιν (dat. pl. of Δαναοί) 'from the Danaans/Greeks'; ἀεικέα (acc. sg. masc. of ἀεικής) 'shameful, unseemly'; λοιγόν (acc. sg. of λοιγός) 'ruin, destruction'; ἄμυνον (aor. imperative of ἀμύνω) 'ward off, defend against.'

lines.original: Ζεῦ πάτερ εἴ ποτε δή σε μετʼ ἀθανάτοισιν ὄνησα
lines.english: "Hera," replied the sire of gods and men, "you must not expect to be informed of all my counsels. You are my wife, but you would find it hard to understand them. When it is proper…
lines.gloss: Ζεῦ (voc. sg.) 'Zeus'; πάτερ (voc. sg.) 'father'; εἴ ποτε δή 'if ever indeed'; σε (acc. sg. pronoun) 'you'; μετʼ ἀθανάτοισιν (= μετὰ ἀθανάτοισι, dat. pl.) 'among the immortals'; ὄνησα (1st sg. aor. indic. of ὀνίνημι) 'I benefited, aided'.

lines.original: ἢ ἔπει ἢ ἔργῳ, τόδε μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ·
lines.english: "Hera," replied the sire of gods and men, "you must not expect to be informed of all my counsels. You are my wife, but you would find it hard to understand them. When it is proper…
lines.gloss: ἢ ἔπει ἢ ἔργῳ: "either by word or by deed" (dat. sg. of ἔπος and ἔργον, instrumental); τόδε (acc. sg. neut. of ὅδε) "this"; κρήηνον (aor. imperative of κραίνω) "fulfill, accomplish"; ἐέλδωρ (acc. sg. of ἔλδωρ) "wish, prayer."

lines.original: τίμησόν μοι υἱὸν ὃς ὠκυμορώτατος ἄλλων
lines.english: you must not pry nor ask questions." "Dread son of Kronos," answered Hera, "what are you talking about? I? Pry and ask questions? Never. I let you have your own way in everything.
lines.gloss: τίμησόν (aor. imperative of τιμάω) 'honor!'; υἱόν (acc. sg.) 'son'; ὅς (relative pronoun, nom. sg.) 'who'; ὠκυμορώτατος (superlative adj., nom. sg.) 'most short-lived, swiftest to die'; ἄλλων (gen. pl. of ἄλλος) 'of others, than others'.

lines.original: ἔπλετʼ· ἀτάρ μιν νῦν γε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σύ πέρ μιν τῖσον Ὀλύμπιε μητίετα Ζεῦ·

'you' (emphatic); πέρ (enclitic particle) adds emphasis 'at least, indeed'; μιν (acc. sg. pronoun) 'him' (= Achilles); τῖσον (aor. imperative of τίνω) 'honor, avenge!'; Ὀλύμπιε (voc. sg.) 'Olympian'; μητίετα (voc. sg. of μητίετης) 'counselor, deviser'; Ζεῦ (voc. sg.) 'Zeus'.

lines.original: τόφρα δʼ ἐπὶ Τρώεσσι τίθει κράτος ὄφρʼ ἂν Ἀχαιοὶ

lines.original: υἱὸν ἐμὸν τίσωσιν ὀφέλλωσίν τέ ἑ τιμῇ.
lines.english: Still, I have a strong misgiving that Thetis, daughter of the Old One of the Sea, has been talking you over, for she was with you and had hold of your knees this self-same…

lines.original: νημερτὲς μὲν δή μοι ὑπόσχεο καὶ κατάνευσον

lines.original: ἢ ἀπόειπʼ, ἐπεὶ οὔ τοι ἔπι δέος, ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδέω

lines.original: ὅσσον ἐγὼ μετὰ πᾶσιν ἀτιμοτάτη θεός εἰμι.
lines.english: Still, I have a strong misgiving that Thetis, daughter of the Old One of the Sea, has been talking you over, for she was with you and had hold of your knees this self-same…

lines.original: ἦ δὴ λοίγια ἔργʼ ὅ τέ μʼ ἐχθοδοπῆσαι ἐφήσεις

lines.original: Ἥρῃ ὅτʼ ἄν μʼ ἐρέθῃσιν ὀνειδείοις ἐπέεσσιν·
lines.english: "Wife," said Zeus, "I can do nothing but you suspect me and find it out. You will take nothing by it, for I shall only dislike you the more, and it will go harder with you.…

lines.original: ἣ δὲ καὶ αὔτως μʼ αἰεὶ ἐν ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι
lines.english: "Wife," said Zeus, "I can do nothing but you suspect me and find it out. You will take nothing by it, for I shall only dislike you the more, and it will go harder with you.…

lines.original: νεικεῖ, καί τέ μέ φησι μάχῃ Τρώεσσιν ἀρήγειν.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ σὺ μὲν νῦν αὖτις ἀπόστιχε μή τι νοήσῃ
